• Root / embed: canonicalType = resolve(type); effectiveName = name ?? lastSegment(canonicalType);
  if name present → name == lastSegment(canonicalType)
• Sub-Block: effectiveName = name (element tag or child <name>);
  expectedType = canonicalParentType + "." + name;
  canonicalType = type ? resolve(type) : expectedType; canonicalType == expectedType

See also doc:SubBlockModel (visibility, embeds, reference scope) and doc:BlockNameConvention.
289.idea: A guide to type references and Block identity

290.name: TypeSystemOverview
290.documentation:
BlockML knows four ValueType kinds at language level — each names a semantic meaning.
They are sibling branches under ValueType (not subtypes of each other):

PrimitiveType — atomic scalar semantics; no stored values on the type itself.
Examples: Boolean, Integer, Decimal, Float, Text, Color (Text subtype), URL, UUID, Version,
TypeSelector / TypeIdentifier / TypeReference, PackageSelector / PackageIdentifier / PackageReference, InstanceIdentifier /
InstanceReference, MemberIdentifier / PropertyIdentifier / …, Date, Time, DateTime, Duration.
PrimitiveType declares parseValue (Text → bml:Self). The TypeScript return is a host encoding;
outputType is always bml:Self (doc:ValueTypeParsing).

StructType — custom value objects; structure via properties.
Examples: EmptyStruct (no fields; only {}), Size3D, Address, Transform. Parameterized
types (Box(T)) are StructTypes with genericTypes — not a separate branch.

EnumType — closed set of named members; own ValueType branch (not a StructType). Allowed
members live in the values aggregation; BOM stores id + typeFqn only.
Examples: Direction, Face, StudType.

ConstantType — singleton value domain; one configured literal.
Example: Constant(Text){value: "auto"} for union alternatives.

Type expressions combine named types — they are not new BlockML type classes:
• Multiplicity: Integer[], Integer[3], Text[0..n] — postfix on a TypeExpression, so it nests via
  explicit grouping: (Integer[])[] (never Integer[][])
• Unions: Boolean | Integer, Constant(Text){value: "auto"} | Float
• Generic application: Box(Integer) · InstanceReference(core:Block) — round parentheses in type
  attributes; open generic instances bind the same (…) list via bml:generics (doc:GenericsModel)
• Instance configuration: Text{maxLength: 100}, Decimal{precision: 10, scale: 2}
• bml:Self — resolves to effective current Block type after inheritance
• T — generic parameter reference from declaring Block's genericTypes

Assignability follows the branch hierarchy — a value of a subtype is accepted wherever a
supertype is required, with ValueType as the top of the value hierarchy:
Integer <: Number <: PrimitiveType <: ValueType. Date <: Temporal <:
PrimitiveType. Duration is a sibling of Temporal under PrimitiveType — not a Temporal subtype.
A type reference with multiplicity is compatible per element type: Integer[] <: Number[]
<: ValueType[], and each element of a collection is validated independently, so ValueType[]
also accepts mixed element types (doc:TypeExpressions — Collection compatibility · Heterogeneous
collections).

Only ValueTypes may appear where a bare type name is required (Property type,
Capability inputType/outputType). Aggregation type may be any Block FQN. Association type
must be InstanceReference(T) or InstanceReference(T)[] — bare Block FQNs are invalid.
ValueTypes never store data — Properties own all concrete values.

Identifier vs Reference — parseValue on Identifier types checks syntax only. Existence is a
later validator step on Reference types (doc:ValueTypeParsing). The validator keys off the
declared ValueType of the field, never the property or attribute name (type= vs abc= is
irrelevant):
• TypeReference, PropertyReference / AggregationReference / …, and
  InstanceReference — the target must resolve in the current corpus. Unknown TypeReference
  → BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE; unknown PropertyReference → BML_UNKNOWN_PROPERTY (or BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE
  if the owning type cannot be resolved); unknown InstanceReference →
  BML_UNRESOLVABLE_INSTANCE_REF. Unresolved is an error, not proof the document is
  ill-formed — like Java class-not-found, it may be a typo or a missing library.
• TypeIdentifier, MemberIdentifier (PropertyIdentifier / …), and InstanceIdentifier —
  syntax only. Ill-formed → BML_INVALID_TYPE_REFERENCE. An unknown but well-formed name is
  valid.
290.idea: A guide to the type system

291.name: ValueTypeConfiguration
291.documentation:
Curly braces configure the Property's owned ValueType instance — orthogonal to generic (...)
binding. The configuration applies to the type instance associated with a Property, not to
the ValueType definition block itself. Both may coexist: Box(Integer){minItems: 1}.
Multiplicity brackets apply after configuration: Text{maxLength: 50}[0..n].

Syntax examples:
• Text{maxLength: 100} — named configuration property (JSON-like key: value)
• Decimal{precision: 10, scale: 2} — named precision and scale
• Decimal{10, 2} — positional by ValueType property declaration order (precision, scale)
• Constant(SizeXY){value: {x: 1, y: 2}} — nested object literals for StructType config values

Rules:
• Named and positional configuration must not be mixed in one {...} block →
  BML_MIXED_TYPE_CONFIGURATION
• Positional mapping follows declaration order — same principle as FunctionMapping
• Do not use key=value inside {...} (that is expression call syntax, not type configuration)
• Unknown config property → BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE_CONFIGURATION; value mismatch →
  BML_TYPE_CONFIGURATION_VIOLATION
• Generic application uses round parentheses: Box(Integer), TypeReference(core:Block)
• Constant(T){value: …} — generic (...) binds T; {value: …} supplies the singleton literal

Prefer multiplicity on the type reference for collection bounds (Text[1..10]) over List{…}
wrappers. Prefer inline configuration for type-intrinsic thresholds (Text{maxLength: 100});
keep Constraints for contextual/composable/business rules (Pattern, cross-property, …).

Configuration runs after PrimitiveType.parseValue accepts the authored text
(doc:ValueTypeParsing). parseValue does not read min / max / maxLength — those stay on the
Property's owned type instance.

ValueType definitions declare configuration Properties on the type block (e.g. precision and
scale on Decimal). Values live on Properties of Block instances — never on the ValueType
definition. There is no new Integer(5) in BlockML; the Property owns value 5 with type Integer.

Decimal is the default for non-integer numerics (3.5, 12.75). Float is special-purpose only
when binary floating-point semantics are explicitly required.

292.name: ValueTypeParsing
292.documentation:
PrimitiveType declares parseValue — a Transformation from authored Text to bml:Self that
throws exception:InvalidValueException. Concrete primitives implement a deterministic
TypeScript body (host-evaluable reading of doc:CapabilitySemantics). The BML outputType is
always bml:Self — the TypeScript return (number, string, boolean) is FunctionMapping / host
encoding, not the Capability signature.

parseValue is lexical only:
• Input is XML attribute or element text, already tokenized by the parser as Text
• Success means the text is a value of this PrimitiveType
• Failure throws InvalidValueException; a validating host reports diag:BML_INVALID_VALUE
• The body sees the type definition, not the Property's configured type instance — no
  this.min / this.max

After a successful parse, in this order:
1. Type instance configuration — Integer{min: 0, max: 100}, Text{maxLength: 50}
   (doc:ValueTypeConfiguration)
2. Property constraints — Pattern, Min, Max, … (doc:ConstraintsModel)
3. Existence checks on Reference types — TypeReference, InstanceReference, PropertyReference /
   … (doc:TypeSystemOverview). parseValue does not consult the TypeRegistry.

Inheritance: Text implements identity (every string is Text). Number implements a numeric
literal; Integer, Decimal, and Float refine. Temporal leaves parseValue abstract; Date, Time,
and DateTime implement ISO forms. Identifier types implement syntax; Reference subtypes inherit
that syntax and add existence in the validator. PackageSelector / TypeSelector accept wildcard
patterns of which Identifier is the concrete form. URI requires an RFC 3986 scheme; URL is an
absolute http/https web address; FilePath is a non-empty path without NUL or line breaks
(existence on disk is not part of parseValue).

parseValue does not cover multiplicity or unions (TypeExpression on the reference, element-wise),
StructType field walks, EnumType membership, or Constant(T){value} equality. Those stay
validator-side.

Bootstrap: the compiler still tokenizes framework BML as text. parseValue runs on loaded
property values after TypeRegistry bootstrap. Hard-coded bootstrap parsers for Text, Integer,
Boolean, and TypeIdentifier remain until a host evaluates these bodies.

293.name: WOTFoundation
293.documentation:
The Web of Things (WOT) provides the philosophical foundation for BlockML. Optional reading
for context — not required to use the compiler or author BML.

Idea (Plato):
The only true constant. Exists independently of Universes, Worlds, Technologies, and
Manifestations. An Idea does not change. In BlockML: Block, ValueType, Language, FQN —
describable without any render target. BML holds the Idea stable. The Block definition
itself is the Idea; the authoring field <is> (BOM block.is, reflection bml:Self.is)
names that Idea in an ultra-short noun phrase for humans and LLMs — it is not the Idea.

Manifestation:
The entire process from Idea to Thing — not a single step. Manifestor (compiler) produces
preconditions; Runtime completes Manifestation in a World the Manifestor cannot fully know.
In BlockML: renderer working model, target output, runtime behaviour. The renderer decides
interpretation — SCAD mb_block(), React components, KiCad symbols are different Manifestations
of the same Ideas.

Grammar (BlockML / BOM):
How Things are structured. Blocks are the grammar of a World. Types, Languages, Services,
and Capabilities are part of that grammar — not implementation detail. stud:// is how Things
communicate; BOM Core is how Things are structured.

World:
Delivers interpretation. An Idea carries no properties of its own — no substance, material,
or weight. The World assigns meaning. MachineBlocks is one World (physical geometry → SCAD);
other Worlds (ScreenMachine → React, EBOM → electronics) share type FQNs with different
render mappings.

WOT alignment at language layer: ontological unity in BML; engineering freedom in compiler
internals and renderer output. Without adoption, there is no WOT — and without internal
freedom, there is no maintainable compiler.
293.idea: A guide to the WOT foundation

294.name: InvalidValueException
294.documentation:
Thrown by PrimitiveType.parseValue when authored text is not a lexical value of this
ValueType. Inherits message:Text from core:Exception — the instance carries the reason;
the type is listed on the Capability throws clause.

A host that evaluates parseValue maps this Exception to diag:BML_INVALID_VALUE. Existence
failures (unknown TypeReference, missing instance) stay validator Diagnostics — they are
not this Exception. Type instance configuration and Property constraints run after a
successful parse (doc:ValueTypeParsing).

295.name: BlockGroup
295.documentation:
Abstract Group branch for block groups — named categories that organize Blocks
for editors and tooling. Intentionally empty — no properties, aggregations, or Sub-Blocks.
Concrete group kinds extend this branch. BlockDefinition.groups overrides
StructuralDefinition.groups to TypeReferenceEntity(group:BlockGroup)[].

296.name: MemberGroup
296.documentation:
Abstract Group branch for member groups — named categories that organize Block
members (properties, aggregations, associations, capabilities) for editors and tooling.
A member may reference several groups via MemberDefinition.groups (e.g. UI category and usage
facet). Intentionally empty — no properties, aggregations, or Sub-Blocks. Concrete group kinds
extend this branch. MemberDefinition.groups overrides StructuralDefinition.groups to
TypeReferenceEntity(group:MemberGroup)[].

297.name: BML
297.documentation:
MarkupLanguage for BlockML (BML) document implementations on Capabilities — block
definitions, library catalogs, and other structured BML markup. Forwards MarkupLanguage.L
(NaturalLanguage, default English) for the content/text language inside the BML body — bare BML
is BML(English).

298.name: C
298.documentation:
ProgrammingLanguage for C function implementations on Capabilities. Forwards
ProgrammingLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for the content language of identifiers
and comments — bare C is C(English).

299.name: Chinese
299.documentation:
Natural language for documentation prose, example titles, and Chinese
natural-language capability implementations.

300.name: CPP
300.documentation:
ProgrammingLanguage for C++ function implementations on Capabilities. Forwards
ProgrammingLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for the content language of identifiers
and comments — bare CPP is CPP(English).

301.name: CSharp
301.documentation:
ProgrammingLanguage for C# method implementations on Capabilities. Forwards
ProgrammingLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for the content language of identifiers
and comments — bare CSharp is CSharp(English).

302.name: English
302.documentation:
Natural language for documentation prose, example titles, and English
natural-language capability implementations.

303.name: French
303.documentation:
Natural language for documentation prose, example titles, and French
natural-language capability implementations.

304.name: German
304.documentation:
Natural language for documentation prose, example titles, and German
natural-language capability implementations.

305.name: Japanese
305.documentation:
Natural language for documentation prose, example titles, and Japanese
natural-language capability implementations.

306.name: Java
306.documentation:
ProgrammingLanguage for Java method implementations on Capabilities. Forwards
ProgrammingLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for the content language of identifiers
and comments — bare Java is Java(English).

307.name: JavaScript
307.documentation:
ProgrammingLanguage for JavaScript function implementations on Capabilities. Forwards
ProgrammingLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for the content language of identifiers
and comments — bare JavaScript is JavaScript(English).

308.name: JSON
308.documentation:
MarkupLanguage for JSON document implementations on Capabilities — configuration,
structured data, or templates. Forwards MarkupLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for
the content/text language inside the document — bare JSON is JSON(English).

309.name: Markdown
309.documentation:
MarkupLanguage for Markdown prose — documentation bodies and Markdown document
implementations on Capabilities — with lightweight structure (headings, lists, links, code
fences).

Generic parameter L (NaturalLanguage, default English) is forwarded from MarkupLanguage and names
the content language of the Markdown body: Markdown = Markdown(English), Markdown(German) for
German prose. Because L is forwarded rather than bound, Markdown(NaturalLanguage) is a usable
type bound — def:StructuralDefinition.Documentation.language binds
Markdown(NaturalLanguage) | NaturalLanguage, where the bare-language alternative is shorthand for
Markdown in that language.

Also the default content language of documentation prose: Markdown(English) is the default value
of language on def:StructuralDefinition.Documentation, so every <documentation> body is
Markdown unless it declares otherwise. summary is plain text and never Markdown. CDATA is an XML
serialization detail — Markdown itself never requires it. See doc:DocumentationModel —
Documentation, Summary, Markdown and CDATA.

310.name: MarkupLanguage
310.documentation:
Abstract branch for markup languages — XML and other structured document formats
used as capability implementation bodies and, for Markdown, as documentation prose. Generic
parameter L (NaturalLanguage, default English) names the content/text language inside the markup
(element text, comments, human-facing labels, prose).

Concrete sub-types forward L via baseType MarkupLanguage(L) and redeclare it locally, so the
parameter stays open on the sub-type — Markdown(German) is authorable and Markdown(NaturalLanguage)
is usable as a type bound. Because L defaults to English, a bare sub-type name needs no argument:
Markdown ≡ Markdown(English). Binding L in baseType instead (MarkupLanguage(lang:German)) fixes
the content language for that sub-type and closes the parameter.

311.name: NaturalLanguage
311.documentation:
Abstract branch for natural languages used in documentation text, example
titles, and natural-language capability implementations. All locale-specific language blocks
(English, German, French, Spanish, Chinese, Japanese, Russian, …) must extend this branch —
not org.blockml.bml.core.Language directly. Distinct from implementation languages
(ProgrammingLanguage, MarkupLanguage) used in capability bodies and example content. Those
formal branches reuse NaturalLanguage as optional generic L (default English) when their
content/text language must be named.

312.name: OpenSCAD
312.documentation:
ProgrammingLanguage for OpenSCAD function implementations on Capabilities.
Emitted by the MachineBlocks SCAD renderer with FQN-prefixed function names. Forwards
ProgrammingLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for the content language of identifiers
and comments — bare OpenSCAD is OpenSCAD(English).

313.name: ProgrammingLanguage
313.documentation:
Abstract branch for programming languages — TypeScript, OpenSCAD, PseudoCode, and
other languages with defined or interpretable syntax. Generic parameter L (NaturalLanguage,
default English) names the content/text language of the formal code — for example pseudocode
prose, identifiers, or LLM-oriented wording.

Concrete sub-types forward L via baseType ProgrammingLanguage(L) and redeclare it locally, so the
parameter stays open on the sub-type — PseudoCode(German) is authorable and
PseudoCode(NaturalLanguage) is usable as a type bound. Because L defaults to English, a bare
sub-type name needs no argument: TypeScript ≡ TypeScript(English). Binding L in baseType instead
(ProgrammingLanguage(lang:German)) fixes the content language for that sub-type and closes the
parameter.

314.name: PseudoCode
314.documentation:
ProgrammingLanguage for free-form pseudocode implementations. The code must be
internally consistent but is otherwise unconstrained — an LLM may interpret it. Forwards
ProgrammingLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) — declare a content language only when
the pseudocode prose is not English, directly on this language (PseudoCode(German)); bare
PseudoCode is PseudoCode(English).

315.name: Python
315.documentation:
ProgrammingLanguage for Python function implementations on Capabilities. Forwards
ProgrammingLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for the content language of identifiers
and comments — bare Python is Python(English).

316.name: Russian
316.documentation:
Natural language for documentation prose, example titles, and Russian
natural-language capability implementations.

317.name: Spanish
317.documentation:
Natural language for documentation prose, example titles, and Spanish
natural-language capability implementations.

318.name: TypeScript
318.documentation:
ProgrammingLanguage for TypeScript arrow-function implementations on Capabilities.
V1: compile-time execution when all arguments are literals. Forwards ProgrammingLanguage.L
(NaturalLanguage, default English) for the content language of identifiers and comments — bare
TypeScript is TypeScript(English).

319.name: Unity
319.documentation:
C# dialect for Unity script implementations on Capabilities — MonoBehaviour methods,
UnityEngine APIs, and game-logic code. Forwards L on through CSharp (NaturalLanguage, default
English) for the content language of identifiers and comments — bare Unity is
Unity(English).

320.name: XML
320.documentation:
MarkupLanguage for XML document implementations on Capabilities — templates,
configuration, or structured markup. Forwards MarkupLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English)
for the content/text language inside the markup — bare XML is XML(English).

321.name: YML
321.documentation:
MarkupLanguage for YAML document implementations on Capabilities — configuration,
structured data, or templates. Forwards MarkupLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for
the content/text language inside the document — bare YML is YML(English).

322.name: Library
322.documentation:
Publishable BlockML core library (org.blockml.bml.Library). Exports the framework grammar:
core branches (Block, Annotation, ValueType, Language, Status, Relation, Constraint, Validation, Capability, Exception, Definition, Group),
group branch (org.blockml.bml.group.MemberGroup, org.blockml.bml.group.BlockGroup),
concrete value types and constraints, implementation languages, built-in services, lifecycle
status blocks, the Definition meta-model branch (org.blockml.bml.definition.*), the language
annotation (org.blockml.bml.annotation.BmlAnnotation), bootstrap
documentation blocks (org.blockml.bml.documentation.*), how-to blocks (org.blockml.bml.documentation.howto.*),
diagnostic blocks (org.blockml.bml.diagnostic.*), and definition metadata
(org.blockml.bml.meta.Keyword, org.blockml.bml.meta.Alias, org.blockml.bml.meta.FixedKeyword,
org.blockml.bml.meta.FixedAlias). Keyword and Alias are PrimitiveEntity(Text) — ad-hoc
instances and comma-separated value sugar. Fixed* freeze value and companion members as
readOnly; domain libraries extend them for catalogue-controlled tags and alternative names.

Root Blocks in org.blockml.bml.core must inherit directly from core:Block; nested Sub-Blocks
in that package are exempt (doc:ModelingGuidelines).

Membership is defined exclusively by this file's blocks list — not by directory layout.
Version 3.0.0 applies to all exported blocks (framework convention: version only on
Library.bml).

323.name: FunctionMapping
323.documentation:
Concrete Mapping for function-like call syntax. Describes translation between a
function-parameter list and a Capability inputType or outputType.

Two application sites (opposite directions):
1. Expression calls — function syntax → FunctionMapping → Capability inputType
2. Capability implementation — Capability inputType → FunctionMapping → target-language
   function parameters (and reverse for return values)

Canonical call form passes a value matching inputType directly, using JSON-like syntax:
• Primitive → primitive literal
• StructType → object literal
• Collection → array literal

Helper syntax (when supported by this mapping):
• Named parameters — mapped by StructType property names; order irrelevant
• Positional parameters — mapped by property declaration order (mapping config only;
  does not create general StructType index semantics)

Default FunctionMapping (used when no explicit mapping is declared on an implementation):
• Primitive inputType — exactly one positional or named parameter
• StructType inputType — object literal (canonical), named parameters, or positional
  parameters by declaration order
• Primitive collection — positional parameters → array literal
• StructType collection — one outer parameter per struct instance → array literal
• Mixed positional and named arguments — not supported (BML_MIXED_FUNCTION_ARGUMENTS)

Capability implementations that require a target-language function signature must declare an
explicit FunctionMapping child when the default rules are insufficient.

Validation errors: BML_UNKNOWN_FUNCTION_PARAMETER, BML_DUPLICATE_FUNCTION_PARAMETER,
BML_MISSING_FUNCTION_PARAMETER, BML_TOO_MANY_FUNCTION_PARAMETERS,
BML_MIXED_FUNCTION_ARGUMENTS, BML_MISSING_FUNCTION_MAPPING,     BML_AMBIGUOUS_FUNCTION_MAPPING.

324.name: Alias
324.documentation:
Instantiable PrimitiveEntity(Text) for alternative Block type names in an aliases
aggregation on org.blockml.bml.definition.BlockDefinition only (root blocks and Sub-Blocks).
Not a core root branch. Ad-hoc names are Alias instances (for example
<meta:Alias value="Sub-Block" />). Comma-separated character content on <aliases> is
PrimitiveEntity value sugar and expands to Alias instances — one value per trimmed token —
not to FixedAlias catalogue blocks. Not XML namespace prefix aliases. Not search tags —
use org.blockml.bml.meta.Keyword for those.

Domain libraries define catalogue alias blocks extending org.blockml.bml.meta.FixedAlias.
Those types set value on the definition; references are empty fixed blocks (for example
<vocab:SubBlockAlias />). Type FQN is the catalogue identity; value, language, and
legacy resolve from the alias definition.

325.name: FixedAlias
325.documentation:
Abstract catalogue freeze of org.blockml.bml.meta.Alias. Domain libraries declare concrete
alias blocks extending FixedAlias and set inherited members on the type definition
(for example <value>Sub-Block</value>). References in <aliases> are empty fixed
blocks (for example <vocab:SubBlockAlias />) — type FQN is the catalogue identity; value,
language, and legacy resolve from the alias definition and are readOnly at reference sites.

Concrete children must set value on the definition (value is abstract here). They do not
redeclare the member unless the declaration itself changes. Comma-separated shorthand on
<aliases> expands to Alias instances — not to FixedAlias or its catalogue descendants.

326.name: FixedKeyword
326.documentation:
Abstract catalogue freeze of org.blockml.bml.meta.Keyword. Domain libraries declare concrete
keyword blocks extending FixedKeyword and set inherited members on the type definition
(for example <value>inheritance</value>). References in <keywords> are empty fixed
blocks (for example <vocab:Inheritance />) — type FQN is the catalogue identity; value,
language, and weight resolve from the keyword definition and are readOnly at reference sites.

Concrete children must set value on the definition (value is abstract here). They do not
redeclare the member unless the declaration itself changes. Comma-separated shorthand on
<keywords> expands to Keyword instances — not to FixedKeyword or its catalogue descendants.

327.name: Keyword
327.documentation:
Instantiable PrimitiveEntity(Text) for search and discovery tags in a keywords aggregation
on org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition. Not a core root branch. Ad-hoc tags are
Keyword instances (for example <meta:Keyword value="inheritance" />). Comma-separated
character content on <keywords> is PrimitiveEntity value sugar and expands to Keyword
instances — one value per trimmed token — not to FixedKeyword catalogue blocks.

Domain libraries define catalogue keyword blocks extending org.blockml.bml.meta.FixedKeyword
(for example org.example.keyword.Inheritance). Those types set value on the definition;
references are empty fixed blocks (for example <vocab:Inheritance />). Type FQN is the
catalogue identity; value, language, and weight resolve from the keyword definition.
Distinct from org.blockml.bml.meta.Alias (alternative Block type names on BlockDefinition).

328.name: README
328.documentation:
README block for the BlockML core library. Start with references marked relation=ReadFirst —
thirty-six documentation blocks in mental learning order. The early entries form the BlockML
conceptual core — the core use cases, the type system, and the expression language
(${ } and <$ $>).
Later entries cover conventions, authoring rules (visibility, overrides, member authoring,
composition, annotations, directives, type identity, Sub-Blocks, contracts, constraints),
organisation, and background knowledge.

Library.bml points here via the required readMe aggregation (<blockml:README />).
Tooling filters references where relation=ReadFirst to build a curated learning context bundle;
relation=HowToIndex lists accomplishable procedural how-tos for humans, agents, and CI. Automated
process SPOE uses Library.bootstrap (core:Bootstrap) — not this ReadMe.

329.name: AuthoringGuide
329.documentation:
Typical file= targets — repository markdown with authoring rules, examples, or
migration notes. Use when the link is procedural ("how to write…") rather than structural
(Extends) or optional background (SeeAlso).

330.name: ContrastsWith
330.documentation:
Use to disambiguate easily confused concepts — for example Sub-Block vs embedded Block,
contract vs baseType, Inbound vs Outbound capability. The context text body must explain the
difference explicitly.

331.name: DeepDive
331.documentation:
Use for file= or url= targets with long-form prose the reader may skip on first
pass. Distinct from Requires (mandatory) and AuthoringGuide (procedural). Typical for architecture
documents, WOT foundation, or specification deep-dives.

332.name: Defines
332.documentation:
Use when the referenced Block or Definition element is the formal specification
the current type conforms to — for example def:PropertyDefinition on a property member, or
core:Bootstrap on a README block.

333.name: Extends
333.documentation:
Use when the referenced Block is in the baseType chain or represents a branch the
current type belongs to. Typical type= targets only — not for file or url references.

334.name: HowToIndex
334.documentation:
Use on <see> entries in README / ReadMe blocks to list accomplishable how-tos.
Distinct from ReadFirst (mental learning order) and SeeAlso (optional peer link). Tooling
filters relation=HowToIndex to build a how-to menu for humans, agents, or CI. Target should
reference an org.blockml.bml.documentation.howto.* HowTo block. Not a catalog of executable
workflow Tasks.

335.name: HowToStep
335.documentation:
Use on <see> entries inside org.blockml.bml.documentation.howto.* HowTo blocks.
Document order in <references> is step order — same convention as ReadFirst on README.
Target may be a Block, repository markdown file, or external URL. Distinct from Prerequisite
(before starting the how-to) and Requires (hard dependency on the current definition).

336.name: Prerequisite
336.documentation:
Use on <see> entries at the start of a HowTo <references> container
— before HowToStep entries. Distinct from Requires (dependency of the current definition) and
ReadFirst (library-wide learning path). Prerequisite scopes to one how-to procedure.

337.name: ReadFirst
337.documentation:
Two uses:
1. Concrete Library.bml — required single ReadFirst <see> targeting the ReadMe named in
   the readMe aggregation (catalog entry point). May be followed by ThenContinueWith → Bootstrap
   when bootstrap is present; no other <see> relations on concrete Libraries.
2. README / ReadMe blocks — curated mental learning order. ReadFirst entries should appear
   first in <references>, in reading order.

Distinct from Library.readMe (aggregation that names the ReadMe block) and from ReadNext
(forward edge between documentation blocks outside the README catalog).

338.name: ReadNext
338.documentation:
Use on <see> entries in documentation blocks (org.blockml.bml.documentation.*)
to point to the next topic in a learning chain — typically body text starting with
"Next reading step". Distinct from ReadFirst (README curated entry points), Prerequisite
(task-scoped do-this-first), and SeeAlso (optional peer link). ReadNext is a single forward
edge between narrative documentation blocks, not a library-wide ordered catalog.

339.name: Requires
339.documentation:
Use for hard dependencies — types, documentation, or external resources the reader
or runtime must know first. Distinct from ReadFirst (curated path) and SeeAlso (optional peer link).

340.name: Resolves
340.documentation:
Use on <see> entries in org.blockml.bml.diagnostic.* blocks to link a
validator code to a procedural fix guide. Target should reference an org.blockml.bml.documentation.howto.*
HowTo block. Enables error-driven navigation: reported BML_* code → Diagnostic block →
Resolves → HowTo with HowToStep entries.

341.name: SeeAlso
341.documentation:
Default relation when relation is omitted on <see>. Use for related Blocks,
documentation files, or URLs that help understand the current definition but do not extend,
require, or define it. Omitted relation= on <see> resolves to this block.

342.name: ThenContinueWith
342.documentation:
TypeRelation(core:Bootstrap) — use on concrete Library <see type="…"> entries
to point at the library's Bootstrap SPOE after the human/LLM reading entry. Target must be a
type reference whose resolved type satisfies satisfiesTypeBound(…, core:Bootstrap); file/url/
instance/member targets are forbidden (TypeRelation rule).

Sequence on Library.bml: ReadFirst → ReadMe (required), then ThenContinueWith → Bootstrap when
the library declares a bootstrap aggregation. Distinct from ReadNext (narrative learning chain)
and from HowToIndex / HowToStep (how-to catalog). Signals: after reading, continue with the
automation entry.

343.name: TypeRelation
343.documentation:
Abstract Relation subtype that may be used only on <see type="…"> entries —
never on instance, file, url, property, aggregation, association, or capability targets.
Not a core root branch — lives with the other relation types in org.blockml.bml.relation.*.

Generic T is the allowed target Block branch. The resolved type of see type= must satisfy
satisfiesTypeBound(resolve(type), T) — otherwise BML_TYPE_BOUND_NOT_SATISFIED. Default
T = core:Block — any Block type reference is allowed until a concrete subtype binds T more
narrowly (e.g. ThenContinueWith binds T = core:Bootstrap).

Plain Relation (SeeAlso, AuthoringGuide, …) remains unrestricted across target kinds.
TypeRelation is for relations whose semantics require a Block type identity target.

344.name: Bools
344.documentation:
Built-in booleans service. Expression prefix #bools.* — logical and boolean
conversion utilities.

345.name: Lists
345.documentation:
Built-in lists service. Expression prefix #lists.* — list construction,
indexing, and aggregation utilities.

Inputs typed core:ValueType[] are compatible with a collection of any element type, because
collections are compared per element type and every ValueType is assignable to ValueType:
Integer[] <: Number[] <: PrimitiveType[] <: ValueType[], Text[] <: ValueType[]. Elements are
validated independently, so heterogeneous collections such as [1, "text", true] are accepted
here. Capabilities declaring a narrower element type are homogeneous by that element type —
sequence returns Integer[], where [1, "text", 3] would be invalid. Element access (first, last,
get) declares core:ValueType as output — the element type of its core:ValueType[] input; the
concrete ValueType of the returned element follows the list element at runtime.

Multi-argument capabilities use an anonymous StructType whose field types are full
TypeExpressions — { list: core:ValueType[], index: Integer } on get is one anonymous StructType
with a qualified, multiplicity-carrying list field and an unqualified index field. concat takes a
nested multiplicity instead — (core:ValueType[])[], a collection of lists, where every call
argument becomes one element of the outer collection.
See doc:TypeExpressions — Collection compatibility · Heterogeneous collections ·
Nested multiplicities · Anonymous StructTypes.

346.name: Math
346.documentation:
Built-in math service. Expression prefix #math.* — min, max, abs, floor,
round, and related numeric utilities.

347.name: Numbers
347.documentation:
Built-in numbers service. Expression prefix #numbers.* — sequence,
formatting, and numeric conversion utilities.

348.name: Strings
348.documentation:
Built-in strings service. Expression prefix #strings.* — concat, length,
substring, and related text utilities.

349.name: Deprecated

350.name: Draft
350.documentation:
Declared in BML but not yet fully implemented, validated, or mapped. May change
without deprecation notice. Use when a known gap exists between target and canonical form —
add an explicit note in <documentation> or sibling prose.

351.name: Stable
351.documentation:
Implemented, validated, and mapping complete. Behavior is reliable and may be
depended on by downstream definitions and tooling. Implicit default when no status is declared
on an element — omit <status> and bml:status on Stable content.

352.name: Stub
352.documentation:
Structural placeholder only. Documents intent or reserves a member slot without
committing to behaviour, types, or mapping. Stronger signal than Draft for incomplete ideas.
Toolchain: Stage 2 validation accepts Stub; each Render Target may emit stubs (e.g. empty
methods with logs), omit, or abort — policy is target-specific.

353.name: AggregationIdentifier
353.documentation:
Concrete MemberIdentifier binding D = AggregationDefinition. Value is a canonical
aggregation path (com.foo.Bar.aggregations.children) or a local aggregation name when paired
with a type qualifier. Syntax only — the owning type and aggregation need not exist.
AggregationReference extends this type and adds existence. Use when addressing a potential
aggregation. see aggregation= uses AggregationReference. AggregationReference(B) introduces
the owning Block bound after resolution.

354.name: AggregationIdentifierEntity
354.documentation:
Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping an AggregationIdentifier primitive. Binds T =
AggregationIdentifier on org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value
property automatically. Use when a potential aggregation path must appear as an identifiable
Block instance. Existence-checked counterparts use AggregationReferenceEntity.
354.idea: An Aggregation member path as a PrimitiveEntity

355.name: AggregationReference
355.documentation:
Existence-checked AggregationIdentifier. Value is a canonical aggregation path
(com.foo.Bar.aggregations.children) or a local aggregation name when paired with a type
qualifier. The owning type and aggregation must resolve. Used as the type of see aggregation=.
A potential aggregation that need not exist uses AggregationIdentifier.
355.idea: A path to an Aggregation member

356.name: AggregationReferenceEntity
356.documentation:
Open generic Entity wrapping an AggregationReference primitive. Forwards B from
org.blockml.bml.type.AggregationReference onto org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType —
inherits the value property automatically as value : AggregationReference(B). Use when a
resolved aggregation path must appear as an identifiable Block instance. Syntax-only paths use
AggregationIdentifierEntity.
356.idea: A path to an Aggregation member as a PrimitiveEntity

357.name: AssociationIdentifier
357.documentation:
Concrete MemberIdentifier binding D = AssociationDefinition. Value is a canonical
association path (com.foo.Bar.associations.basePresets) or a local association name when paired
with a type qualifier. Syntax only — the owning type and association need not exist.
AssociationReference extends this type and adds existence. Use when addressing a potential
association. see association= uses AssociationReference. AssociationReference(B) introduces
the owning Block bound after resolution.

358.name: AssociationIdentifierEntity
358.documentation:
Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping an AssociationIdentifier primitive. Binds T =
AssociationIdentifier on org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value
property automatically. Use when a potential association path must appear as an identifiable
Block instance. Existence-checked counterparts use AssociationReferenceEntity.
358.idea: An Association member path as a PrimitiveEntity

359.name: AssociationReference
359.documentation:
Existence-checked AssociationIdentifier. Value is a canonical association path
(com.foo.Bar.associations.basePresets) or a local association name when paired with a type
qualifier. The owning type and association must resolve. Used as the type of see association=.
A potential association that need not exist uses AssociationIdentifier.
359.idea: A path to an Association member

360.name: AssociationReferenceEntity
360.documentation:
Open generic Entity wrapping an AssociationReference primitive. Forwards B from
org.blockml.bml.type.AssociationReference onto org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType —
inherits the value property automatically as value : AssociationReference(B). Use when a
resolved association path must appear as an identifiable Block instance. Syntax-only paths use
AssociationIdentifierEntity.
360.idea: A path to an Association member as a PrimitiveEntity

361.name: Boolean
361.documentation:
BOM Core primitive ValueType for true/false values. Unqualified name Boolean
resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.Boolean. Boolean is neither textual nor numeric — its own
primitive branch. Values are stored in Properties — not on the Boolean type itself.

Authoring accepts case variants of the literals: true / True / TRUE and false / False / FALSE.
Preferred form is lowercase true and false. The BOM always stores the canonical boolean
(lowercase true or false) — never the authored casing.

Sub-Blocks True and False are Constant(Boolean) singletons — use type:Boolean.True /
type:Boolean.False (or Boolean.True / Boolean.False) as named alternatives to
Constant(Boolean){true} / Constant(Boolean){false} in type expressions.

362.fqnText: org blockml bml type Boolean False
362.name: False
362.documentation:
Singleton Constant for the literal false.
FQN: org.blockml.bml.type.Boolean.False.
Equivalent to Constant(Boolean){false} / Constant(Boolean){value: false}.

363.fqnText: org blockml bml type Boolean True
363.name: True
363.documentation:
Singleton Constant for the literal true.
FQN: org.blockml.bml.type.Boolean.True.
Equivalent to Constant(Boolean){true} / Constant(Boolean){value: true}.

364.name: BooleanEntity
364.documentation:
Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping a Boolean primitive. Binds T = Boolean on
org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
364.idea: A true-or-false value as a PrimitiveEntity

365.name: CapabilityIdentifier
365.documentation:
Concrete MemberIdentifier binding D = CapabilityDefinition. Value is a canonical
capability path (com.foo.Bar.capabilities.render) or a local capability name when paired with a
type qualifier. Syntax only — the owning type and capability need not exist.
CapabilityReference extends this type and adds existence. Use when addressing a potential
capability. see capability= uses CapabilityReference. CapabilityReference(B) introduces the
owning Block bound after resolution.

366.name: CapabilityIdentifierEntity
366.documentation:
Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping a CapabilityIdentifier primitive. Binds T =
CapabilityIdentifier on org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value
property automatically. Use when a potential capability path must appear as an identifiable
Block instance. Existence-checked counterparts use CapabilityReferenceEntity.
366.idea: A Capability member path as a PrimitiveEntity

367.name: CapabilityReference
367.documentation:
Existence-checked CapabilityIdentifier. Value is a canonical capability path
(com.foo.Bar.capabilities.render) or a local capability name when paired with a type qualifier.
The owning type and capability must resolve. Used as the type of see capability=. A potential
capability that need not exist uses CapabilityIdentifier.
367.idea: A path to a Capability member

368.name: CapabilityReferenceEntity
368.documentation:
Open generic Entity wrapping a CapabilityReference primitive. Forwards B from
org.blockml.bml.type.CapabilityReference onto org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType —
inherits the value property automatically as value : CapabilityReference(B). Use when a
resolved capability path must appear as an identifiable Block instance. Syntax-only paths use
CapabilityIdentifierEntity.
368.idea: A path to a Capability member as a PrimitiveEntity

369.name: Color
369.documentation:
Textual primitive subtype for color values. Unqualified name Color resolves to
org.blockml.bml.type.Color.

Accepted forms (case-insensitive for function names and named colors):
• Hex — CSS lengths #RGB, #RGBA, #RRGGBB, #RRGGBBAA (for example #afafaf, #a3d4e200)
• rgb / RGB — rgb(255,12,230)
• rgba / RGBA — rgba(34,54,21,0.5) with alpha in the CSS 0–1 range
• Named color — free-text name in language L (for example red, Blue); the base Color type
  does not validate named colors against a catalogue. A subtype may later constrain L to a
  fixed set of names.

Generic parameter L (NaturalLanguage, default English) names the language of free-text color
names. Bare Color resolves to English; supply Color(lang:German) only when named colors are
expected in another language.

370.name: ColorEntity
370.documentation:
Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping a Color primitive. Binds T = Color on
org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
Bare Color uses L = English for free-text color names.
370.idea: A color value as a PrimitiveEntity

371.name: Constant
371.documentation:
Standard ConstantType implementation for singleton (constant) values in type expressions —
without a dedicated literal-type language feature. Unqualified name Constant resolves to
org.blockml.bml.type.Constant.

Constant(T) binds the generic parameter T to any ValueType. Instance configuration supplies
the single allowed value via the value Property — for example Constant(Text){value: "auto"} or
Constant(Integer){value: 5}. The generic type argument is mandatory; bare Constant or
Constant{value: "auto"} without (T) is invalid.

The configured value Property belongs to the internal ValueType instance on the Property
definition. The external representation is always identical to the representation of the
underlying generic type T — Constant(Text){value: "auto"} accepts the external value "auto",
not { value: "auto" }.

Validation proceeds in two steps: first against the bound type T, then equality with the
configured constant value. No type inference is required — T is always authored explicitly
at the reference site.

Used primarily as a union alternative alongside ordinary ValueTypes:

Boolean | Constant(Text){value: "auto"}

Future literal union syntax (Boolean | "auto") desugars to this form. See
doc:ConstantValueType.

372.name: ConstantType
372.documentation:
Abstract ValueType branch for constant (singleton) value types. Unqualified name ConstantType
resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.ConstantType.

One of four language-level ValueType kinds (PrimitiveType · StructType · EnumType ·
ConstantType). ConstantType is neither a PrimitiveType, StructType, nor EnumType:

• A PrimitiveType defines a value domain (Text → all text values; Integer → all integers).
• A StructType defines the shape of the external value via its properties.
• An EnumType defines a closed set of named members; BOM stores id + typeFqn only.
• A ConstantType defines a singleton value domain — a value is valid if and only if it
  conforms to the underlying generic ValueType and equals the configured constant value.

The standard implementation is Constant<T extends ValueType> with a single Property
value : T. The generic type parameter is mandatory. Instance configuration supplies the
allowed value — for example Constant(Text){value: "auto"} or Constant(Integer){value: 5}.

The configured value Property belongs to the internal ValueType instance on the Property
definition — not to the property's external representation. The external value is always
identical to the representation of the underlying generic type T. For
Constant(Text){value: "auto"}, the external value is "auto" — not { value: "auto" }.

Validation proceeds in two steps:
1. Validate the supplied value against the generic ValueType T.
2. Compare the supplied value with the configured constant value.

Used primarily as a union alternative alongside ordinary ValueTypes:

Boolean | Constant(Text){value: "auto"}

373.name: Date
373.documentation:
BOM Core primitive ValueType for a calendar day without a time of day. Unqualified
name Date resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.Date. Extends org.blockml.bml.type.Temporal. Payload
values are stored on Properties — not on the Date type itself.

Authored values use ISO 8601 calendar-date form YYYY-MM-DD (for example 2024-08-29). Date is a
position on the calendar, not an elapsed span — use Duration for lengths of time.

Optional configuration Properties (min, max) configure a Property's owned Date instance via
inline type syntax — Date{min: "2020-01-01", max: "2030-12-31"}. Positional order: min, max.

374.name: DateEntity
374.documentation:
Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping a Date primitive. Binds T = Date on
org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
Use when a date must appear as an identifiable Block instance.
374.idea: A calendar date as a PrimitiveEntity

375.name: DateTime
375.documentation:
BOM Core primitive ValueType for a combined date and time of day. Unqualified name
DateTime resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.DateTime. Extends org.blockml.bml.type.Temporal. Payload
values are stored on Properties — not on the DateTime type itself.

Authored values use ISO 8601 combined date-and-time form (for example 2024-08-29T14:30:00,
2024-08-29T14:30:00Z, 2024-08-29T16:30:00+02:00). A trailing Z denotes UTC; a numeric offset
denotes a local civil time with that offset. DateTime is a position on the timeline, not an
elapsed span — use Duration for lengths of time.

Optional configuration Properties (min, max) configure a Property's owned DateTime instance via
inline type syntax — DateTime{min: "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", max: "2024-12-31T23:59:59Z"}.
Positional order: min, max.

376.name: DateTimeEntity
376.documentation:
Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping a DateTime primitive. Binds T = DateTime on
org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
Use when a date-time must appear as an identifiable Block instance.
376.idea: A date and time as a PrimitiveEntity

377.name: Decimal
377.documentation:
BOM Core primitive ValueType for decimal numbers — the default type for all
non-integer numeric values (3.5, 12.75, 0.1). Unqualified name Decimal resolves to
org.blockml.bml.type.Decimal. Extends org.blockml.bml.type.Number. Represents mathematical decimal
numbers; the renderer decides target representation (BigDecimal, decimal, number, …).
Payload values are stored on Properties — not on the Decimal type itself.

Generic parameter N (Unit, default unit:None) is forwarded from Number — e.g.
Decimal(unit:Meter). Bare Decimal is dimensionless.

Optional configuration Properties (precision, scale) configure a Property's owned Decimal
instance via inline type syntax — Decimal{precision: 10, scale: 2} or Decimal{10, 2}.
Positional order: precision, scale. See 20_value_type_instance_configuration.md.
precision/scale apply after parseValue (doc:ValueTypeParsing).

378.name: DecimalEntity
378.documentation:
Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping a Decimal primitive. Binds T = Decimal on
org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
378.idea: A decimal number as a PrimitiveEntity

379.name: Duration
379.documentation:
BOM Core primitive ValueType for an elapsed length of time. Unqualified name
Duration resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.Duration. Duration is its own primitive branch under
PrimitiveType — not a Temporal subtype. Temporal types name a position (Date, Time, DateTime);
Duration names a magnitude. Payload values are stored on Properties — not on the Duration type
itself.

Authored values use ISO 8601 duration form PnYnMnDTnHnMnS, with optional week form PnW (for
example P3D, PT1H30M, P1Y2M3DT4H5M6S, P2W). DateTime minus DateTime yields Duration; DateTime
plus Duration yields DateTime.

Duration is not a Number subtype. Calendar components such as years and months do not have a
fixed SI length.

Optional configuration Properties (min, max) configure a Property's owned Duration instance via
inline type syntax — Duration{min: "PT0S", max: "P1Y"}. Positional order: min, max.

380.name: DurationEntity
380.documentation:
Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping a Duration primitive. Binds T = Duration on
org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
Use when a duration must appear as an identifiable Block instance.
380.idea: A length of time as a PrimitiveEntity

381.name: EmptyStruct
381.documentation:
Instantiable StructType with no fields. Unqualified name EmptyStruct resolves to
org.blockml.bml.type.EmptyStruct.

The only compatible value is an empty object {}. EmptyStruct is a named, reusable unit
struct — the named counterpart of an anonymous empty StructType {}. It is not abstract:
use it wherever a StructType is required and no fields are needed, including Property
types, Capability inputType / outputType, and default generic bindings.

382.name: EnumType
382.documentation:
Abstract ValueType branch for closed enum ValueTypes — finite sets of named literal values.
Unqualified name EnumType resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.EnumType.

One of four language-level ValueType kinds (PrimitiveType · StructType · EnumType ·
ConstantType). EnumType is its own ValueType branch — not a StructType and not a
PrimitiveType:

• A PrimitiveType defines an open value domain (Text → all text values).
• A StructType defines the shape of the external value via its properties.
• An EnumType defines a closed set of named members; the external property value is the
  member identity (id + EnumType), not a struct payload.
• A ConstantType defines a singleton value domain.

Concrete EnumTypes declare allowed members as Block instances in the values
aggregation — no special enum syntax. Examples: Direction, Face, StudType, BaseCutout,
Align.

Each catalog member is a Block instance of the EnumType with a mandatory bml:id (the
reference token). An EnumType may declare arbitrary properties on the type — filled per
member in values — analogous to private fields on a Java enum constant. Those properties
are catalog metadata on the type definition (for example a MachineBlocks value string for
SCAD). They are not part of the stored property value when an EnumType is used.

BOM storage for a property typed with an EnumType is only id + typeFqn (the EnumType).
Catalog properties are looked up from the EnumType definition when a renderer or tool needs
them. The editor renders EnumType properties as a SelectBox; the compiler validates authored
tokens against values by id.

Properties typed with an EnumType must not carry <suggestions> — valid values come
exclusively from values → BML_SUGGESTIONS_ON_ENUM. Properties may still carry
<constraints> where a compatible Constraint sub-type exists.

Enum value references in property values (defaultValue, composition attributes, expressions):
when the property type is an EnumType, qualified references may omit the {EnumTypeFQN}::
prefix — Standard is equivalent to com.machineblocks.bml.type.BaseCutout::Standard when the
expected type is known from the property declaration. The short form is invalid for untyped
strings. The validator resolves tokens against values by id; unknown values → validation
error.

Domain XSD enums remain accepted during migration with BML_LEGACY_TYPE_SOURCE warning — new
enums should be defined as BML EnumType blocks.

Used wherever BlockML declares or validates closed value sets:
• Property <type> references (for example type="com.machineblocks.bml.type.BaseCutout")
• defaultValue and instance attribute values on EnumType properties
• Expression enum literals where the expected EnumType is known from context
• Library blocks export alongside other ValueType definitions
382.idea: A closed set of named values

383.name: FilePath
383.documentation:
Textual primitive subtype for file path values (for example
blockml-library.xsd). Unqualified name FilePath resolves
to org.blockml.bml.type.FilePath. Existence on disk is not part of parseValue.

384.name: FilePathEntity
384.documentation:
Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping a FilePath primitive. Binds T = FilePath on
org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
384.idea: A filesystem path as a PrimitiveEntity

385.name: Float
385.documentation:
BOM Core primitive ValueType for binary floating-point numbers. Not the default
floating-point type — use Decimal unless binary IEEE754 semantics are explicitly required
(GPU, OpenGL, native C APIs, binary protocols). Unqualified name Float resolves to
org.blockml.bml.type.Float. Extends org.blockml.bml.type.Number. Values are stored in Properties.

Generic parameter N (Unit, default unit:None) is forwarded from Number — e.g.
Float(unit:Millimeter). Bare Float is dimensionless.

parseValue accepts a binary-floating literal (same lexical form as Number, including
exponent). NaN and infinities are rejected (doc:ValueTypeParsing).

386.name: FloatEntity
386.documentation:
Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping a Float primitive. Binds T = Float on
org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
386.idea: A floating-point number as a PrimitiveEntity

387.name: InstanceIdentifier
387.documentation:
ValueType for non-owning instance name strings identified by bml:id. Unqualified name
InstanceIdentifier resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.InstanceIdentifier. Syntax only — the
named instance need not exist. No generic parameters. InstanceReference(T) extends this type
and adds existence plus the branch bound T.

Lexical forms:
• Local id — myId (visibility-scoped within the enclosing composition)
• Qualified — {EnclosingBlockFQN}::{instanceId} (e.g. com.foo.Bar::myId)
• Prefixed qualified — foo:Bar::myId (xmlns QName of the enclosing Block document, then :: and id)

Not a Block type FQN (use TypeIdentifier / TypeReference), not a package string (use
PackageIdentifier / PackageReference), not a member definition path (use MemberIdentifier /
AssociationIdentifier), and not a resource URI (use URI).

Primary use — planned or future instance pointers. AssociationDefinition type and see
instance= use InstanceReference — not InstanceIdentifier.

388.name: InstanceIdentifierEntity
388.documentation:
Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping an InstanceIdentifier primitive. Binds T =
InstanceIdentifier on org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value
property automatically. Use when an instance name that need not exist must appear as an
identifiable Block instance. Existence-checked counterparts use InstanceReferenceEntity.
388.idea: A Block instance name as a PrimitiveEntity

389.name: InstanceReference
389.documentation:
ValueType for non-owning pointers to concrete Block instances identified by bml:id that must
resolve. Extends InstanceIdentifier (syntax, including inherited parseValue) with existence
and the branch bound T.
Unqualified name InstanceReference resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.InstanceReference.

Lexical forms:
• Local id — myId (visibility-scoped within the enclosing composition)
• Qualified — {EnclosingBlockFQN}::{instanceId} (e.g. com.foo.Bar::myId)
• Prefixed qualified — foo:Bar::myId (xmlns QName of the enclosing Block document, then :: and id)

Not a Block type FQN (use TypeReference), not a package string (use PackageReference), not a
member definition path (use MemberIdentifier / AssociationReference), and not a resource URI
(use URI). An instance name that need not exist uses InstanceIdentifier — not
InstanceReference.

Generic parameter:
• T (baseType core:Block) — target instance must satisfy T

In type="..." attributes, write generic applications with round parentheses:
• InstanceReference(core:Block) → 0..1 pointer to a core:Block instance
• InstanceReference(bml:Self)[] → 0..n pointers to instances of the effective Block type

Primary use — AssociationDefinition type (associations may only declare InstanceReference(T)
or InstanceReference(T)[] — instance-to-instance model links). Also the type of see instance=
on StructuralDefinition.Reference (documentation type→instance links — not Associations).

Resolution and visibility rules: docs/01_bom_core.md — Qualified Block Instance References
(public aggregation, static authored bml:id, BML_UNRESOLVABLE_INSTANCE_REF, …).

390.name: InstanceReferenceEntity
390.documentation:
Open generic Entity wrapping an InstanceReference primitive. Forwards T from
org.blockml.bml.type.InstanceReference onto org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType —
inherits the value property automatically as value : InstanceReference(T). Use when a resolved
instance pointer must appear as an identifiable Block instance. Syntax-only names use
InstanceIdentifierEntity.
390.idea: A Block instance pointer as a PrimitiveEntity

391.name: Integer
391.documentation:
BOM Core primitive ValueType for whole numbers. Unqualified name Integer resolves
to org.blockml.bml.type.Integer. Extends org.blockml.bml.type.Number. Payload values are stored on
Properties — not on the Integer type itself.

Generic parameter N (Unit, default unit:None) is forwarded from Number — e.g.
Integer(unit:Millimeter). Bare Integer is dimensionless.

Optional configuration Properties (min, max) configure a Property's owned Integer instance via
inline type syntax — Integer{min: 0, max: 100}. Positional order: min, max. See
20_value_type_instance_configuration.md. min/max are applied after parseValue
(doc:ValueTypeParsing).

392.name: IntegerEntity
392.documentation:
Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping an Integer primitive. Binds T = Integer on
org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
Use when an integer must appear as an identifiable Block instance.
392.idea: A whole number as a PrimitiveEntity

393.name: MemberIdentifier
393.documentation:
Abstract ValueType for member definition path names — properties, aggregations,
associations, and capabilities. Syntax only — the named member and owning type need not exist.
Concrete Identifier specializations bind D without requiring the path to resolve.
Existence-checked counterparts (PropertyReference, AggregationReference, AssociationReference,
CapabilityReference) extend the matching Identifier and introduce the owning Block bound B.

Value forms:
• Canonical definition path — for example com.foo.Bar.properties.width
• Local member name when paired with a type qualifier (for example see type="com.foo.Bar"
  property="width" → com.foo.Bar.properties.width)

Generic parameter:
• D (baseType def:MemberDefinition) — member definition kind (path shape). The owning Block
  bound B is introduced on PropertyReference / … after resolution — not here.

Concrete Identifier specializations bind D:
• PropertyIdentifier     → D = def:PropertyDefinition
• AggregationIdentifier  → D = def:AggregationDefinition
• AssociationIdentifier  → D = def:AssociationDefinition
• CapabilityIdentifier   → D = def:CapabilityDefinition

There is no collective existence type for an unbound member kind — member sites declare a
concrete Reference. Not for Block type identity (use TypeIdentifier / TypeReference) or
instance pointers (use InstanceIdentifier / InstanceReference).

394.name: MemberIdentifierEntity
394.documentation:
Open generic Entity wrapping a MemberIdentifier primitive. Forwards D from
org.blockml.bml.type.MemberIdentifier onto org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType —
inherits the value property automatically as value : MemberIdentifier(D). Use when a member
path that need not exist must appear as an identifiable Block instance. Existence-checked
counterparts use PropertyReferenceEntity / AggregationReferenceEntity / …. Concrete Identifier
Entities (PropertyIdentifierEntity, …) bind D.
394.idea: A Block member path as a PrimitiveEntity

395.name: MimeType
395.documentation:
Textual primitive subtype for MIME type values (for example text/plain,
application/json). Unqualified name MimeType resolves to     org.blockml.bml.type.MimeType.

396.name: MimeTypeEntity
396.documentation:
Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping a MimeType primitive. Binds T = MimeType on
org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
396.idea: A MIME type as a PrimitiveEntity

397.name: Number
397.documentation:
Abstract numeric primitive branch under org.blockml.bml.type.PrimitiveType.
Concrete types: Integer (whole numbers), Decimal (default for non-integer numeric values),
Float (binary floating-point — only when IEEE754 semantics are explicitly required).
Abstract numeric branch — not resolvable via Property.type implicit namespace; use Integer, Decimal, or Float explicitly.
Numeric types describe semantics only; values are stored in Properties.

Generic parameter N constrains the measurement unit (extends org.blockml.bml.core.Unit).
Default is org.blockml.bml.unit.None — bare Number / Integer / Decimal / Float are dimensionless.
Supply N at reference sites when a unit is required, e.g. Integer(unit:Millimeter).

parseValue accepts a numeric literal (optional sign, digits, optional fraction and exponent).
Integer, Decimal, and Float refine the lexical form. min/max and unit are not applied here
(doc:ValueTypeParsing).

398.name: PackageIdentifier
398.documentation:
ValueType for package names — reverse-domain package strings without a type (class) segment.
Unqualified name PackageIdentifier resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.PackageIdentifier. The
most specific PackageSelector: a concrete package name with no wildcards
(PackageIdentifier <: PackageSelector). Syntax only — the named package need not be known
in the corpus. PackageReference extends this type and adds existence. No generic parameters.

Package format (Java-style reverse-domain, dot-separated, all lowercase):
• Package segments — lowercase (for example org.blockml.bml.core, com.machineblocks.bml.type)
• No class segment — PascalCase type names belong on TypeIdentifier (org.blockml.bml.type.Integer
  is a type FQN, not a package)
• Valid: org.blockml.bml.type · com.example.bml
• Invalid as PackageIdentifier: org.blockml.bml.type.Integer · core:Block · Integer

Namespace prefixes in BML (core:, type:, def:, …) bind to packages; a prefix that targets a
Package resolves to that package string (core → org.blockml.bml.core). A prefix that targets an
Annotation is not a PackageIdentifier.

Primary use — planned or foreign package names. Documentation see package= uses
PackageReference. Block type FQNs use TypeIdentifier / TypeReference. Instance pointers use
InstanceIdentifier / InstanceReference. Member paths use the MemberIdentifier branch.

399.name: PackageIdentifierEntity
399.documentation:
Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping a PackageIdentifier primitive. Binds T = PackageIdentifier
on org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
Use when a package name that need not exist must appear as an identifiable Block instance.
Existence-checked counterparts use PackageReferenceEntity.
399.idea: A package name as a PrimitiveEntity

400.name: PackageReference
400.documentation:
ValueType for package references — reverse-domain package strings without a type (class)
segment that must be known in the corpus. Extends PackageIdentifier (syntax, including
inherited parseValue) with existence.
Unqualified name PackageReference resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.PackageReference.
Sibling of TypeReference under Text — not a TypeReference subtype. No generic parameters.

Package format (Java-style reverse-domain, dot-separated, all lowercase):
• Package segments — lowercase (for example org.blockml.bml.core, com.machineblocks.bml.type)
• No class segment — PascalCase type names belong on TypeReference (org.blockml.bml.type.Integer
  is a type FQN, not a package)
• Valid: org.blockml.bml.type · com.example.bml
• Invalid as PackageReference: org.blockml.bml.type.Integer · core:Block · Integer

Namespace prefixes in BML (core:, type:, def:, …) bind to packages; a prefix that targets a
Package resolves to that package string (core → org.blockml.bml.core). A prefix that targets an
Annotation is not a PackageReference.

Primary use — documentation see package= on StructuralDefinition.Reference, and any property
that names a package rather than a Block type. When a package reference must appear as a PrimitiveEntity
in composition or aggregation, use org.blockml.bml.type.PackageReferenceEntity.

A package name that need not exist uses PackageIdentifier — not PackageReference. Block type
FQNs and TypeExpressions use org.blockml.bml.type.TypeReference — not PackageReference.
Instance pointers use InstanceReference. Member definition paths use the MemberIdentifier
branch.

401.name: PackageReferenceEntity
401.documentation:
Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping a PackageReference primitive. Binds T = PackageReference
on org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
Use when a package reference must appear as an identifiable Block instance.
401.idea: A package name reference as a PrimitiveEntity

402.name: PackageSelector
402.documentation:
ValueType for package selectors — reverse-domain package patterns that match one or more
packages. Unqualified name PackageSelector resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.PackageSelector.
Syntax only — matched packages need not be known in the corpus. A concrete package name is
the most specific selector: PackageIdentifier <: PackageSelector. No generic parameters.

Segments are dot-separated. Concrete package segments are lowercase. Wildcards:
• * as a whole segment — exactly one arbitrary segment
• ** as a whole segment — one or more arbitrary segments (1..n, not 0..n)
• * inside a segment — zero or more characters inside that segment only
• ** inside a segment — not allowed (a.foo**.b and a.**foo.b are invalid)

Neither a.* nor a.** includes package a itself — unlike TypeSelector, where trailing **
includes types in the starting package:
• a — exact package a
• a.* — every direct child package of a (a.b yes; a and a.b.c no)
• a.** — every package descendant of a (a.b, a.b.c yes; a no)
• a.*.b — exactly one segment between a and b (a.c.b yes; a.b and a.c.d.b no)
• a.**.b — one or more segments between a and b (a.c.b, a.c.d.b yes; a.b no)
• a.fo*.b — character wildcard inside one segment (a.foo.b, a.foobar.b yes; a.x.foo.b no)

Valid: org.blockml.bml.core · org.blockml.bml.* · org.blockml.** · org.blockml.bml.co* ·
org.*.bml.*. Invalid: org.blockml.bml.Core · org.Blockml.bml.core (uppercase package
segment).

Type-name patterns use TypeSelector. Existence-checked package names use PackageReference.

403.name: PackageSelectorEntity
403.documentation:
Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping a PackageSelector primitive. Binds T = PackageSelector
on org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
Use when a package selector must appear as an identifiable Block instance.
Concrete package names use PackageIdentifierEntity.
403.idea: A package selector as a PrimitiveEntity

404.name: PrimitiveType
404.documentation:
Abstract branch for built-in scalar ValueTypes. PrimitiveTypes describe semantics
only — they never store concrete values. All values are stored exclusively in Properties.

Numeric branch: Number (Integer, Decimal, Float). Textual branch: Text (TypeSelector /
TypeIdentifier / TypeReference, PackageSelector / PackageIdentifier / PackageReference, InstanceIdentifier / InstanceReference,
MemberIdentifier / PropertyIdentifier / PropertyReference / …, Version, URL, URI, UUID, FilePath,
MimeType, …). Temporal
branch: Temporal (Date, Time, DateTime) — calendar or clock positions. Boolean is its own
branch — neither textual nor numeric. Duration is its own branch — an elapsed-time magnitude,
not a Temporal subtype.

Lexical acceptance of authored text is parseValue (Text → bml:Self, throws
InvalidValueException). Concrete primitives implement a deterministic host-evaluable body.
Configuration, constraints, and Reference existence run after parse — doc:ValueTypeParsing.

When a primitive value must exist as a PrimitiveEntity inside a composition or aggregation, use a
concrete PrimitiveEntity specialization (for example IntegerEntity) — not by adding a value member to
the PrimitiveType.

Invalid: <type:Integer value="5"/> — PrimitiveTypes cannot carry values.
Valid: <property name="count" type="Integer"><value>5</value></property>

405.name: PropertyIdentifier
405.documentation:
Concrete MemberIdentifier binding D = PropertyDefinition. Value is a canonical
property path (com.foo.Bar.properties.width) or a local property name when paired with a Block
qualifier. Syntax only — the owning type and property need not exist. PropertyReference extends
this type and adds existence. Use when addressing a potential property (planned, generated, or
foreign). see property= uses PropertyReference. PropertyReference(B) introduces the owning
Block bound after resolution.

406.name: PropertyIdentifierEntity
406.documentation:
Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping a PropertyIdentifier primitive. Binds T =
PropertyIdentifier on org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value
property automatically. Use when a potential property path must appear as an identifiable
Block instance. Existence-checked counterparts use PropertyReferenceEntity.
406.idea: A Property member path as a PrimitiveEntity

407.name: PropertyReference
407.documentation:
Existence-checked PropertyIdentifier. Introduces the owning Block bound B.
Value is a canonical property path (com.foo.Bar.properties.width) or a local property name
when paired with a Block qualifier. The owning type and property must resolve. Used as the
type of see property= and other PropertyDefinition reference sites. A potential property
that need not exist uses PropertyIdentifier.
407.idea: A path to a Property member

408.name: PropertyReferenceEntity
408.documentation:
Open generic Entity wrapping a PropertyReference primitive. Forwards B from
org.blockml.bml.type.PropertyReference onto org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType —
inherits the value property automatically as value : PropertyReference(B). Use when a resolved
property path must appear as an identifiable Block instance. Syntax-only paths use
PropertyIdentifierEntity.
408.idea: A path to a Property member as a PrimitiveEntity

409.name: StructType
409.documentation:
Abstract ValueType branch for composite value objects — complex values described by normal
Properties. Unqualified name StructType resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.StructType.

One of four language-level ValueType kinds (PrimitiveType · StructType · EnumType ·
ConstantType). StructType is a dedicated branch — EnumType is a sibling under ValueType,
not a subtype of StructType.
StructTypes describe the structure of a value — their properties define the data layout.
StructTypes usually contain no values themselves; Property values remain stored in the owning
Property. Default values on StructType property definitions are allowed. Concrete StructTypes
declare <properties> whose members become struct fields — no special struct syntax.
Examples: EmptyStruct (no fields; only {}), Size3d, Color, Address, Transform.
Parameterized value types (for example Box<T>) are StructTypes that declare
<genericTypes> — not a separate ValueType branch.

Struct property access is exclusively by name (size.x, size.y, size.z). Numeric index access
on StructType members (size[0]) is not valid — StructType is a typed object with named
properties only. Positional function-parameter syntax (#tool.capa("x", "y")) is handled by
FunctionMapping at call sites, not by general StructType semantics.

Field declaration order remains significant for:
• Positional array literals (size="[4, 2, 3]") — values map to properties by declaration order
• FunctionMapping positional parameter order for capability calls
• Compatibility — existing field order must not change across versions; new fields may be
  appended only at the end

Named object literals (size="{ x: 4, y: 2, z: 3 }") and attribute syntax on StructType
instances (<Size3d x="4" y="2" z="3"/>) are type-equivalent authoring forms.

Anonymous StructTypes — { field: Type, … } is a StructType without a declared name, written
directly in a type expression; it is the mechanism for structured Capability inputs. Each field
is Identifier ":" TypeExpression, so a field type is a full type expression and not merely an
unqualified type name: qualified references, multiplicity, generics, unions, instance
configuration, and nested anonymous StructTypes are all valid.
• { list: core:ValueType[], index: Integer } — qualified reference with multiplicity
• { values: foo:Thing[1..n] } · { value: Integer | Text } · { nested: { x: Integer, y: Integer } }
The field-name separator and the prefix colon of a qualified reference sit at different grammar
levels (list : core:ValueType[]) — unambiguous, not a naming conflict. Field declaration order is
significant exactly as for named StructTypes. Rejecting a qualified field type while accepting an
unqualified one is a parser / mapper limitation, not a type-expression ambiguity.
See doc:TypeExpressions — Anonymous StructTypes.

Used wherever BlockML declares or validates structured values:
• Property <type> references (for example type="com.machineblocks.bml.type.Size3d")
• Block instances of the StructType as composition children or property payloads
• Capability inputType / outputType — named StructType or anonymous struct expressions
• Generic type applications (for example Box<Integer>) on StructTypes with
  <genericTypes>

410.name: Temporal
410.documentation:
Abstract temporal primitive branch under org.blockml.bml.type.PrimitiveType.
Concrete types: Date (calendar day), Time (time of day), DateTime (instant combining date and
time). Temporal types name a position on a calendar or clock — not a length of elapsed time.
Abstract temporal branch — not resolvable via Property.type implicit namespace; use Date, Time,
or DateTime explicitly.
Temporal types describe semantics only; values are stored in Properties.

Duration is a sibling primitive under PrimitiveType, not a Temporal subtype. DateTime minus
DateTime yields Duration; DateTime plus Duration yields DateTime; DateTime plus DateTime is
invalid.

parseValue stays abstract here — Date, Time, and DateTime implement ISO lexical forms
(doc:ValueTypeParsing).

411.name: Text
411.documentation:
BOM Core primitive ValueType for text. Unqualified name Text resolves to
org.blockml.bml.type.Text. Replaces the former String type — BlockML describes semantic types, not
implementation data structures. Renderers may map Text to Java String, TypeScript string,
Python str, C# string, or any target representation.

Semantic subtypes extend Text: TypeSelector / TypeIdentifier / TypeReference, PackageSelector /
PackageIdentifier / PackageReference, InstanceIdentifier / InstanceReference, MemberIdentifier (PropertyIdentifier /
PropertyReference / …), Version, URL, URI, UUID, FilePath, MimeType, …
Concrete payload values are stored on Properties — not on the Text type itself.

Member values of this type may contain restricted ${ } holes in running text
(InterpolatedTextValue). A whole-value "${ expr }" remains an ExpressionValue. See
doc:Expressions.

Optional configuration Properties (minLength, maxLength) configure a Property's owned Text
