extend this branch. MemberDefinition.groups overrides StructuralDefinition.groups to
TypeReferenceEntity(group:MemberGroup)[].

Abstract identification marker for the Definition branch under org.blockml.bml.core.Block.
Intentionally empty — no properties, aggregations, or Sub-Blocks. Any block whose baseType
chain includes org.blockml.bml.core.Definition is a Definition meta-model block
(org.blockml.bml.definition.*). Concrete grammar lives on subtypes such as
org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition and org.blockml.bml.definition.BlockDefinition.

Used as a generic constraint and branch marker for definition-element references. Member path
ValueTypes (org.blockml.bml.type.MemberIdentifier and children) constrain D to
org.blockml.bml.definition.MemberDefinition. Framework core branch types remain baseType markers;
domain interface-style type bounds use contracts and satisfiesTypeBound — see 17_type_system_bml.md.

Abstract meta-model base for all Block definition documents — root blocks,
Sub-Blocks, and embedded virtual files. Semantically a Class: declarative type shape without instance
state. Parsed into BomDocument.block and nested block definition trees. Generic type parameter B
binds this definition to the Block type it describes — conceptually BlockDefinition of
com.foo.Bar when B resolves to com.foo.Bar.

Declares identity first (name, type, baseType, version), then semantic and discovery fields
(is, isNot, aliases), generic parameters, contracts, and
member declaration containers (properties, aggregations, associations, capabilities). Inherits
summary and keywords aggregation (meta.Keyword[]) from
org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition. isNot is block-level only; aliases aggregation
(meta.Alias[]) lists ad-hoc Alias instances or domain FixedAlias catalogue blocks. Omitted when unnecessary. Type modifiers abstract and final are inherited from
org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition. Every definition element is addressable via
its canonical structural path within the Block FQN (for example com.foo.Bar.properties.width).
Member declaration order in BML is preserved in BOM and is significant for StructType
positional mapping and render targets.

Declares definition (meta-model role selector) and subBlocks (recursive nested type hierarchy).
Specialized as three sibling kinds that each override definition with a tighter TypeReference and
default: SubBlockDefinition (nested), RootBlockDefinition (document root + embeddedBlocks),
EmbeddedBlockDefinition (virtual .bml under root embeddedBlocks). Identity properties type and
baseType are TypeReference strings (not TypeReferenceEntity aggregations) — type names the Block
being declared; baseType carries the parent TypeExpression including generic applications. Other
type references (composition tags, member type attributes, contracts) accept FQN, xmlns QName,
context-bound unqualified fallback, or Sub-Block-relative names — all normalized to a canonical
FQN during resolution (BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE, BML_AMBIGUOUS_TYPE, BML_UNKNOWN_NAMESPACE_PREFIX).

Abstract numeric primitive branch under org.blockml.bml.type.PrimitiveType.
Concrete types: Integer (whole numbers), Decimal (default for non-integer numeric values),
Float (binary floating-point — only when IEEE754 semantics are explicitly required).
Abstract numeric branch — not resolvable via Property.type implicit namespace; use Integer, Decimal, or Float explicitly.
Numeric types describe semantics only; values are stored in Properties.

Generic parameter N constrains the measurement unit (extends org.blockml.bml.core.Unit).
Default is org.blockml.bml.unit.None — bare Number / Integer / Decimal / Float are dimensionless.
Supply N at reference sites when a unit is required, e.g. Integer(unit:Millimeter).

parseValue accepts a numeric literal (optional sign, digits, optional fraction and exponent).
Integer, Decimal, and Float refine the lexical form. min/max and unit are not applied here
(doc:ValueTypeParsing).

Abstract publishable library unit — groups exported Block and ValueType definitions,
optional legacy XSD schemas, dependencies on other libraries, and nested sub-libraries.
Replaces the legacy library.xml descriptor. XSD is not a standard feature
(doc:DocumentFormat).

Framework base type in org.blockml.bml.core — not exported via Library blocks.
Concrete Library.bml files inherit from BlockLibrary and declare aggregations explicitly.

Catalog aggregations are public and readOnly: foreign Blocks and tools may inspect a library
descriptor (e.g. list exports or dependencies) in expressions; only the Library definition
(and child overrides) may author the catalog. Instances must not rewrite these members.

Documentation prose language is Definition meta (def:BlockDefinition.language) on the Library
document — not a catalog aggregation. Exported blocks inherit that document language unless
they declare their own <language>.

Aggregations (each aggregation member is opened by name; none is default):
• readMe — required human/LLM reading entry (ReadMe block, 1..1)
• bootstrap — optional automation SPOE (Bootstrap block, 0..1)
• dependencies — other Library blocks this library depends on (typical: inner library
  depends on outer)
• subLibraries — nested child Library blocks grouped under this library
• schemas — optional legacy XSD paths as FilePathEntity instances; omitted by default
• blocks — exported Block and ValueType definitions (membership SSOT)

readMe and bootstrap hold TypeReferenceEntity children — empty QName sugar sets value to
that FQN. dependencies, subLibraries, and blocks use the same pattern. Optional bml:version on
sugar (or explicit TypeReferenceEntity) children is an exact-version assert against the
referenced type (value) — same semantics as external composition references; omitted → resolve
from TypeRegistry / library context; no match → BML_UNKNOWN_VERSION. schemas holds
FilePathEntity composition children; value is the relative .xsd path from the library package
root (directory containing Library.bml).

Concrete Library.bml <references> rule — at most two <see> entries:
1. Required: relation=ReadFirst targeting the same ReadMe named in readMe.
2. Optional: relation=ThenContinueWith targeting the Bootstrap named in bootstrap, only when
   bootstrap is present. Signals: after reading, continue by executing the automation SPOE.
No AuthoringGuide / DeepDive / Extends / SeeAlso (or other) entries on concrete Libraries —
those belong on documentation blocks, not on the catalog descriptor.

Abstract Relation subtype that may be used only on <see type="…"> entries —
never on instance, file, url, property, aggregation, association, or capability targets.
Not a core root branch — lives with the other relation types in org.blockml.bml.relation.*.

Generic T is the allowed target Block branch. The resolved type of see type= must satisfy
satisfiesTypeBound(resolve(type), T) — otherwise BML_TYPE_BOUND_NOT_SATISFIED. Default
T = core:Block — any Block type reference is allowed until a concrete subtype binds T more
narrowly (e.g. ThenContinueWith binds T = core:Bootstrap).

Plain Relation (SeeAlso, AuthoringGuide, …) remains unrestricted across target kinds.
TypeRelation is for relations whose semantics require a Block type identity target.

Abstract temporal primitive branch under org.blockml.bml.type.PrimitiveType.
Concrete types: Date (calendar day), Time (time of day), DateTime (instant combining date and
time). Temporal types name a position on a calendar or clock — not a length of elapsed time.
Abstract temporal branch — not resolvable via Property.type implicit namespace; use Date, Time,
or DateTime explicitly.
Temporal types describe semantics only; values are stored in Properties.

Duration is a sibling primitive under PrimitiveType, not a Temporal subtype. DateTime minus
DateTime yields Duration; DateTime plus Duration yields DateTime; DateTime plus DateTime is
invalid.

parseValue stays abstract here — Date, Time, and DateTime implement ISO lexical forms
(doc:ValueTypeParsing).

Abstract universal root for all constraint types. Specialized by
org.blockml.bml.constraint.ValueConstraint (property value rules) and
org.blockml.bml.constraint.StructuralConstraint (definition-shape rules on Blocks and members).
Every concrete constraint extends one of the branch types; the <constraints> embedding
context determines the target and automatic generic binding — authors never specify target or
type arguments in BML. Constraints describe the condition only. Whether BlockML enforces a
constraint is controlled by the optional validation property, which references an
org.blockml.bml.core.Validation block. When validation is omitted, validateConstraints() does not
enforce the rule — the constraint remains metadata for renderers, editors, runtimes, and custom
validators. The constraint instance itself is still validated (type, properties, generic
binding, branch compatibility).

Abstract ValueType branch for closed enum ValueTypes — finite sets of named literal values.
Unqualified name EnumType resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.EnumType.

One of four language-level ValueType kinds (PrimitiveType · StructType · EnumType ·
ConstantType). EnumType is its own ValueType branch — not a StructType and not a
PrimitiveType:

• A PrimitiveType defines an open value domain (Text → all text values).
• A StructType defines the shape of the external value via its properties.
• An EnumType defines a closed set of named members; the external property value is the
  member identity (id + EnumType), not a struct payload.
• A ConstantType defines a singleton value domain.

Concrete EnumTypes declare allowed members as Block instances in the values
aggregation — no special enum syntax. Examples: Direction, Face, StudType, BaseCutout,
Align.

Each catalog member is a Block instance of the EnumType with a mandatory bml:id (the
reference token). An EnumType may declare arbitrary properties on the type — filled per
member in values — analogous to private fields on a Java enum constant. Those properties
are catalog metadata on the type definition (for example a MachineBlocks value string for
SCAD). They are not part of the stored property value when an EnumType is used.

BOM storage for a property typed with an EnumType is only id + typeFqn (the EnumType).
Catalog properties are looked up from the EnumType definition when a renderer or tool needs
them. The editor renders EnumType properties as a SelectBox; the compiler validates authored
tokens against values by id.

Properties typed with an EnumType must not carry <suggestions> — valid values come
exclusively from values → BML_SUGGESTIONS_ON_ENUM. Properties may still carry
<constraints> where a compatible Constraint sub-type exists.

Enum value references in property values (defaultValue, composition attributes, expressions):
when the property type is an EnumType, qualified references may omit the {EnumTypeFQN}::
prefix — Standard is equivalent to com.machineblocks.bml.type.BaseCutout::Standard when the
expected type is known from the property declaration. The short form is invalid for untyped
strings. The validator resolves tokens against values by id; unknown values → validation
error.

Domain XSD enums remain accepted during migration with BML_LEGACY_TYPE_SOURCE warning — new
enums should be defined as BML EnumType blocks.

Used wherever BlockML declares or validates closed value sets:
• Property <type> references (for example type="com.machineblocks.bml.type.BaseCutout")
• defaultValue and instance attribute values on EnumType properties
• Expression enum literals where the expected EnumType is known from context
• Library blocks export alongside other ValueType definitions

Abstract ValueType branch for composite value objects — complex values described by normal
Properties. Unqualified name StructType resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.StructType.

One of four language-level ValueType kinds (PrimitiveType · StructType · EnumType ·
ConstantType). StructType is a dedicated branch — EnumType is a sibling under ValueType,
not a subtype of StructType.
StructTypes describe the structure of a value — their properties define the data layout.
StructTypes usually contain no values themselves; Property values remain stored in the owning
Property. Default values on StructType property definitions are allowed. Concrete StructTypes
declare <properties> whose members become struct fields — no special struct syntax.
Examples: EmptyStruct (no fields; only {}), Size3d, Color, Address, Transform.
Parameterized value types (for example Box<T>) are StructTypes that declare
<genericTypes> — not a separate ValueType branch.

Struct property access is exclusively by name (size.x, size.y, size.z). Numeric index access
on StructType members (size[0]) is not valid — StructType is a typed object with named
properties only. Positional function-parameter syntax (#tool.capa("x", "y")) is handled by
FunctionMapping at call sites, not by general StructType semantics.

Field declaration order remains significant for:
• Positional array literals (size="[4, 2, 3]") — values map to properties by declaration order
• FunctionMapping positional parameter order for capability calls
• Compatibility — existing field order must not change across versions; new fields may be
  appended only at the end

Named object literals (size="{ x: 4, y: 2, z: 3 }") and attribute syntax on StructType
instances (<Size3d x="4" y="2" z="3"/>) are type-equivalent authoring forms.

Anonymous StructTypes — { field: Type, … } is a StructType without a declared name, written
directly in a type expression; it is the mechanism for structured Capability inputs. Each field
is Identifier ":" TypeExpression, so a field type is a full type expression and not merely an
unqualified type name: qualified references, multiplicity, generics, unions, instance
configuration, and nested anonymous StructTypes are all valid.
• { list: core:ValueType[], index: Integer } — qualified reference with multiplicity
• { values: foo:Thing[1..n] } · { value: Integer | Text } · { nested: { x: Integer, y: Integer } }
The field-name separator and the prefix colon of a qualified reference sit at different grammar
levels (list : core:ValueType[]) — unambiguous, not a naming conflict. Field declaration order is
significant exactly as for named StructTypes. Rejecting a qualified field type while accepting an
unqualified one is a parser / mapper limitation, not a type-expression ambiguity.
See doc:TypeExpressions — Anonymous StructTypes.

Used wherever BlockML declares or validates structured values:
• Property <type> references (for example type="com.machineblocks.bml.type.Size3d")
• Block instances of the StructType as composition children or property payloads
• Capability inputType / outputType — named StructType or anonymous struct expressions
• Generic type applications (for example Box<Integer>) on StructTypes with
  <genericTypes>

Abstract ValueType branch for constant (singleton) value types. Unqualified name ConstantType
resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.ConstantType.

One of four language-level ValueType kinds (PrimitiveType · StructType · EnumType ·
ConstantType). ConstantType is neither a PrimitiveType, StructType, nor EnumType:

• A PrimitiveType defines a value domain (Text → all text values; Integer → all integers).
• A StructType defines the shape of the external value via its properties.
• An EnumType defines a closed set of named members; BOM stores id + typeFqn only.
• A ConstantType defines a singleton value domain — a value is valid if and only if it
  conforms to the underlying generic ValueType and equals the configured constant value.

The standard implementation is Constant<T extends ValueType> with a single Property
value : T. The generic type parameter is mandatory. Instance configuration supplies the
allowed value — for example Constant(Text){value: "auto"} or Constant(Integer){value: 5}.

The configured value Property belongs to the internal ValueType instance on the Property
definition — not to the property's external representation. The external value is always
identical to the representation of the underlying generic type T. For
Constant(Text){value: "auto"}, the external value is "auto" — not { value: "auto" }.

Validation proceeds in two steps:
1. Validate the supplied value against the generic ValueType T.
2. Compare the supplied value with the configured constant value.

Used primarily as a union alternative alongside ordinary ValueTypes:

Boolean | Constant(Text){value: "auto"}

Abstract ValueType for member definition path names — properties, aggregations,
associations, and capabilities. Syntax only — the named member and owning type need not exist.
Concrete Identifier specializations bind D without requiring the path to resolve.
Existence-checked counterparts (PropertyReference, AggregationReference, AssociationReference,
CapabilityReference) extend the matching Identifier and introduce the owning Block bound B.

Value forms:
• Canonical definition path — for example com.foo.Bar.properties.width
• Local member name when paired with a type qualifier (for example see type="com.foo.Bar"
  property="width" → com.foo.Bar.properties.width)

Generic parameter:
• D (baseType def:MemberDefinition) — member definition kind (path shape). The owning Block
  bound B is introduced on PropertyReference / … after resolution — not here.

Concrete Identifier specializations bind D:
• PropertyIdentifier     → D = def:PropertyDefinition
• AggregationIdentifier  → D = def:AggregationDefinition
• AssociationIdentifier  → D = def:AssociationDefinition
• CapabilityIdentifier   → D = def:CapabilityDefinition

There is no collective existence type for an unbound member kind — member sites declare a
concrete Reference. Not for Block type identity (use TypeIdentifier / TypeReference) or
instance pointers (use InstanceIdentifier / InstanceReference).

Action capability. Behaviour that neither consumes an external payload nor
produces one — a pure side effect or command (trigger, reset, refresh, invalidate).
Inherits _hasInput=false and _hasOutput=false; inputType and outputType are forbidden.

Aggregation-level structural constraint. T binds to the effective
AggregationDefinition. When validation is set, each composition child under the aggregation must
resolve to the given Block type FQN. Reference implementation for AggregationConstraint branch.

Angular unit — degree of arc (°). Use for rotation and orientation angles,
e.g. Decimal(unit:Degree) or Float(unit:Degree).

Annotations formalize directive namespaces. They are orthogonal to the Definition meta-model
(org.blockml.bml.definition.*) — they do not describe block structure, members, or constraints.
Naming overlap (Property, Aggregation, …) classifies directive form only;
Annotation.Property is not def:PropertyDefinition.

Every BML-semantic xmlns prefix resolves to either a Package (type addressing) or a concrete
Annotation (directives). preferredAlias is authoring convention only (bml, scad) — the BOM
stores the Annotation FQN, never the XML prefix. Document default xmlns remains
http://blockml.org/bml. xmlns:xsi and xsi:schemaLocation are omitted by default — XSD is
not an officially supported standard feature (doc:DocumentFormat). Legacy schema URIs are
obsolete. BML-semantic xmlns:bml must target ann:BmlAnnotation — never a schema URL.

Branch shape (core:Annotation):
• preferredAlias : Text
• directives : Directive[]
• Directive — name = local name
  · Member (name="*") → Property | Aggregation | Association | Capability
  · Element → Document | Summary | Examples | Example | Value (fixed names)
  · Attribute — fixed names (id, each, with, …)

Concrete annotations:
• org.blockml.bml.annotation.BmlAnnotation (bml) — language directives; see doc:BmlDirectives
• Domain annotations (e.g. com.machineblocks.bml.annotation.ScadAnnotation, scad) — members,
  value facets, prose facets, example facets

Directive match:
• Attribute / Element (incl. fixed Document, Summary, Examples, Example, Value) —
  localName == directive.name
• Member subtypes — name="*"; any local name under the annotation; kind from the Member subtype

Parent context for *:value:
• Direct child of <properties> → Member (Annotation.Property) when declared
• Nested under a property element → Value facet (Annotation.Value) — same property identity,
  not member scad:myProp
Never means a renamed member QName.

Parent context for *:example:
• Prefixed child of <examples> → Annotation.Example (sibling of canonical <example>)
• Unprefixed <example> → StructuralDefinition.Example
Prefer sibling *:example for 1:1 BML↔target pairs; use *:examples for independent target-only
sets. Annotation facets never replace required canonical documentation / value / examples slots.

Property value facets multiply PropertyDefinition.value along the Annotation namespace axis
("" | Annotation FQN). Cross-namespace faceting is valid; same-namespace self-faceting is
forbidden. Duplicate namespace on one property → BML_DUPLICATE_PROPERTY_VALUE. Facets do not
satisfy or replace the canonical <value> for BML instance semantics unless a renderer
explicitly prefers an Annotation facet.

Association-level structural constraint. T binds to the effective
AssociationDefinition. When validation is set, association targets must not reference the
enclosing Block's own type. Reference implementation for AssociationConstraint branch.

Attribute directive bml:bean — registers the instance as a named service bean
for expression access via @beanName.

Attribute directive bml:each — expands the element once per loop iteration
(numeric or collection). See doc:BmlDirectives.

Attribute directive bml:id — instance identity within a composition tree.
Required when the instance is referenced or carries bml:each.

Attribute directive bml:if — includes the element only when the expression
evaluates to true.

Attribute directive bml:scope — "local" or "context" for service bean
visibility. Default local when omitted.

Attribute directive bml:status — shorthand status reference; unqualified
values resolve via org.blockml.bml.status.*.

Attribute directive bml:unless — includes the element only when the expression
evaluates to false. Negation of bml:if.

Attribute directive bml:version — optional exact-version assert when a
composition reference targets an external block type.

Attribute directive bml:with — defines local variables visible within the
element and its descendants. See doc:BmlDirectives.

Attribute or child-element directive bml:generics — binds open genericTypes
on a Block instance. Only on Block instances (composition children and instance aggregation
fill). Value is the parenthesized argument list from a baseType generic application — the
type name is omitted because the instance tag is the type. Parentheses are required.
Attribute form: bml:generics="(type:Integer)". Element form:
<bml:generics>(type:String, myns:MyBlock)</bml:generics>. Arguments are
TypeExpressions in declaration order. Authored args win; remaining parameters take
defaultType. Open generic instance without this directive → BML_OPEN_GENERIC_INSTANCE.
Placement elsewhere → BML_GENERICS_DIRECTIVE_NOT_ALLOWED. Argument list incompatible with
the instance's open parameters → BML_GENERICS_ARGUMENT_MISMATCH. See doc:BmlDirectives
and doc:GenericsModel.

Bare type sites (Property type, Capability inputType/outputType) require ValueTypes. Aggregation type may be any Block FQN. Association type must be InstanceReference(T) or InstanceReference(T)[].
Emitted when a Property or Capability payload type does not resolve to a ValueType branch.

Block definitions describe types. The Definition branch (org.blockml.bml.core.Definition) is the
meta-model for describing block structure in BlockML's own language — definitions are normal
Blocks that inherit from org.blockml.bml.core.Block like everything else.

Definition branch hierarchy:
• org.blockml.bml.core.Definition — abstract base of the Definition branch
• org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition — shared documentation model for structural definitions
• org.blockml.bml.definition.BlockDefinition — shape of every block document
• org.blockml.bml.definition.MemberDefinition — abstract base for block member declarations;
  override and boolean implementation; CapabilityDefinition overrides implementation
• AssociationDefinition — instance-to-instance model links (not documentation References)
• PropertyDefinition, AggregationDefinition, CapabilityDefinition
  (CapabilityDefinition.throws lists Exception types the Capability may raise —
  type:TypeReferenceEntity(core:Exception)[], analogous to a Java method throws clause)
• GenericTypeDefinition

org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition declares:
• Properties: documentation, since, status, abstract, final
• Aggregations: changelog, examples, references
  (References connect types to types or types to instances for documentation —
  distinct from Associations)

Definition addressing uses canonical structural paths within the Block FQN:
com.foo.Bar.properties.width → PropertyDefinition
com.foo.Bar.capabilities.render → CapabilityDefinition
com.foo.Bar.references → Reference entries

Reflection resolves these paths via structural containers at query time — no special
definition-reference syntax. Definition blocks may declare bml:xml for how instances
serialize to canonical BML XML.

Definitions as Blocks means the same parser, TypeRegistry, and validation rules apply.
Domain-specific definition types can extend the branch with additional Capabilities
(validateDefinition(), generateDocumentation()) without core changes.

Block-level <bml:xml> is for core:Block and Definition-branch types. Member bml:xml belongs on Definition-branch member declarations. Hybrid Stage 1/2 checks apply.
Emitted when bml:xml is authored where the grammar/branch does not allow it (e.g. block-level on ordinary ValueType).

Block-level structural constraint. T binds to the effective block definition type.
When validation is set, the validator requires a member with the given local name in the
effective member set of the Block. Reference implementation for BlockConstraint branch.

BlockML describes everything that belongs to a World's grammar as Blocks. There is one root
(org.blockml.bml.core.Block), one parser, and one TypeRegistry bootstrap path — branch-specific
rules come from the baseType chain, not from parallel ontologies.

Everything is a Block means:
• Composable domain types (Wall, StandardBrick, Set) are Blocks
• ValueTypes (Integer, Size3D, Decimal) are Blocks — type definitions, not runtime values
• Languages (TypeScript, OpenSCAD, PseudoCode) are Blocks — capability implementation contracts
• Definition meta-model types (PropertyDefinition, StructuralDefinition sub-blocks) are Blocks
• Documentation blocks (this branch) are Blocks
• Libraries, Services, Constraints, Capabilities, Exceptions — all Blocks

Two layers must be distinguished:
• Authoring ontology (BML / WOT): Block = named definable unit with FQN and baseType chain
• Compiler internals: free representation — plain data, split indexes; no mandatory uniform
  runtime Block class hierarchy

One root · one registry · one parser. ValueTypes never store data — Properties own all concrete
values. The type describes nature; the Property owns the value.

BlockML is a universal declarative language for describing parametric, composable semantic
units called Blocks. BML (Block Markup Language) is the human- and editor-friendly authoring
format; the BOM (Block Object Model) is its canonical, immutable, lossless representation.

The BOM Compiler is domain-agnostic. It understands BML and the BOM object model. Domain-specific
knowledge lives exclusively in Render Targets — MachineBlocks (SCAD) is the reference
implementation, not the only possible World.

Key goals:
• One grammar for types, domain blocks, languages, services, and documentation
• Semantics in BML — behaviour as Capabilities, not compiler special cases
• Lossless BML ↔ BOM — the parser makes no semantic decisions
• Renderer freedom — each target decides how to manifest Blocks in its output
• Self-hosting bootstrap — the compiler loads framework BML before user content

BML file extension is .bml. XML is the sole BML serialization for V1 and V2 — a JSON
authoring form is not planned as an equivalent format. Every Block definition wrapper —
document root, Sub-Block, and embedded Block — identifies the Block by its element tag:
preferred type tag (<acme:MyBlock>) or unqualified name tag (<MyBlock>);
the legacy <block> form remains valid during a long transition (doc:DocumentFormat).
xmlns:xsi and xsi:schemaLocation are omitted by default — XSD is not a standard
validation feature. Withdrawn roots such as device / sign / game stay withdrawn.

BlockML is designed around three core use cases. They build on the same principle:
**information is represented as a structured, semantic model instead of unstructured text or
implementation-specific data.**

## 1. Structured Project Documentation

BlockML can be used as a structured alternative to Markdown for project documentation.

Traditional documentation is primarily written for humans. Markdown improves readability and
portability, but its structure remains largely implicit. BlockML makes that structure explicit
while preserving human-readable content such as Markdown inside documentation blocks.

A BlockML document can therefore serve simultaneously as:

• documentation for humans,
• context for AI systems,
• structured input for software tools,
• and a machine-processable source for generated documentation.

Because BlockML has a defined object model and can be processed by parsers, validators,
compilers, and renderers, documentation is no longer merely text attached to a project. It
becomes part of the project's structured model.

    BML Documentation
          │
          ├──→ Human / AI
          ├──→ Markdown
          ├──→ HTML
          ├──→ BlockDoc
          └──→ other representations

The important distinction is that the generated documentation is not the source of truth.
**The BlockML model is.**

## 2. General-Purpose Domain Modeling

BlockML can describe arbitrary domains.

A domain defines its vocabulary as Blocks, types, properties, relationships, capabilities,
constraints, and compositions. Concrete models can then be expressed using that vocabulary.

BlockML itself does not prescribe what these models represent. They may describe software
systems, infrastructure, IAM configurations, physical objects, user interfaces, business
processes, documentation structures, or entirely new domains.

Renderers interpret these semantic models for a particular target. The same BlockML model may
therefore have multiple manifestations.

    Domain Model
         │
         ▼
        BML
         │
         ├──→ Renderer A → Code
         ├──→ Renderer B → Configuration
         ├──→ Renderer C → Documentation
         ├──→ Renderer D → UI
         └──→ Renderer E → Domain-specific output

The renderer determines the output format and interpretation; the model remains independent of
any particular target. This separation is fundamental to BlockML's renderer architecture.

**BlockML describes what something is. Renderers decide how that description manifests in a
particular environment.**

## 3. AI Workspaces

BlockML can serve as the persistent model of an AI workspace.

Instead of giving an AI a collection of documents and repeatedly asking it to produce new text,
the AI works directly on a structured BlockML model.

The model represents the current state of the work. The AI can inspect it, validate it, extend
it, and transform it while preserving explicit structure and semantics.

This makes it possible to represent not only the final result, but also intermediate states of a
process:

    Initial Model
         │
         ▼
      Analysis
         │
         ▼
    Planning Model
         │
         ▼
    Transformation
         │
         ▼
    Refined Model
         │
         ▼
     Validation
         │
         ▼
     Final Model
         │
         ├──→ Renderer
         ├──→ Compiler
         └──→ further AI transformation

Stages, tasks, decisions, constraints, intermediate results, and final artifacts can all become
explicit parts of the workspace rather than disappearing into prompts and conversation history.

The AI is therefore no longer primarily generating isolated outputs. **It is operating on and
evolving a persistent model.**

This turns BlockML from a representation format into a foundation for model-driven AI workflows:

> **The model is the workspace. The AI works on the model. Renderers manifest its current
> state.**
The three core use cases BlockML is designed around — structured project documentation,
general-purpose domain modeling, and AI workspaces — all built on one principle: information is
represented as a structured semantic model instead of unstructured text.

BlockML knows four ValueType kinds at language level — each names a semantic meaning.
They are sibling branches under ValueType (not subtypes of each other):

PrimitiveType — atomic scalar semantics; no stored values on the type itself.
Examples: Boolean, Integer, Decimal, Float, Text, Color (Text subtype), URL, UUID, Version,
TypeSelector / TypeIdentifier / TypeReference, PackageSelector / PackageIdentifier / PackageReference, InstanceIdentifier /
InstanceReference, MemberIdentifier / PropertyIdentifier / …, Date, Time, DateTime, Duration.
PrimitiveType declares parseValue (Text → bml:Self). The TypeScript return is a host encoding;
outputType is always bml:Self (doc:ValueTypeParsing).

StructType — custom value objects; structure via properties.
Examples: EmptyStruct (no fields; only {}), Size3D, Address, Transform. Parameterized
types (Box(T)) are StructTypes with genericTypes — not a separate branch.

EnumType — closed set of named members; own ValueType branch (not a StructType). Allowed
members live in the values aggregation; BOM stores id + typeFqn only.
Examples: Direction, Face, StudType.

ConstantType — singleton value domain; one configured literal.
Example: Constant(Text){value: "auto"} for union alternatives.

Type expressions combine named types — they are not new BlockML type classes:
• Multiplicity: Integer[], Integer[3], Text[0..n] — postfix on a TypeExpression, so it nests via
  explicit grouping: (Integer[])[] (never Integer[][])
• Unions: Boolean | Integer, Constant(Text){value: "auto"} | Float
• Generic application: Box(Integer) · InstanceReference(core:Block) — round parentheses in type
  attributes; open generic instances bind the same (…) list via bml:generics (doc:GenericsModel)
• Instance configuration: Text{maxLength: 100}, Decimal{precision: 10, scale: 2}
• bml:Self — resolves to effective current Block type after inheritance
• T — generic parameter reference from declaring Block's genericTypes

Assignability follows the branch hierarchy — a value of a subtype is accepted wherever a
supertype is required, with ValueType as the top of the value hierarchy:
Integer <: Number <: PrimitiveType <: ValueType. Date <: Temporal <:
PrimitiveType. Duration is a sibling of Temporal under PrimitiveType — not a Temporal subtype.
A type reference with multiplicity is compatible per element type: Integer[] <: Number[]
<: ValueType[], and each element of a collection is validated independently, so ValueType[]
also accepts mixed element types (doc:TypeExpressions — Collection compatibility · Heterogeneous
collections).

Only ValueTypes may appear where a bare type name is required (Property type,
Capability inputType/outputType). Aggregation type may be any Block FQN. Association type
must be InstanceReference(T) or InstanceReference(T)[] — bare Block FQNs are invalid.
ValueTypes never store data — Properties own all concrete values.

Identifier vs Reference — parseValue on Identifier types checks syntax only. Existence is a
later validator step on Reference types (doc:ValueTypeParsing). The validator keys off the
declared ValueType of the field, never the property or attribute name (type= vs abc= is
irrelevant):
• TypeReference, PropertyReference / AggregationReference / …, and
  InstanceReference — the target must resolve in the current corpus. Unknown TypeReference
  → BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE; unknown PropertyReference → BML_UNKNOWN_PROPERTY (or BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE
  if the owning type cannot be resolved); unknown InstanceReference →
  BML_UNRESOLVABLE_INSTANCE_REF. Unresolved is an error, not proof the document is
  ill-formed — like Java class-not-found, it may be a typo or a missing library.
• TypeIdentifier, MemberIdentifier (PropertyIdentifier / …), and InstanceIdentifier —
  syntax only. Ill-formed → BML_INVALID_TYPE_REFERENCE. An unknown but well-formed name is
  valid.

Blocks may declare <contracts> at root level to compose one or more contract Blocks —
reusable partial definitions whose member fragments merge into the effective Block definition.
Declared only on the document root (not on nested Sub-Blocks). Child elements are direct Block
references (TypeReferenceEntity sugar — empty element is not an instance of the named Block).

baseType vs contracts:
• baseType — framework taxonomy and branch detection (extends); single inheritance; inBranch()
  uses the baseType chain only
• contracts — domain cross-cutting member mixins and type-bound identifiers (implements) via
  satisfiesTypeBound
Framework core branch types (ValueType, Language, Constraint, …) remain baseType markers
only — not duplicated as interface contracts in org.blockml.bml.*.

Semantics:
• Role — reusable partial Block definition (replaces interfaces / traits / mixins) plus type-bound
  identifier
• Scope — Properties, Aggregations, Associations, Capabilities, Constraints, Suggestions,
  documentation, examples, references, optional Capability defaults
• Ignored on contract types — subBlocks, embeddedBlocks, and compositions
• Partial members — contracts may declare incomplete members; the concrete Block completes them
  with override="true" (same rule as baseType refinement) → omission BML_OVERRIDE_REQUIRED
• Merge order — baseType chain → contracts (declaration order) → local Block declarations
• Conflict — later contract wins; Block overrides all contracts
• Override — only explicitly specified attributes replace merged values; final members from any
  layer cannot be overridden → BML_FINAL_MEMBER_OVERRIDE
• Validation — resolveEffectiveMembers() and satisfiesTypeBound() at Stage 2

Type bounds — satisfiesTypeBound(T, G) is true when G is on T's baseType chain OR G appears
directly in T.contracts[] (V1: no transitive closure through a contract's own contracts[]).
Used for generic bounds and polymorphic reference checks. Branch rules (inBranch) ignore
contracts.

Authoring tip: keep contract Blocks abstract with focused member fragments; complete defaults,
constraints, and documentation on the concrete Block with override="true". See
doc:PartialMemberOverrides for merge details and doc:ModelingGuidelines for when to prefer
baseType vs contracts.

BML Directives are attributes and elements in the bml: namespace, formalized by
org.blockml.bml.annotation.BmlAnnotation (preferredAlias bml). Bind with
xmlns:bml="org.blockml.bml.annotation.BmlAnnotation". Directives are not Block properties and not
Definition members. Flow-control directives structure composition; serialization directives
(bml:xml) declare how Definition blocks map to canonical BML XML.

Flow-control follows the Thymeleaf model — attributes on the element they apply to. Whether a
directive is pre-processed at compile time or translated into target constructs is the
BlockProcessor's decision.

Placement:
• bml:id — Block instances; composition identity (literal or ${ expr }); required when
  referenced or on bml:each
• bml:version — Block instances; external type version pin
• bml:bean — Block instances; service bean name for @bean expressions
• bml:scope — Block instances; bean visibility "local" (default) or "context"
• bml:generics — Block instances only; binds open genericTypes. Value is the parenthesized
  argument list from a baseType generic application (parentheses required). Attribute
  bml:generics="(type:Integer)" or child
  <bml:generics>(type:String, myns:MyBlock)</bml:generics>. Open generic
  aggregated without it → BML_OPEN_GENERIC_INSTANCE. Elsewhere →
  BML_GENERICS_DIRECTIVE_NOT_ALLOWED. Incompatible args → BML_GENERICS_ARGUMENT_MISMATCH
• bml:with — composition, bml:container, Block instances; local variable scope
• bml:each — bml:container, Block instances; loop
• bml:if / bml:unless — bml:container, Block instances; conditional include / exclude
• <bml:xml>…</bml:xml> — core:Block and Definition-branch blocks; root XML element recipe
• bml:xml="…" on members — Definition-branch member serialization shape
Bare id= / version= on instances are ordinary member values — use bml:id / bml:version for
composition meta. Do not bind xmlns:bml to a Package or use bml: as a member Annotation prefix.

bml:each — expands the element once per iteration (numeric or collection). Forms:
i : ${ n } · i, stat : ${ n } · item, stat : ${ collection }. Stat fields: index, count, size,
first, last, even, odd (0-based index/even/odd). For numeric loops i equals stat.index.

bml:if / bml:unless — include when expression is true / false respectively.

bml:container — virtual element; produces no Block output; groups children for shared directives
(each, if, with).

bml:with — defines local variables on the element and descendants. Comma-separated assignments;
evaluated left-to-right; later variables may reference earlier ones; shadows outer names of the
same name; may reference Properties of the current Block and override Properties within local
scope. Primary mechanism for sharing values between sibling composition children.

Dynamic instance IDs: combine bml:each with bml:id="${ 'prefix_' + i }" (or equivalent).

bml:generics — instance-only binding of open genericTypes (doc:GenericsModel). Same TypeExpression
grammar as the (…) of a baseType application; the type name is the instance tag, so only the
parenthesized list is authored. Parentheses are required. Not allowed on definitions,
composition wrappers, bml:container, or member declarations. Abstract Blocks remain uninstantiable
even with bml:generics.

bml:xml (serialization — orthogonal to flow control):
• Element form on core:Block / Definition branch: literal local name, ${ bml:Self }, or
  ${ #this.name } only — other recipes → BML_XML_RENDERING_INVALID
• Ordinary composable / ValueType blocks must not redeclare block-level <bml:xml> →
  BML_XML_DIRECTIVE_NOT_ALLOWED (Stage 2)
• Member attribute form selects node kind (element | attribute | text | cdata, including
  element|attribute alternatives). May change on override="true"
Shared XML grammar metadata for serializer, FatBlock, the optional XSD compiler, and
similar targets — not a serializer-private detail. XSD is not a standard feature
(doc:DocumentFormat). Meta-driven emit is WIP; Definition blocks already declare shapes.

Catalogue of directive Sub-Blocks: ann:BmlAnnotation.Id, Version, Bean, Scope, Status, Generics,
Each, If, Unless, With, Xml, Container. Composition usage: doc:CompositionModel.

BML Embedded Expressions are language-neutral Capability references inside a Capability
<implementation> body. Delimiters: opening <$ · closing $>.

The implementation CDATA is source text of the language named by language= (OpenSCAD,
TypeScript, …). Regions wrapped in <$ … $> are BlockML Expression Language fragments. The
renderer replaces each embedded region (including delimiters) with equivalent target-language
syntax; surrounding text is copied unchanged. Embedded Expressions are not a separate
implementation language and not a replacement for <implementation>.

Supported call forms inside embeds (at least):
• #this.someCapability(...) — own Block Capability (required for self-refs; bare foo(...) not
  supported here)
• #math.max(...) / #strings.concat(...) — built-in services (same registry as ${ })
• @bean.someCapability(...) — Transformation Capability on a bound bean

Property access, operators, literals, and nested calls follow the same rules as ${ }
expressions unless noted otherwise. #this is the outer Block instance — the same binding as
${ }; it does not rebind in nested compositions. Bare this is a member (#this.this), not the
instance. Own-Capability calls in embeds still require #this.foo() (doc:Expressions).

Delimiter rules:
• Zero, one, or many regions per implementation body; multiline OK
• Whitespace immediately after <$ and before $> is ignored
• Nested delimiters forbidden
• Unclosed <$ → BML_UNCLOSED_EMBEDDED_EXPRESSION
• Invalid embed content → BML_INVALID_EMBEDDED_EXPRESSION
• Literal <$ or $> in implementation source must not appear outside a valid pair

Contrast with ${ } (member values):
• Host: BML attributes / <value> / directives vs implementation CDATA
• Own Capability: myCapa(...) or link vs #this.myCapa(...) only
• BOM: ExpressionValue.raw on members vs EmbeddedExpression { raw, start, end } on
  ImplementationBlock

See doc:Expressions for ${ } language, layers, V1 scope, and scope rules; doc:SubBlockModel
for utility Sub-Block implementations that commonly host embeds.

BML is semantic XML: framework elements (root, identity fields, member containers, facets) must
highlight differently from user/domain member tags. A HighlightScheme declares those roles and
tag lists as SSOT.

Workflow: edit roles/tags/scopes here (or add another concrete scheme under
org.blockml.bml.vscode.theme.*), point GrammarContribution.highlightScheme at the active
scheme type, then run an LLM render task to update GrammarContribution patterns and
syntaxes/bml.tmLanguage.json. Do not auto-build — regeneration is an explicit LLM / generator
step (see GenerationWorkflow).

Multiple schemes may coexist in the library; only the scheme referenced by the active
GrammarContribution is used when rendering TextMate.
Configurable role → tag → TextMate-scope map for BlockML's semantic XML. Active scheme
on GrammarContribution drives framework tag patterns when the TextMate grammar is re-rendered.

BML TextMate scope colors. Two emission modes (do not combine with a registered theme while
F5-testing: the Extension Development Host auto-applies the first contributed color theme):

• contributeTheme — package.json contributes.themes plus themes/*.json (full editor theme).
  marketplace=true also adds the Themes category. Avoid this for a language extension whose
  users should keep their own color theme.
• overlayTokenColors — contributes.configurationDefaults editor.tokenColorCustomizations
  textMateRules from ColorTheme.tokenColors whose scopes end in .bml. Colors sit on top of
  the user's theme; other languages stay untouched. Skip xml / non-bml scopes.
• overlaySemanticTokenColors — contributes.configurationDefaults
  editor.semanticTokenColorCustomizations.rules from TokenColorRule.semanticTokenType +
  foreground/fontStyle, keyed as type:bml. Needed because semantic tokens do not pick up
  tokenColorCustomizations; without this overlay, LSP tokens stay unstyled and TextMate
  (including rule-stack failures) shows through. Skip rules without semanticTokenType.

Do not invent tokenColors only in JSON — amend theme:ColorTheme / TokenColorRule in BML first,
then re-render.

BOM Core primitive ValueType for a calendar day without a time of day. Unqualified
name Date resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.Date. Extends org.blockml.bml.type.Temporal. Payload
values are stored on Properties — not on the Date type itself.

Authored values use ISO 8601 calendar-date form YYYY-MM-DD (for example 2024-08-29). Date is a
position on the calendar, not an elapsed span — use Duration for lengths of time.

Optional configuration Properties (min, max) configure a Property's owned Date instance via
inline type syntax — Date{min: "2020-01-01", max: "2030-12-31"}. Positional order: min, max.

BOM Core primitive ValueType for a combined date and time of day. Unqualified name
DateTime resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.DateTime. Extends org.blockml.bml.type.Temporal. Payload
values are stored on Properties — not on the DateTime type itself.

Authored values use ISO 8601 combined date-and-time form (for example 2024-08-29T14:30:00,
2024-08-29T14:30:00Z, 2024-08-29T16:30:00+02:00). A trailing Z denotes UTC; a numeric offset
denotes a local civil time with that offset. DateTime is a position on the timeline, not an
elapsed span — use Duration for lengths of time.

Optional configuration Properties (min, max) configure a Property's owned DateTime instance via
inline type syntax — DateTime{min: "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", max: "2024-12-31T23:59:59Z"}.
Positional order: min, max.

BOM Core primitive ValueType for a time of day without a calendar date. Unqualified
name Time resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.Time. Extends org.blockml.bml.type.Temporal. Payload
values are stored on Properties — not on the Time type itself.

Authored values use ISO 8601 time-of-day form HH:MM:SS with optional fractional seconds (for
example 14:30:00, 09:15:30.5). Time is a clock position, not an elapsed span — use Duration for
lengths of time. Timezone offset belongs on DateTime, not on Time.

Optional configuration Properties (min, max) configure a Property's owned Time instance via
inline type syntax — Time{min: "09:00:00", max: "17:00:00"}. Positional order: min, max.

BOM Core primitive ValueType for an elapsed length of time. Unqualified name
Duration resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.Duration. Duration is its own primitive branch under
PrimitiveType — not a Temporal subtype. Temporal types name a position (Date, Time, DateTime);
Duration names a magnitude. Payload values are stored on Properties — not on the Duration type
itself.

Authored values use ISO 8601 duration form PnYnMnDTnHnMnS, with optional week form PnW (for
example P3D, PT1H30M, P1Y2M3DT4H5M6S, P2W). DateTime minus DateTime yields Duration; DateTime
plus Duration yields DateTime.

Duration is not a Number subtype. Calendar components such as years and months do not have a
fixed SI length.

Optional configuration Properties (min, max) configure a Property's owned Duration instance via
inline type syntax — Duration{min: "PT0S", max: "P1Y"}. Positional order: min, max.

BOM Core primitive ValueType for binary floating-point numbers. Not the default
floating-point type — use Decimal unless binary IEEE754 semantics are explicitly required
(GPU, OpenGL, native C APIs, binary protocols). Unqualified name Float resolves to
org.blockml.bml.type.Float. Extends org.blockml.bml.type.Number. Values are stored in Properties.

Generic parameter N (Unit, default unit:None) is forwarded from Number — e.g.
Float(unit:Millimeter). Bare Float is dimensionless.

parseValue accepts a binary-floating literal (same lexical form as Number, including
exponent). NaN and infinities are rejected (doc:ValueTypeParsing).

BOM Core primitive ValueType for decimal numbers — the default type for all
non-integer numeric values (3.5, 12.75, 0.1). Unqualified name Decimal resolves to
org.blockml.bml.type.Decimal. Extends org.blockml.bml.type.Number. Represents mathematical decimal
numbers; the renderer decides target representation (BigDecimal, decimal, number, …).
Payload values are stored on Properties — not on the Decimal type itself.

Generic parameter N (Unit, default unit:None) is forwarded from Number — e.g.
Decimal(unit:Meter). Bare Decimal is dimensionless.

Optional configuration Properties (precision, scale) configure a Property's owned Decimal
instance via inline type syntax — Decimal{precision: 10, scale: 2} or Decimal{10, 2}.
Positional order: precision, scale. See 20_value_type_instance_configuration.md.
precision/scale apply after parseValue (doc:ValueTypeParsing).

BOM Core primitive ValueType for text. Unqualified name Text resolves to
org.blockml.bml.type.Text. Replaces the former String type — BlockML describes semantic types, not
implementation data structures. Renderers may map Text to Java String, TypeScript string,
Python str, C# string, or any target representation.

Semantic subtypes extend Text: TypeSelector / TypeIdentifier / TypeReference, PackageSelector /
PackageIdentifier / PackageReference, InstanceIdentifier / InstanceReference, MemberIdentifier (PropertyIdentifier /
PropertyReference / …), Version, URL, URI, UUID, FilePath, MimeType, …
Concrete payload values are stored on Properties — not on the Text type itself.

Member values of this type may contain restricted ${ } holes in running text
(InterpolatedTextValue). A whole-value "${ expr }" remains an ExpressionValue. See
doc:Expressions.

Optional configuration Properties (minLength, maxLength) configure a Property's owned Text
instance via inline type syntax — Text{maxLength: 100}. Positional order: minLength, maxLength.
See 20_value_type_instance_configuration.md.

BOM Core primitive ValueType for true/false values. Unqualified name Boolean
resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.Boolean. Boolean is neither textual nor numeric — its own
primitive branch. Values are stored in Properties — not on the Boolean type itself.

Authoring accepts case variants of the literals: true / True / TRUE and false / False / FALSE.
Preferred form is lowercase true and false. The BOM always stores the canonical boolean
(lowercase true or false) — never the authored casing.

Sub-Blocks True and False are Constant(Boolean) singletons — use type:Boolean.True /
type:Boolean.False (or Boolean.True / Boolean.False) as named alternatives to
Constant(Boolean){true} / Constant(Boolean){false} in type expressions.

BOM Core primitive ValueType for whole numbers. Unqualified name Integer resolves
to org.blockml.bml.type.Integer. Extends org.blockml.bml.type.Number. Payload values are stored on
Properties — not on the Integer type itself.

Generic parameter N (Unit, default unit:None) is forwarded from Number — e.g.
Integer(unit:Millimeter). Bare Integer is dimensionless.

Optional configuration Properties (min, max) configure a Property's owned Integer instance via
inline type syntax — Integer{min: 0, max: 100}. Positional order: min, max. See
20_value_type_instance_configuration.md. min/max are applied after parseValue
(doc:ValueTypeParsing).

Built-in booleans service. Expression prefix #bools.* — logical and boolean
conversion utilities.

Built-in lists service. Expression prefix #lists.* — list construction,
indexing, and aggregation utilities.

Inputs typed core:ValueType[] are compatible with a collection of any element type, because
collections are compared per element type and every ValueType is assignable to ValueType:
Integer[] <: Number[] <: PrimitiveType[] <: ValueType[], Text[] <: ValueType[]. Elements are
validated independently, so heterogeneous collections such as [1, "text", true] are accepted
here. Capabilities declaring a narrower element type are homogeneous by that element type —
sequence returns Integer[], where [1, "text", 3] would be invalid. Element access (first, last,
get) declares core:ValueType as output — the element type of its core:ValueType[] input; the
concrete ValueType of the returned element follows the list element at runtime.

Multi-argument capabilities use an anonymous StructType whose field types are full
TypeExpressions — { list: core:ValueType[], index: Integer } on get is one anonymous StructType
with a qualified, multiplicity-carrying list field and an unqualified index field. concat takes a
nested multiplicity instead — (core:ValueType[])[], a collection of lists, where every call
argument becomes one element of the outer collection.
See doc:TypeExpressions — Collection compatibility · Heterogeneous collections ·
Nested multiplicities · Anonymous StructTypes.

Built-in math service. Expression prefix #math.* — min, max, abs, floor,
round, and related numeric utilities.

Built-in numbers service. Expression prefix #numbers.* — sequence,
formatting, and numeric conversion utilities.

Built-in strings service. Expression prefix #strings.* — concat, length,
substring, and related text utilities.

C# dialect for Unity script implementations on Capabilities — MonoBehaviour methods,
UnityEngine APIs, and game-logic code. Forwards L on through CSharp (NaturalLanguage, default
English) for the content language of identifiers and comments — bare Unity is
Unity(English).

Capability branch of BlockML. Declares a capability type. Every capability may
carry an implementation whose language attribute references a Language FQN.

The implementation body is not restricted to a compiler-emit template. It may
describe intent (PseudoCode or a natural language), supply a companion template
for a renderer, or be a deterministic function a host toolchain evaluates.
Those readings coexist — doc:CapabilitySemantics.

Exception types a capability may raise are declared on
org.blockml.bml.definition.CapabilityDefinition.throws
(type:TypeReferenceEntity(core:Exception)[]) — not on this branch type.

Capability-level structural constraint. T binds to the effective
CapabilityDefinition. When validation is set, the Capability must declare an implementation
binding on concrete Blocks. Reference implementation for CapabilityConstraint branch.

Child Blocks override inherited members with override="true", or satisfy abstract implementation
obligations with a locally complete override. The flag is required whenever a local member
redeclaration merges with an existing member from the baseType chain or from contracts[] —
contract completion uses the same rule as baseType refinement.

Local declaration properties (never inherited; only effects propagate):
• abstract="true" — incomplete declaration; creates an implementation obligation
• final="true" — seals the declaration; descendants cannot override
• override="true" — confirms deliberate redefinition of an inherited member
Boolean properties require an explicit true or false — empty elements and bare attributes are
invalid. Preferred literals: lowercase true / false.

Modes:
• new — introduces a member; must not set override="true" → else BML_OVERRIDE_WITHOUT_PARENT
• override — refines an inherited member; omit override when merging → BML_OVERRIDE_REQUIRED
Each redeclaration layer must set override="true" again — override is not inherited.

Partial authoring: only the member name, override mode, and changed attributes need to be
specified — all other attributes are inherited from the parent definition. Omit unchanged type
(and other unchanged attributes such as bml:xml or defaults). On aggregations, restating an
identical type when only filling an inherited member → BML_REDUNDANT_AGGREGATION_TYPE (warning
V1). Declare type on an override only when refining or replacing the inherited type.

Abstract → implementation:
• Parent may omit required parts (e.g. property without type or value) when abstract="true"
• Child implements with override="true" and a locally complete declaration (abstract defaults
  to false → locally concrete)
• To keep a member abstract in a child, redeclare with override="true" abstract="true"
• Abstract member left unimplemented on a concrete block → BML_ABSTRACT_MEMBER_NOT_IMPLEMENTED
Capability overrides supply a full implementation child element (not a boolean attribute).

Merge rules (resolveEffectiveMembers — baseType chain → contracts declaration order → local):
• Same member kind required (property overrides property, …)
• Only specified attrs replaced; unspecified attrs inherited
• Override matching key: (resolvedNamespace, normalizedLogicalName) — visibility prefixes
  stripped; xmlns prefix aliases may differ if they resolve to the same namespace
• Visibility may widen (protected → public); narrowing → BML_VISIBILITY_NARROWING
• Member-level bml:xml may change on the same override
• Private members cannot be overridden → BML_FINAL_MEMBER_OVERRIDE
• final="true" on parent prevents override → BML_FINAL_MEMBER_OVERRIDE

readOnly is orthogonal to final / abstract / override: it controls instance authoring only.
• Block definition — may declare and set readOnly members via value, composition, or partial
  override
• Child Block definition — may override an inherited readOnly member (value/composition only;
  cannot override a final member at all)
• Block instance — must not set a member whose effective definition has readOnly=true →
  BML_READONLY_MEMBER_WRITE (after resolveEffectiveMembers on every BlockInstance)
• Expressions — may read readOnly members subject to visibility; renderers may read the BOM
A public readOnly member remains publicly readable. final blocks value overrides entirely;
readOnly does not.

Declared on org.blockml.bml.definition.MemberDefinition (abstract, final, override, readOnly,
visibility) and specialized on PropertyDefinition, AggregationDefinition, AssociationDefinition,
and CapabilityDefinition.

Classifies annotation QNames as aggregation-shaped member directives
(name="*"). Orthogonal to org.blockml.bml.definition.AggregationDefinition.

Classifies annotation QNames as association-shaped member directives
(name="*"). Orthogonal to org.blockml.bml.definition.AssociationDefinition.

Classifies annotation QNames as capability-shaped member directives
(name="*"). Orthogonal to org.blockml.bml.core.Capability and
org.blockml.bml.definition.CapabilityDefinition.

Classifies annotation QNames as property-shaped member directives (name="*").
Orthogonal to org.blockml.bml.definition.PropertyDefinition.

Closed set of BlockML VS Code extension roadmap slices. Contributions declare
milestone V1 or V2 so documentation and generators stay aligned.

Collision checking uses normalizedLogicalName with visibility prefixes stripped. A logical member or Sub-Block exists exactly once with exactly one visibility.
Emitted when members or Sub-Blocks differ only by visibility prefix (myVar / _myVar / __myVar).

Concrete Annotation for BlockML language directives. preferredAlias is bml. Authoring documents
bind xmlns:bml to this FQN. Directives control composition structure, instance identity, generic
binding, service beans, and serialization shape — they are not Block properties and not
Definition members.

Attribute directives: id, version, bean, scope, status, generics, each, if, unless, with, xml.
Element directives: container. Dual authoring (attribute or child element) is documented on
generics and xml.

The legacy schema URI http://blockml.org/schema/bml remains an XSD/catalog identifier only —
BML-semantic xmlns:bml must target this Annotation. XSD is not a standard feature;
xmlns:xsi and xsi:schemaLocation are omitted by default (doc:DocumentFormat).

Concrete HighlightScheme used by bmlSimpleGrammar. Roles map to TextMate scopes by structural
position:

• blockBody — direct children of the document wrapper (identity + block facets). Wrapper is
  legacy <block> or the preferred type/name tag (<acme:MyBlock>, <MyBlock>,
  Sub-Block <Inner> under <subBlocks> / embed under <embeddedBlocks>)
• memberContainer — <properties>, <aggregations>, <associations>, …
• memberContainerBody — direct children = user member names (domainScope)
• memberBody — framework member fields inside a member element
• memberSubContainerBody — composition instances (PascalCase) inside <composition>, etc.

The root role tag list keeps the legacy keyword block. Type-as-tag wrappers cannot be a
closed keyword list — TextMate matches them with the same PascalCase / visibility-underscore
regex as the parser (isDocumentRootLocalName), but only at document top level and inside
subBlocks / embeddedBlocks. PascalCase elsewhere stays domainType or compositionInstance.

Re-render syntaxes/bml.tmLanguage.json after changing scopes or tag lists.
Position-based highlight scheme: block declaration, member container, member name, and
member field scopes are distinct so the same tag local name (e.g. abstract, documentation) colors
differently by XML nesting — not by keyword lists alone.

Concrete Mapping for function-like call syntax. Describes translation between a
function-parameter list and a Capability inputType or outputType.

Two application sites (opposite directions):
1. Expression calls — function syntax → FunctionMapping → Capability inputType
2. Capability implementation — Capability inputType → FunctionMapping → target-language
   function parameters (and reverse for return values)

Canonical call form passes a value matching inputType directly, using JSON-like syntax:
• Primitive → primitive literal
• StructType → object literal
• Collection → array literal

Helper syntax (when supported by this mapping):
• Named parameters — mapped by StructType property names; order irrelevant
• Positional parameters — mapped by property declaration order (mapping config only;
  does not create general StructType index semantics)

Default FunctionMapping (used when no explicit mapping is declared on an implementation):
• Primitive inputType — exactly one positional or named parameter
• StructType inputType — object literal (canonical), named parameters, or positional
  parameters by declaration order
• Primitive collection — positional parameters → array literal
• StructType collection — one outer parameter per struct instance → array literal
• Mixed positional and named arguments — not supported (BML_MIXED_FUNCTION_ARGUMENTS)

Capability implementations that require a target-language function signature must declare an
explicit FunctionMapping child when the default rules are insufficient.

Validation errors: BML_UNKNOWN_FUNCTION_PARAMETER, BML_DUPLICATE_FUNCTION_PARAMETER,
BML_MISSING_FUNCTION_PARAMETER, BML_TOO_MANY_FUNCTION_PARAMETERS,
BML_MIXED_FUNCTION_ARGUMENTS, BML_MISSING_FUNCTION_MAPPING,     BML_AMBIGUOUS_FUNCTION_MAPPING.

Concrete MemberIdentifier binding D = AggregationDefinition. Value is a canonical
aggregation path (com.foo.Bar.aggregations.children) or a local aggregation name when paired
with a type qualifier. Syntax only — the owning type and aggregation need not exist.
AggregationReference extends this type and adds existence. Use when addressing a potential
aggregation. see aggregation= uses AggregationReference. AggregationReference(B) introduces
the owning Block bound after resolution.

Concrete MemberIdentifier binding D = AssociationDefinition. Value is a canonical
association path (com.foo.Bar.associations.basePresets) or a local association name when paired
with a type qualifier. Syntax only — the owning type and association need not exist.
AssociationReference extends this type and adds existence. Use when addressing a potential
association. see association= uses AssociationReference. AssociationReference(B) introduces
the owning Block bound after resolution.

Concrete MemberIdentifier binding D = CapabilityDefinition. Value is a canonical
capability path (com.foo.Bar.capabilities.render) or a local capability name when paired with a
type qualifier. Syntax only — the owning type and capability need not exist.
CapabilityReference extends this type and adds existence. Use when addressing a potential
capability. see capability= uses CapabilityReference. CapabilityReference(B) introduces the
owning Block bound after resolution.

Concrete MemberIdentifier binding D = PropertyDefinition. Value is a canonical
property path (com.foo.Bar.properties.width) or a local property name when paired with a Block
qualifier. Syntax only — the owning type and property need not exist. PropertyReference extends
this type and adds existence. Use when addressing a potential property (planned, generated, or
foreign). see property= uses PropertyReference. PropertyReference(B) introduces the owning
Block bound after resolution.

Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping a Boolean primitive. Binds T = Boolean on
org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.

Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping a CapabilityIdentifier primitive. Binds T =
CapabilityIdentifier on org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value
property automatically. Use when a potential capability path must appear as an identifiable
Block instance. Existence-checked counterparts use CapabilityReferenceEntity.

Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping a Color primitive. Binds T = Color on
org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
Bare Color uses L = English for free-text color names.

Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping a Date primitive. Binds T = Date on
org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
Use when a date must appear as an identifiable Block instance.

Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping a DateTime primitive. Binds T = DateTime on
org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
Use when a date-time must appear as an identifiable Block instance.

Concrete PrimitiveEntity wrapping a Decimal primitive. Binds T = Decimal on
org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.

Constant provides singleton (constant) value domains in type expressions without a dedicated
literal-type language feature. Branch: ConstantType. Standard implementation:
org.blockml.bml.type.Constant.

Surface syntax — Constant(T){value: …}:
• (…) binds generic T to any ValueType (mandatory — bare Constant or Constant{value: …}
  without (T) is invalid)
• {value: …} configures the single allowed literal on the internal ValueType instance

External representation equals the representation of T — Constant(Text){value: "auto"} accepts
the external value "auto", not { value: "auto" }. Validation: first against bound type T, then
equality with the configured constant. No type inference — T is always authored explicitly.

Primary use — union alternatives:
Boolean | Constant(Text){value: "auto"}
Float | Constant(Text){value: "auto"}

Future literal shorthand Boolean | "auto" desugars to the Constant form; until enabled, author
Constant explicitly. Legacy literal unions remain parseable; normalize to Constant at map time.

Boolean.True / Boolean.False — Sub-Blocks of org.blockml.bml.type.Boolean; prefer these shortcuts
over spelling Constant(Boolean){value: true/false} in type expressions.

Obsolete wrappers migrate to Constant unions (doc:TypeExpressions): AutoOr<T> →
Constant(Text){value: "auto"} | T, FalseOr<T> → Boolean.False | T, etc.

Orthogonal mechanisms on one reference: Constant(SizeXY){value: {x: 1, y: 2}} — generic bind +
instance configuration (doc:ValueTypeConfiguration). value is required (ValuePresent).

Constraints are reusable validation rules attached via a single <constraints> container on
ConstrainableDefinition elements (Blocks and members). There is no target= property — the
embedding context binds the constraint automatically. Constraint branches declare genericTypes;
the compiler binds T from context (never authored):
• ValueConstraint on Property → T = effective ValueType
• PropertyConstraint → T = PropertyDefinition
• AggregationConstraint / AssociationConstraint / CapabilityConstraint → corresponding Definition
• BlockConstraint → BlockDefinition (incl. Sub-/Root-)
Wrong branch for context → BML_CONSTRAINT_TARGET_MISMATCH. Unknown constraint type →
BML_CONSTRAINT_UNKNOWN. Generic T incompatible → BML_CONSTRAINT_TYPE_MISMATCH. Instance property
incompatible with T → BML_CONSTRAINT_VALUE_MISMATCH.

Validation property (optional) references org.blockml.bml.validation.*:
• Error → BML_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION (fail compile)
• Warning → BML_CONSTRAINT_WARNING
• Information → BML_CONSTRAINT_INFORMATION
Omitted validation → constraint is metadata only (not value-enforced by the BlockML validator).

Standard value constraints include Min, Max, MinLength, MaxLength, MinItems, MaxItems, Pattern,
ValuePresent. Structural examples: RequiresMember, AllowedChildType, NoSelfReference,
MustBeReadOnly, RequiresImplementation.     Prefer ValueType instance configuration for
type-intrinsic thresholds (Text{maxLength: 100}); keep Constraints for contextual/composable
rules (doc:ValueTypeConfiguration). Both run after PrimitiveType.parseValue accepts the
authored text (doc:ValueTypeParsing).

Suggestions — Property-only metadata: Block instances compatible with the property type for
editors/renderers. Not validation. Forbidden on EnumType properties → BML_SUGGESTIONS_ON_ENUM.
Incompatible suggestion instance → BML_SUGGESTION_TYPE_MISMATCH (PrimitiveType properties use
matching *Entity wrappers).

Procedure: task:AddConstraint.

Contribution → generator mapping:
• LanguageContribution → contributes.languages + language-configuration.json (comments,
  brackets, autoClosingPairs, surroundingPairs from CharacterPair aggregations). When
  xmlLanguageParticipant is true, also contributes.xmlLanguageParticipants[{ languageId }]
  so vscode-xml keeps applying XSD (xsi:schemaLocation) after .bml is claimed as language bml
• GrammarContribution → contributes.grammars + syntaxes/*.tmLanguage.json (from structured
  GrammarPattern children, topLevelIncludes, and scopes). When highlightScheme is set,
  framework tag patterns must follow that HighlightScheme's roles/tags/scopes.
• HighlightScheme / HighlightRole (org.blockml.bml.vscode.theme.*) → SSOT for semantic
  framework-tag coloring; not a package.json contribution by itself — consumed when rendering
  GrammarContribution / tmLanguage
• IconContribution → when contributeLanguageIcon is true, contributes.languages[].icon
  { light, dark } from iconPath / iconPathDark. When contributeIconTheme is true, also
  contributes.iconThemes + icon theme JSON (themeId / themeLabel / themePath). Do not
  register an icon theme while F5-testing a language extension: the Development Host
  auto-applies the first contributed file icon theme.
• ColorThemeContribution → when contributeTheme is true, contributes.themes + themes/*.json
  (marketplace=true adds the Themes category). When overlayTokenColors is true, also
  configurationDefaults editor.tokenColorCustomizations.textMateRules for *.bml scopes so
  colors sit on the user's theme. When overlaySemanticTokenColors is true, also
  configurationDefaults editor.semanticTokenColorCustomizations.rules from
  TokenColorRule.semanticTokenType (keys type:bml) so LSP / client semantic tokens get the
  same colors — tokenColorCustomizations does not style semantic tokens. Do not register a
  color theme while F5-testing: the Development Host auto-applies the first contributed
  color theme.
• ConfigurationContribution / Setting → contributes.configuration (SSOT for all settings)
• CommandContribution → contributes.commands
• KeybindingContribution → contributes.keybindings
• LanguageServerContribution → vscode-languageclient bootstrap (not a package.json key alone)
• NavigationContribution → LSP definition/references expectations + optional client providers
• SemanticHighlightingContribution → semantic token legend
  (contributes.semanticTokenTypes / semanticTokenScopes) plus a client
  DocumentSemanticTokensProvider that runs the @blockml/lsp classifier locally. LSP
  semanticTokens remain advertised; colors come from overlaySemanticTokenColors.
• MarketplaceListing → README.md (Marketplace / Open VSX page body). CHANGELOG.md is the
  changelog tab. Distinct from vscode:README (library reading entry).

Settings must not be invented only in TypeScript — add a Setting under ConfigurationContribution
first, then generate accessors from BML. Language-config and grammar regexes must not be
invented only in JSON — amend LanguageContribution / GrammarPattern in BML first. Framework
tag lists and role scopes must not be invented only in JSON — amend HighlightScheme first, then
re-render GrammarPatterns + tmLanguage via LLM. Token colors must not be invented only in
themes/*.json — amend theme:ColorTheme / TokenColorRule in BML first, then re-render.

Curly braces configure the Property's owned ValueType instance — orthogonal to generic (...)
binding. The configuration applies to the type instance associated with a Property, not to
the ValueType definition block itself. Both may coexist: Box(Integer){minItems: 1}.
Multiplicity brackets apply after configuration: Text{maxLength: 50}[0..n].

Syntax examples:
• Text{maxLength: 100} — named configuration property (JSON-like key: value)
• Decimal{precision: 10, scale: 2} — named precision and scale
• Decimal{10, 2} — positional by ValueType property declaration order (precision, scale)
• Constant(SizeXY){value: {x: 1, y: 2}} — nested object literals for StructType config values

Rules:
• Named and positional configuration must not be mixed in one {...} block →
  BML_MIXED_TYPE_CONFIGURATION
• Positional mapping follows declaration order — same principle as FunctionMapping
• Do not use key=value inside {...} (that is expression call syntax, not type configuration)
• Unknown config property → BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE_CONFIGURATION; value mismatch →
  BML_TYPE_CONFIGURATION_VIOLATION
• Generic application uses round parentheses: Box(Integer), TypeReference(core:Block)
• Constant(T){value: …} — generic (...) binds T; {value: …} supplies the singleton literal

Prefer multiplicity on the type reference for collection bounds (Text[1..10]) over List{…}
wrappers. Prefer inline configuration for type-intrinsic thresholds (Text{maxLength: 100});
keep Constraints for contextual/composable/business rules (Pattern, cross-property, …).

Configuration runs after PrimitiveType.parseValue accepts the authored text
(doc:ValueTypeParsing). parseValue does not read min / max / maxLength — those stay on the
Property's owned type instance.

ValueType definitions declare configuration Properties on the type block (e.g. precision and
scale on Decimal). Values live on Properties of Block instances — never on the ValueType
definition. There is no new Integer(5) in BlockML; the Property owns value 5 with type Integer.

Decimal is the default for non-integer numerics (3.5, 12.75). Float is special-purpose only
when binary floating-point semantics are explicitly required.

Declare xmlns:prefix for Packages (type addressing) or Annotations (directives/facets). Prefixes are authoring aliases — BOM stores canonical FQNs/namespaces.
Emitted when a QName uses an xmlns prefix that is not declared on the document.

Declared in BML but not yet fully implemented, validated, or mapped. May change
without deprecation notice. Use when a known gap exists between target and canonical form —

Declares a language id, aliases, extensions, filenames, configuration path, and the semantic
contents of language-configuration.json (comments, brackets, autoClosingPairs,
