Declares one generic type parameter on a root Block definition. Rendered inside
the genericTypes container as an element whose local name is the parameter identifier (root
block only). Maps to BOM GenericType { name, baseType, defaultType? } — name is derived from
the XML element name, not from a child or attribute. The name is substituted in type references
within this Block (e.g. type="T" → GenericParameterReference). baseType is the FQN constraint —
each concrete type argument at reference sites (type applications and instance bml:generics)
must inherit from that branch (BML_GENERIC_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION on mismatch). Optional
defaultType supplies the binding when a generic application or bml:generics omits the
corresponding type argument: a concrete TypeExpression, or the name of an earlier sibling
generic parameter (declaration-order only; cycles and forward references forbidden). Must
satisfy baseType after resolution. See 17_type_system_bml.md — defaultType. Optional
documentation on the entry describes the parameter itself (not the enclosing Block). Parameter
name must differ from the Block name and every Sub-Block name.

Default relation when relation is omitted on <see>. Use for related Blocks,
documentation files, or URLs that help understand the current definition but do not extend,
require, or define it. Omitted relation= on <see> resolves to this block.

Defaults: RootBlockDefinition, SubBlockDefinition, EmbeddedBlockDefinition. Unqualified names resolve via org.blockml.bml.definition.*.
Emitted when the definition meta-model type is incompatible with the block role (root / Sub-Block / embedded).

Definition authoring and child definition overrides may set readOnly member values/composition; instances must not. Expressions may still read subject to visibility.
Emitted when a Block instance sets a member whose effective definition has readOnly=true.

Describes a Block member defining how the Block communicates. Rendered as a child
element inside the capabilities container; the XML element name is the capability name
(bml:xml="${ #this.name }"). An optional XML prefix on the element name supplies the member
namespace — resolved via xmlns to BOM namespace; unprefixed elements use the default namespace
(empty string). Member identity is (resolvedNamespace, localName).

Maps to BOM CapabilityDefinition (kind: "capability") with typeFqn, inputType, outputType,
optional throws, and optional implementation binding. Inbound requires inputType; Outbound
requires outputType; Transformation requires both; Action requires neither. inputType and
outputType use TypeExpression syntax and must resolve to ValueTypes.

throws lists Exception types this Capability may raise — the BlockML equivalent of a Java
method throws clause (type:TypeReferenceEntity(core:Exception)[]).

Scalar capability fields (type, inputType, outputType) follow
org.blockml.bml.definition.MemberDefinition placement rules — element preferred on definitions,
attribute preferred on Block instances. Structured implementation remains a child element;
throws is an aggregation of TypeReferenceEntity children.

Describes a Block member representing an owned collection. Children are always
Block instances; the aggregation type attribute selects the payload type:

• Plain Block type (for example core:Block[], bricks:Brick[]) — composition ownership of those
  Block types. Children are Block instances: member values, nested aggregations filled without
  a composition wrapper, and bml:id. A child whose type still has open genericTypes after
  inheritance must bind them with bml:generics (attribute or child element; parenthesized
  TypeExpression list). Missing → BML_OPEN_GENERIC_INSTANCE. See doc:GenericsModel.
• TypeReferenceEntity application (for example type:TypeReferenceEntity(core:Block)[]) —
  owned TypeReferenceEntity instances whose value holds an FQN / TypeExpression. Empty children
  whose element QName is not TypeReferenceEntity are syntactic sugar for
  <type:TypeReferenceEntity value="…QName…" /> (B/D bound by the aggregation type).

Rendered as a child element inside the aggregations container; the XML element name is the
aggregation name (bml:xml="${ #this.name }"). An optional XML prefix on the element name supplies
the member namespace — resolved via xmlns to BOM namespace; unprefixed elements use the default
namespace (empty string). Member identity is (resolvedNamespace, localName). Maps to BOM
AggregationDefinition (kind: "aggregation") with type expression, cardinality (from type
multiplicity), and optional nested composition template. There is no default aggregation —
on Block instances the aggregation member element must always be opened by name; bare child
Block instances directly under the parent instance are invalid. Standalone composition is
never allowed — <composition> must be nested inside the aggregation member
(BML_STANDALONE_COMPOSITION). Scalar member field (type) follows
org.blockml.bml.definition.MemberDefinition placement rules — element preferred on aggregation
declarations. Structured composition remains a child element.
Composition instance ID reachability for bml:id references is controlled by this aggregation
member's visibility (inherited from org.blockml.bml.definition.MemberDefinition) — public
aggregations export ids for cross-document {EnclosingBlockFQN}::{id} references; protected
limits reach to the declaring Block and its child Blocks; private limits reach to the declaring
Block only. Service binding on composition children uses bml:bean and bml:scope on Block
instances — not aggregation member fields. Open generic children use bml:generics on the
instance — not aggregation member fields.

Describes a Block member that carries a scalar or structured value. Rendered as a
child element inside the properties container; the XML element name is the property name
(bml:xml="${ #this.name }"). An optional XML prefix on the element name supplies the member
namespace — for example ui5:width resolves via xmlns:ui5 to the canonical namespace stored in
BOM namespace; unprefixed elements belong to the default namespace (empty string). The prefix
itself is never stored. Member identity is (resolvedNamespace, localName). Maps to BOM
PropertyDefinition (kind: "property") with typeFqn, values[] (value-field entries with
namespace), optional groups (inherited from MemberDefinition), and optional constraints (via
ConstrainableDefinition) and suggestions. Convenience path value is the default-namespace entry.
Property type must resolve to a ValueType branch. Scalar member fields (type, value) follow
org.blockml.bml.definition.MemberDefinition placement rules on the PropertyDefinition
declaration — element preferred on definitions. The value field is definition syntax only;
it is not a wrapper around a Property assignment on a domain Block instance. On instances the
Property is a Block attribute or the Property element's direct content
(myProperty="…" / <myProperty>…</myProperty>) — see doc:MemberAuthoring. Structured
children (groups, suggestions) remain elements. Every Property behaves as Optional — it has a
value or has no value; there is no null. Declaration order among properties is significant for
StructType positional mapping and Capability parameter order.

Value-field Annotation facets: nested under this property element, an Annotation-prefixed
value element (e.g. scad:value from Annotation.Value) multiplies the value field along the
Annotation namespace axis — same property identity, not a member QName and not scad:myProp.
Parent context disambiguates from top-level <properties><scad:value/> members.
See doc:AnnotationModel — Property value facets.

Describes a Block member that connects instances to instances — non-owning model
links between concrete Block instances, without lifecycle ownership. Distinct from documentation
References (<see> on StructuralDefinition.references), which connect types to types or
types to instances for documentation only. Rendered as a child element inside the associations
container; the XML element name is the association name (bml:xml="${ #this.name }"). An optional
XML prefix on the element name supplies the member namespace — resolved via xmlns to BOM
namespace; unprefixed elements use the default namespace (empty string). Member identity is
(resolvedNamespace, localName). Maps to BOM AssociationDefinition (kind: "association") with
type (InstanceReference TypeExpression) and cardinality (from type multiplicity). Association
type must be InstanceReference(T) or InstanceReference(T)[] with T extending core:Block — bare
Block FQNs (e.g. core:Block, bml:Self[]) are invalid. Instance values are authored on Block
instances as member attributes or elements (space-separated InstanceReference tokens, or
expressions). Associations do not own composition children. Scalar member field type follows
org.blockml.bml.definition.MemberDefinition placement rules — element preferred on definitions,
attribute preferred on Block instances. Domain examples include basePresets on MachineBlocks
Block types (type InstanceReference(bml:Self)[]).

Describes a single changelog entry in a changelog container on any definition
element (block, property, aggregation, …). Rendered as a change element with a required
version attribute and a trimmed text body describing what changed. Maps to BOM
ChangelogEntry { version, text, languageFqn? }. Entries must be ordered chronologically by
version — oldest first (BML_CHANGELOG_VERSION_ORDER when out of order). Optional language
attribute overrides the effective natural language for this entry's text body.

Describes how the extension hosts or connects to a BlockML LSP. Generators emit
vscode-languageclient bootstrap code from this Block. Does not implement the server itself —
it specifies client wiring and expected server capabilities the extension relies on.
V2 integration of a BlockML Language Server — transport, document selectors, middleware
notes, and feature flags for diagnostics, completion, and hover.

Describes one documentation prose entry on any
org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition (block, property, aggregation, …). Rendered
as a documentation element (optionally QName-prefixed for Annotation facets) with optional language
attribute and a trimmed text body. The body is Markdown(English) by default — see the
language and content properties for the content model and the CDATA serialization rules.
Authors may place multiple siblings: i18n via language=
(Markdown(NaturalLanguage) or a bare NaturalLanguage); facets via annotation element namespace
(e.g. scad:document from
Annotation.Document). Facet namespaces are Annotations, not locales. Maps to BOM documentations[] DocumentationProseEntry
{ namespace, text, languageFqn }. Identity (namespace, languageFqn) within documentations[] —
duplicate → BML_DUPLICATE_DOCUMENTATION. Declared as a repeatable property shape on
org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition.

Describes one usage example in an examples container on any definition element
(block, property, aggregation, …). Rendered as an example element with a required title
attribute and a character-data body (bml:xml="text" — Text node or CDATA equally valid;
serializer chooses CDATA vs text per escape policy, 19 D8). The enclosing container may be
default-namespace <examples> or an Annotation facet (e.g. scad:examples). Paired
target-language samples use Annotation.Example as a sibling under the same <examples>
(e.g. scad:example with matching title) — preferred over a parallel scad:examples container.
Maps to BOM DocumentationExample { title, content, contentLanguageFqn?, namespace?, snippet }.
Empty body → BML_EXAMPLE_EMPTY_BODY. The title is always written in the effective natural
language of the enclosing block definition. An optional language attribute on the example
element references a Language FQN — implementation languages (OpenSCAD, TypeScript, …) for
code samples, or NaturalLanguage (English, German, …) for prose bodies. Optional snippet
marks illustrative fragments that are not complete / not to be syntax-checked.

Describes the BML file icon for the explorer and editor tabs. Two independent VS Code
contributions may be emitted from the same iconPath:

• Language mode icon — contributes.languages[].icon (light/dark). Works with whatever file
  icon theme the user has selected (Seti, Material, …); other file types keep their icons.
• File icon theme — contributes.iconThemes (themeId, themeLabel, themePath). A full theme
  that only maps .bml and replaces other themes. Do not emit this while developing a
  language extension: the Extension Development Host (F5) auto-applies the first file
  icon theme from the extension under development (ConfigurationTarget.MEMORY), even if
  the user never selected it. Language mode icons do not trigger that.

Generators emit the icon theme JSON that maps fileExtension / languageId to iconPath. For
the BlockML extension, the filetype icon asset is icons/blockml.svg at the repository root.

Do not confuse with Extension.icon (icons/blockml.png) — that large PNG is the Marketplace
gallery image in package.json, not the editor filetype glyph.

Describes the composition element on an aggregation member declaration only.
Rendered as composition with optional bml:with directives and a tree of composition child
nodes (Block instances and bml:container virtual containers). Not an instance wrapper —
nested Block instances in this tree fill their own aggregations directly, without a nested
composition element. Maps to BOM
CompositionTemplate { aggregationName (from enclosing aggregation member name), directives,
children }. Instance ID reachability is determined by the enclosing aggregation member's
visibility — not by attributes on the composition element. Standalone composition outside an
aggregation member element is invalid (BML_STANDALONE_COMPOSITION). Declared as the
composition property on org.blockml.bml.definition.AggregationDefinition.

Describes the implementation element on a capability member. Rendered as
implementation with a required language attribute referencing org.blockml.bml.language.*
and a CDATA source body. Maps to BOM ImplementationBlock { languageFqn, source,
embeddedExpressions }. Not a ValueType — structured metadata on the Capability member
(an ordinary Block Sub-Block). The
body may be intent, a companion template, or a host-evaluable function
(doc:CapabilitySemantics). Capability references inside the body use BML Embedded
Expression syntax (<$ … $>). Declared as the implementation property on
org.blockml.bml.definition.CapabilityDefinition.

Directive that appears as an XML element under the annotation namespace

Every Block definition wrapper is identified by its element tag: the document root, each
Sub-Block under `<subBlocks>`, and each embedded Block under `<embeddedBlocks>`. Two
authoring formats are valid during a long transition. The type-or-name-as-tag form is the
intended long-term format; the legacy `<block>` wrapper remains valid until it is withdrawn.

Existing sources in this library stay in the legacy form until they are migrated.

Member containers (`<properties>`, `<aggregations>`, …) and instance children are unchanged.
Instance serialization already uses the declared type tag (`<core:Block>`, `<myns:Wall>`).

## Qualified Blocks — document root and embedded Blocks

Legacy:

    <block>
      <name>MyBlock</name>  <!-- optional -->
      <type>acme:MyBlock</type>
      …
    </block>

Preferred:

    <acme:MyBlock>
      <name>MyBlock</name>  <!-- optional -->
      …
    </acme:MyBlock>

The element QName is the type. Prefixes resolve via xmlns Package bindings
(doc:BmlNamespace). Child `<type>` is omitted when the tag already supplies the type.
Optional `<name>` must still equal `lastSegment(resolve(type))` when present
(BML_BLOCK_NAME_TYPE_MISMATCH).

Embedded Blocks use this same authoring as the document root. Their identity is still an
independent FQN — `resolve(type)`, not nested under the root (doc:SubBlockModel).

## Unqualified Blocks — document root, Sub-Blocks, and optional embeds

Legacy:

    <block>
      <name>MyBlock</name>
      …
    </block>

Preferred:

    <MyBlock>
      <name>MyBlock</name>  <!-- optional, not recommended -->
      …
    </MyBlock>

The local name of the element is the type (and the effective name). A redundant `<name>`
is allowed but not recommended. Unqualified roots and embeds follow the same identity rules
as unqualified type references (doc:TypeIdentityDerivation / doc:ImplicitNamespaceResolution).
Embeds still require a fully qualified resolved FQN
(BML_UNQUALIFIED_EMBEDDED_BLOCK_TYPE) — prefer the qualified tag.

## Sub-Blocks — unqualified name as the element

Sub-Blocks always use the unqualified form. The element local name *is* the Sub-Block name.
Type stays derived as `resolve(parent.type) + "." + name` (doc:TypeIdentityDerivation).

Legacy:

    <subBlocks>
      <block>
        <name>MyBlock</name>
        …
      </block>
    </subBlocks>

Preferred:

    <subBlocks>
      <MyBlock>
        <!-- <name>MyBlock</name> is optional and not recommended -->
        …
      </MyBlock>
    </subBlocks>

Child `<name>` may still be authored and must equal the element local name when present
(BML_BLOCK_NAME_TYPE_MISMATCH). BML_MISSING_SUBBLOCK_NAME when neither the element tag nor
`<name>` supplies the name (legacy `<block>` without `<name>`). Visibility prefixes stay on
the logical name and therefore on the tag (`<_Utils>`, `<__Helper>`). Nested Sub-Blocks use
the same rule at every depth.

## Dual format

Parser, validator, and LSP accept both forms on the root, on Sub-Blocks, and on embeds.
New documents should use the type-or-name-as-tag form. Both remain valid until the legacy
form is withdrawn.

Identity rules (doc:TypeIdentityDerivation):

• Root and embed — type is required as canonical identity: the element tag and/or child
  `<type>`. BML_MISSING_BLOCK_TYPE / BML_MISSING_EMBEDDED_BLOCK_TYPE when neither supplies
  a type. When both supply a type, they must resolve to the same FQN.
• Sub-Block — name is required as local identity: the element tag and/or child `<name>`.
  Type is normally omitted and derived. When `<type>` is present it must equal
  `parentType + "." + name`.
• A generic `<block>` wrapper is not itself a type or name. In the legacy form, identity
  comes from `<type>` / `<name>`. In the preferred form the element tag *is* that identity.

## XSD is not a standard feature

`xmlns:xsi` and `xsi:schemaLocation` are omitted by default. XML Schema is not an officially
supported standard feature. The XSD compiler remains available; it is not used by default.
Semantic validation is the validator and the LSP.

Default `xmlns="http://blockml.org/bml"` and BML-semantic prefixes stay. Other URI bindings
(schemaLocation keys) are not BML-semantic type namespaces (doc:BmlNamespace).
`Library.schemas` remains an optional legacy catalog of XSD paths during migration
(doc:LibrarySystem).
Every Block definition wrapper — document root, Sub-Block, and embedded Block — uses
the type or name as its element tag. Legacy <block> remains valid during a long
transition. xmlns:xsi and xsi:schemaLocation are omitted by default — validation is the
validator and LSP, not XSD.

Every BML definition — Blocks, Libraries, Types, Languages, Services, Capabilities, and all
other BlockML definitions — must reside below the owning domain's bml package.

General form:
• <domain>.bml.*

Examples:
• org.blockml.bml.*
• com.machineblocks.bml.*
• com.example.bml.*

No BML Block, Library, or other BlockML definition may exist outside the domain's bml
namespace (BML_OUTSIDE_BML_NAMESPACE). Physical source layout mirrors the FQN:
blocks/org/blockml/bml/core/Block.bml defines org.blockml.bml.core.Block.

Typical BlockML branches (all under org.blockml.bml.*):
• org.blockml.bml.core.* — framework base types (Block, Annotation, ValueType, Status, Capability, Exception, Library, …)
• org.blockml.bml.annotation.* — concrete Annotations (BmlAnnotation)
• org.blockml.bml.type.* — bootstrap ValueTypes
• org.blockml.bml.service.* — built-in expression services (#math, #strings, …)
• org.blockml.bml.language.* — implementation language types
• org.blockml.bml.capability.* — Capability type branches
• org.blockml.bml.definition.* — Definition meta-model (orthogonal to Annotations)
• org.blockml.bml.documentation.* — bootstrap documentation blocks
• org.blockml.bml.status.* / constraint.* / validation.* / relation.* / unit.* — matching branches

xmlns prefixes are BML-semantic only when they target a Package or an Annotation:
• Package — type addressing (xmlns:core="org.blockml.bml.core")
• Annotation — directives (xmlns:bml="org.blockml.bml.annotation.BmlAnnotation")
Other URI bindings (schemaLocation keys) are not BML-semantic type namespaces.
xmlns:xsi and xsi:schemaLocation are omitted by default — XSD is not a standard
feature (doc:DocumentFormat). Undeclared
prefix → BML_UNKNOWN_NAMESPACE_PREFIX; non-Package/Annotation target →
BML_INVALID_NAMESPACE_TARGET; colliding prefixes across a bundle →
BML_NAMESPACE_PREFIX_COLLISION.

XML prefix convention (required authoring practice — BOM stores FQNs; compiler does not
rewrite aliases). Rule of thumb: a bare short prefix always means BlockML. Domain mirrors of
the same segment use a domain token in front (MachineBlocks → mb):
• core → org.blockml.bml.core · type → org.blockml.bml.type · unit → org.blockml.bml.unit
• lang → org.blockml.bml.language · status / def / constraint / validation / … → matching
  org.blockml.bml.*
• mbcore → com.machineblocks.bml.core · mbt → …type · mbunit → …unit
• bricks / cal / scad — collective or annotation packages (descriptive OK when no collision)
Do not steal framework aliases (xmlns:core="com.machineblocks.bml.core" is wrong). Do not use
legacy bcore / btype. Other domains use their own short token (ac → acore / atype / aunit).

Member and facet QNames: optional XML prefix on member element names supplies the member
namespace (resolved via xmlns; unprefixed → default empty namespace). Prefixed member QNames
that are Annotation Member directives (name="*") resolve to that Annotation — see
doc:AnnotationModel. There is no namespace= attribute on members.

Domain libraries follow the same <domain>.bml.* rule
(com.machineblocks.bml.core / bricks / type / annotation.*, …).

npm workspace packages (@blockml/core, @blockml/parser, …) are deployment units — not
identical to FQN namespaces. TypeScript toolchain code ships in package src/ directories;
it is not a BML definition and does not receive a domain.bml FQN.

Every redeclaration layer that merges with an inherited or contract member must set override="true" again — including contract completion. Override is not inherited.
Emitted when a local member redeclaration merges with a baseType or contracts member without override="true".

Every root block definition carries a documentation model at the definition site — single
source of truth inside BML files:

Definition identity first (required at top of every Block document):
name / type / baseType — FQN identity before prose (baseType omitted only on org.blockml.bml.core.Block).
Preferred: the element tag supplies type on the document root and on embeds, and name
on Sub-Blocks (doc:DocumentFormat); <type> / <name> remain valid in the legacy
<block> form.

is (always required, after identity) — names the Idea (Urbild): what this Block semantically
  represents. Noun phrase; several words when name/type alone is too thin — not purpose and not
  full technical detail. Urbild is a fixed BlockML term (keep German explicit in meta-prose):
  English/French gloss + (Urbild); German docs may use Urbild alone. WOT: the Block itself is
  the Idea (Urbild); <is> names it in prose. Reflection: bml:Self.is. Omitted →
  BML_MISSING_IS. Motto: as simple as Lego at the designation; as powerful as SAP beneath.
summary (required when documentation is too long) — short prose expansion between is and
  documentation; inherited from StructuralDefinition on blocks and members. Missing when
  required → BML_MISSING_SUMMARY.
keywords aggregation (optional) — meta.Keyword[]; ad-hoc Keyword instances or domain FixedKeyword catalogue blocks; comma shorthand → Keyword only.
language (optional Definition meta — def:BlockDefinition.language) — natural language for
  documentation prose; inherits enclosing Library document language, then the English default
  authored on org.blockml.bml.core.Block.
documentation (always required on every Block definition) — technical description of the Block
  definition itself; Markdown(English) by default, with an optional language attribute
  (Markdown(NaturalLanguage) or a bare NaturalLanguage) when prose deviates from the effective
  block language. Omitted → BML_MISSING_DOCUMENTATION.
isNot (required when confusion risk exists, blocks only) — what this Block is not; block-level
  disambiguation. Reflection: bml:Self.isNot. Missing when required → BML_MISSING_IS_NOT.
aliases aggregation (optional, blocks only) — meta.Alias[]; ad-hoc Alias instances or domain FixedAlias catalogue blocks; comma shorthand → Alias only.
Member elements carry their own summary, keywords, and documentation for individual Properties, Aggregations, etc.

Optional extensions (wherever documentation is permitted):
since — version from which the element is available
changelog — container of change entries (oldest first)
examples — container of example entries (title in block natural language + CDATA body)
references — container of see entries (type, instance, file, url, or member path + relationship text)

Natural language inheritance (documentation prose and example titles) — Definition meta only,
not a core:Block / BlockLibrary member:
Library document <language> → Block document <language> → documentation / change / see
language attribute. Unqualified names inside <language> and on documentation, change, and
see language= resolve via org.blockml.bml.language.*. On documentation the natural language is
either the generic argument of Markdown (Markdown(German)) or the bare shorthand (German); on
change and see language= it is always the NaturalLanguage itself, since those bodies carry no
markup. Authors declare language only when deviating from the effective inherited language. Example title language always follows the
enclosing block — example language attribute applies to CDATA content only (implementation
dialect: OpenSCAD, TypeScript, …) and also resolves via org.blockml.bml.language.*.

## Documentation, Summary, Markdown and CDATA

`summary` and `documentation` serve different purposes and therefore use different content
models:

    summary         → plain text
    documentation   → Markdown(English) by default

### Summary

`summary` is a short, presentation-independent description for contexts such as lists, search
results, explorers, tooltips, and IDE tooling. It is **plain text** and does not support
Markdown:

    <summary>A generic block for describing a reusable component.</summary>

### Documentation

`documentation` is rich textual content and uses Markdown by default. The default is declared by
the documentation definition itself as `Markdown(English)`
(def:StructuralDefinition.Documentation.language), so authors normally **do not** write the
`language` attribute:

    <documentation>
    A **Block** is the fundamental unit of BlockML.
    </documentation>

is semantically equivalent to:

    <documentation language="Markdown(English)">
    A **Block** is the fundamental unit of BlockML.
    </documentation>

The explicit `language` attribute is only necessary when overriding the default. It is bound to
`Markdown(NaturalLanguage) | NaturalLanguage`: `Markdown` forwards `MarkupLanguage.L`
(NaturalLanguage, default English), so the natural language travels as the generic argument —
`language="Markdown(German)"` for German prose, `language="Markdown"` being the same as
`Markdown(English)`. A bare natural language stays valid as shorthand: `language="German"` means
`Markdown(German)`. Both forms denote the same i18n entry, so do not author them side by side on
one definition element.

### CDATA usage

Markdown itself does **not** require CDATA. CDATA is purely an XML serialization mechanism and
has no semantic meaning for documentation. The serialization rule is:

    no XML escaping required   → ordinary XML text
    XML escaping required      → prefer CDATA over entity escaping

Documentation should be ordinary XML text when nothing needs escaping. When the content contains
characters that would require escaping — especially `<` and `&` — the body is wrapped in a
`<![CDATA[` … section, because that keeps the authored Markdown readable. Preferred payload:

    Returns `true` when `value < maximum && enabled`.

Avoid entity escaping when CDATA can preserve the original content verbatim — the same payload
written as `value < maximum && enabled` is the form to avoid. This block itself is
serialized as CDATA for exactly that reason.

### CDATA terminators inside CDATA

XML CDATA sections cannot be nested: the sequence `]]` followed by `>` terminates the current
section. This occurs when Markdown documentation contains XML or BML examples that themselves
contain CDATA. A serializer must therefore split the CDATA section around such a sequence so
that the original text is preserved losslessly.

This is purely a serialization concern. Ordinary XML text, a single CDATA section, and split
CDATA sections all represent the same documentation content after parsing.

**Principle:** `Markdown(English)` is the default semantics of `documentation`; CDATA is only an
XML representation detail, used when necessary to keep BML readable.

### Human-friendly formatting

Block documentation is Markdown and should be written as such — in particular the main
documentation of a Block, and in particular for longer texts. Use paragraphs, headings, lists,
and inline code to make the structure visible. Long block documentation without paragraph breaks
is to be avoided; readable formatting for humans and LLMs is a central part of BlockML, not
decoration. `summary` stays a single plain-text paragraph — when documentation grows long enough
to need structure, that is exactly when summary becomes required.

Authoring split:
• documentation carries technical prose only
• references carries all documentation cross-links — types to types, types to packages, or types to instances
  (also Definition members, repository markdown files, and external URLs) — each with an
  explicit relationship note
• Associations connect instances to instances (model links); References do not form the
  instance graph — use associations for that
• Do not repeat cross-links in documentation prose

see target attributes — exactly one target kind:
type="core:ValueType" — Block or Definition type via xmlns prefix (TypeReference)
package="org.blockml.bml.type" — package string without a type segment (PackageReference)
instance="myId" / instance="foo:Bar::myId" — Block instance pointer (InstanceReference)
file="guide.md" — optional companion markdown in the consuming repository (not Core SSOT)
url="https://…" — external URL
property="com.foo.Bar.properties.width" — PropertyDefinition canonical path
aggregation="com.foo.Bar.aggregations.parts" — AggregationDefinition canonical path
association="com.foo.Bar.associations.parent" — AssociationDefinition canonical path
capability="com.foo.Bar.capabilities.render" — CapabilityDefinition canonical path
Split forms (still one target): type="com.foo.Bar" property="width" →
com.foo.Bar.properties.width in BOM; type="com.foo.Bar" instance="myId" → com.foo.Bar::myId.
(Retired attribute name: block= — use type=.)

relation attribute (optional) — Block reference to org.blockml.bml.relation.*; unqualified
names resolve via implicit namespace org.blockml.bml.relation.*. Omitted =
org.blockml.bml.relation.SeeAlso. Standard blocks: SeeAlso, ReadFirst, ReadNext,
ThenContinueWith, Extends, Requires, ContrastsWith, AuthoringGuide, Defines, DeepDive,
HowToIndex, HowToStep, Prerequisite, Resolves. README curates with ReadFirst; documentation
blocks chain with ReadNext.

README / ReadMe blocks (baseType org.blockml.bml.core.ReadMe) are library reading entry points
for humans and LLMs (Library.readMe). Curated reading order is expressed via references with
relation=ReadFirst; available how-tos via relation=HowToIndex — not via separate aggregations on
ReadMe. Documentation blocks (org.blockml.bml.documentation.*) inherit from
org.blockml.bml.core.Documentation. HowTo blocks (org.blockml.bml.documentation.howto.*) inherit from
org.blockml.bml.documentation.howto.HowTo. Diagnostic blocks (org.blockml.bml.diagnostic.*) inherit from
org.blockml.bml.core.Diagnostic.

Every type name in BML — composition tags, identity type / baseType on definitions, member type
attributes — may be written in one of four forms. All normalize to a canonical FQN during
resolution:
1. Fully qualified name — com.foo.Bar
2. QName (xmlns prefix) — foo:Bar with xmlns:foo="com.foo"
3. Unqualified fallback — Integer at a context-bound site (doc:ImplicitNamespaceResolution)
4. Sub-Block-relative name — MySubBlock or foo:Bar.MySubBlock

Validator — declared ValueType wins, never the field name. type=, baseType=, abc=, or any
other name is irrelevant; only whether the field's type is-a TypeReference / TypeIdentifier /
PropertyReference / … matters:
• TypeReference / TypeReferenceEntity — FQN must resolve in TypeRegistry → else BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE
• TypeIdentifier (and not TypeReference) — syntax only; unknown FQN is valid
• PropertyReference / AggregationReference / … — path must resolve → else BML_UNKNOWN_PROPERTY
  (or BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE if the owning type cannot be resolved)
• MemberIdentifier / PropertyIdentifier / … — path syntax only
• InstanceReference — instance must resolve → else BML_UNRESOLVABLE_INSTANCE_REF
• InstanceIdentifier — id / path syntax only
Ill-formed syntax on any of these → BML_INVALID_TYPE_REFERENCE (and, when a host evaluates
parseValue, BML_INVALID_VALUE). Syntax is PrimitiveType.parseValue; existence stays a
validator step on Reference types (doc:ValueTypeParsing).

An unresolved Reference is an error, but it does not mean the document is ill-formed. Like
Java class-not-found, it may be a typo or a missing dependency (library not on the current
classpath). Interpretation is left open.

Unqualified names on TypeReference fields require an explicit FQN or xmlns prefix — no
implicit fallback. Unresolvable → BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE. Ambiguous unqualified → BML_AMBIGUOUS_TYPE.
Undeclared QName prefix → BML_UNKNOWN_NAMESPACE_PREFIX.

Sub-Block type references — Java static nested classes: own FQN prefix, optional own
genericTypes, no enclosing-instance and no outer type-parameter scope (forward explicitly, e.g.
Item(T)). Reference unqualified when in scope, as FQN, or as QName. The local part of a QName may
include a relative Sub-Block path (foo:Bar.MySubBlock).

Unqualified nested type resolution (innermost scope first, then enclosing chain):
On the current Block, in order: (1) own Block name, (2) own genericTypes, (3) own direct
Sub-Blocks. Then repeat for the immediate enclosing Block up to the document root. Grandchildren
are never unqualified — from Grid, Range does not resolve to Grid.Selector.Range; write
Selector.Range or Grid.Selector.Range. After the nested walk fails, context-bound implicit
namespace / FQN / xmlns rules apply. Generic / Sub-Block name collisions on the same declaring
Block remain errors (BML_GENERIC_*_COLLISION).

Root Block identity:
• type — required (BML_MISSING_BLOCK_TYPE); canonical identity. Preferred authoring: the
  document root tag is the type (<acme:MyBlock> / <MyBlock>). Legacy: child
  <type> under a <block> root. Both forms are valid during the transition
  (doc:DocumentFormat). When both the root tag and <type> supply a type, they must
  resolve to the same FQN
• name — optional; when omitted effectiveName = lastSegment(resolve(type)); when present must
  equal lastSegment(resolve(type)) → else BML_BLOCK_NAME_TYPE_MISMATCH. On the preferred
  unqualified root, a redundant <name> is not recommended
• definition — optional; default RootBlockDefinition; unqualified via org.blockml.bml.definition.*

Sub-Block identity (opposite convention — unqualified name-as-tag, doc:DocumentFormat):
• name — required (BML_MISSING_SUBBLOCK_NAME). Preferred authoring: the element local name
  is the Sub-Block name (<MyBlock> under <subBlocks>). Legacy: child <name>
  under a <block> wrapper. When both are present they must match
• type — normally omitted; expectedType = resolve(parent.type) + "." + name; when present must
  equal expectedType (full parent path check, not last segment alone) →
  BML_SUBBLOCK_TYPE_MISMATCH
• definition — default SubBlockDefinition
• genericTypes / subBlocks — allowed; embeddedBlocks — forbidden
  (BML_EMBEDDED_BLOCKS_ON_SUBBLOCK)

Embedded Block identity (same authoring as the document root, doc:DocumentFormat):
• type — required and fully qualified (BML_MISSING_EMBEDDED_BLOCK_TYPE /
  BML_UNQUALIFIED_EMBEDDED_BLOCK_TYPE); preferred: the element tag is the type
  (<acme:MyBlock>). Legacy: child <type> under a <block> wrapper. FQN =
  resolve(type), not nested under the root
• name — optional; same matching rule as the document root
• definition — default EmbeddedBlockDefinition

Canonical derivation summary:
• Root / embed: canonicalType = resolve(type); effectiveName = name ?? lastSegment(canonicalType);
  if name present → name == lastSegment(canonicalType)
• Sub-Block: effectiveName = name (element tag or child <name>);
  expectedType = canonicalParentType + "." + name;
  canonicalType = type ? resolve(type) : expectedType; canonicalType == expectedType

See also doc:SubBlockModel (visibility, embeds, reference scope) and doc:BlockNameConvention.

Everything beyond the four ValueType kinds is a type expression — a use or combination of named
types, not a new BlockML type class.

ValueType = named semantic meaning (Primitive · Enum · Struct · Constant)
TypeExpression = usage or combination (multiplicity · union · generic application · instance
configuration · anonymous StructType · bml:Self · T)

Examples: Integer[] · Integer[3] · Integer[0..n] · Boolean | Integer · Box(Integer) ·
InstanceReference(core:Block) · SelectiveGrid(Boolean | HoleType) · Text{maxLength: 100} ·
{ x: Integer, y: Integer } · bml:Self · T

In type="…" XML attributes, generic applications use round parentheses (not angle brackets) so
values stay valid XML. Generic type arguments may be full type expressions — unions,
multiplicity, nested generics, and {…} configuration. Parentheses bind the argument:
SelectiveGrid(Boolean | HoleType) means T = Boolean | HoleType, not SelectiveGrid(Boolean) | HoleType.
When a parameter constrains baseType to ValueType (or another branch), every union alternative
must satisfy satisfiesTypeBound → else BML_GENERIC_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION. The same parenthesized
argument list is authored on Block instances as bml:generics (type name omitted; parentheses
required) — see doc:GenericsModel.

Obsolete wrappers → write unions directly:
• AutoOr<T> → Constant(Text){value: "auto"} | T
• FalseOr<T> → Boolean.False | T
• NoneOr<T> → Constant(Text){value: "none"} | T
• BooleanOr<T> → Boolean | T
• Array<T> → T[]
Boolean.True / Boolean.False are Sub-Block shortcuts for Constant(Boolean){value: true/false}.

Multiplicity — no separate Array type. Bracket notation is a postfix operation on a
TypeExpression, not an intrinsic property of a named ValueType; it is metadata on the type
reference and the FQN is unchanged. Prefer Collection / Multiplicity terminology (not Array).
Semantics only — ordered vs unordered and concrete storage are renderer-defined.
• Integer → exactly one
• Integer[] ≡ Integer[0..n]
• Integer[3] · Integer[1..5] · Integer[1..]
Applies commonly on aggregation/association types and capability input fields; bare properties
are usually exactly one value.

Nested multiplicities — multiplicity may be applied to any TypeExpression, including one that
already carries a multiplicity. Parentheses group the inner TypeExpression before the outer
multiplicity is applied, so nested collections need no separate Array or collection type:
• Integer[] → collection of Integer
• (Integer[])[] → collection of collections of Integer
• (Integer[3])[] → collection of fixed-size Integer collections
• (Integer[])[2] → fixed-size collection containing two Integer collections
Integer[][] is intentionally not supported — nested multiplicities must use explicit grouping
((Integer[])[]), which keeps the binding of each multiplicity unambiguous. Ungrouped stacked
brackets are ill-formed → BML_INVALID_TYPE_REFERENCE.

Nested collections nest their rules too: compatibility, element-wise validation, and
multiplicity bounds are applied recursively, outer collection first. (core:ValueType[])[]
accepts [[1, 2], [3, 4], ["a"]] — three elements against the outer multiplicity, each element
validated against core:ValueType[]; (Integer[])[2] rejects [[1], [2], [3]] with
BML_CARDINALITY_VIOLATION on the outer collection. For Capability inputs the ordinary collection
FunctionMapping rule applies to the outermost collection, so service:Lists concat with
inputType="(core:ValueType[])[]" maps #lists.concat([1, 2], [3, 4], ["a"]) to
[[1, 2], [3, 4], ["a"]] — one function argument per outer element, inner collections remaining
ordinary typed values (doc:FunctionMappingModel).

Collection compatibility — for a type reference with multiplicity, compatibility is evaluated
against the referenced element type. If S is assignable to T (S <: T), then a collection of S
values is assignable to a collection of T values, provided the source multiplicity is compatible
with the target multiplicity — collections are covariant in their element type:

  S <: T
  ---------------
  S[] <: T[]

With Integer <: Number <: PrimitiveType <: ValueType:
• Integer[] <: Number[] · Integer[] <: PrimitiveType[] · Integer[] <: ValueType[]
• Text[] <: ValueType[] · SomeStruct[] <: ValueType[]
• Integer[3] <: Number[] — but Integer[] is not assignable to Number[1..2] (bounds do not fit)
• Date[] <: Temporal[] · DateTime[] <: Temporal[] — Duration[] is not assignable to Temporal[]

A value assigned to a collection type is validated element by element against the referenced
element type. core:ValueType[] accepts zero or more values where every element's concrete
ValueType is assignable to ValueType — therefore:
• [1, 2, 3] → valid as Integer[], as Number[], and as ValueType[]
• ["a", "b"] → valid as Text[] and as ValueType[]

Heterogeneous collections — a collection type does not require all elements to have the same
concrete subtype. Each element is validated independently against the declared element type:
• ValueType[] : [1, "text", true] is valid, because Integer <: ValueType, Text <: ValueType,
  and Boolean <: ValueType
• Integer[] : [1, 2, 3] is valid — [1, "text", 3] is invalid, because Text is not assignable to
  Integer
An element whose type is not assignable to the declared element type is rejected
(BML_INVALID_PROPERTY on authored member values, BML_EXPR_TYPE_MISMATCH on expression payloads);
an element count outside the multiplicity bounds → BML_CARDINALITY_VIOLATION.

Unions — alternatives with |. Match order is left to right, first hit wins (no best-match).
Prefer narrower / sentinel alternatives on the left (Boolean | Text, not Text | Boolean).
Later alternatives that can never win → BML_UNREACHABLE_UNION_ALTERNATIVE (warning). Singleton
alternatives use Constant(T){value: …} (doc:ConstantValueType). Future literal shorthand
Boolean | "auto" desugars to Constant form.

Anonymous StructTypes — { field: Type, … } is the type-expression form of a StructType without a
declared name, and the mechanism for structured Capability inputs. An empty anonymous StructType
{} is type-equivalent to the named instantiable type:EmptyStruct. The grammar is recursive:

  AnonymousStruct := "{" StructField ("," StructField)* "}"
  StructField     := Identifier ":" TypeExpression

Because the right side of a field is a full TypeExpression — not merely an unqualified type name
— qualified type references, multiplicity, generic applications, unions, instance configuration,
and nested anonymous StructTypes are all valid field types:
• { list: core:ValueType[], index: Integer } — qualified reference with multiplicity
• { values: foo:Thing[1..n] } · { value: Integer | Text } · { nested: { x: Integer, y: Integer } }
• { lists: (core:ValueType[])[] } — nested multiplicity as a field type

The colon separating a field name from its type and the colon inside a qualified type reference
belong to different grammar levels and are unambiguous:

  list : core:ValueType[]
       ^     ^
       |     +-- prefix colon of a qualified TypeReference (xmlns prefix + local name)
       +-- field name / type separator

So { list: core:ValueType[], index: Integer } is one anonymous StructType with field list of type
core:ValueType[] and field index of type Integer. Field declaration order is significant — same
contract as named StructTypes (doc:FunctionMappingModel).

Braces are disambiguated by position: a { opening a type expression starts an anonymous
StructType whose field values are TypeExpressions; a { directly following a type reference is
ValueType instance configuration whose field values are literals — Text{maxLength: 100}
(doc:ValueTypeConfiguration). Each field type resolves like any other type reference at that
site: unqualified names via the site's implicit namespace (Integer → org.blockml.bml.type.Integer
on inputType / outputType), prefixed names via xmlns, full FQNs always
(doc:ImplicitNamespaceResolution).

Conformance note — an implementation that accepts { list: Integer[], index: Integer } but rejects
{ list: core:ValueType[], index: Integer } is missing support for qualified type references
inside anonymous StructType fields. That is a parser / mapper limitation, not a semantic
ambiguity in the type expression.

Bare type name sites (Property type, Capability inputType/outputType) require ValueTypes (plus
type expressions over them). Aggregation type may be any Block FQN (plain composition or
TypeReferenceEntity application). Association type must be InstanceReference(T) or
InstanceReference(T)[] with T extending core:Block — bare Block FQNs are invalid.
Non-ValueType on a property → BML_INVALID_PROPERTY_TYPE.

Compiler-internal descriptors (UnionTypeDescriptor, …) are not BML Block classes.

Existence-checked AggregationIdentifier. Value is a canonical aggregation path
(com.foo.Bar.aggregations.children) or a local aggregation name when paired with a type
qualifier. The owning type and aggregation must resolve. Used as the type of see aggregation=.
A potential aggregation that need not exist uses AggregationIdentifier.

Existence-checked AssociationIdentifier. Value is a canonical association path
(com.foo.Bar.associations.basePresets) or a local association name when paired with a type
qualifier. The owning type and association must resolve. Used as the type of see association=.
A potential association that need not exist uses AssociationIdentifier.

Existence-checked CapabilityIdentifier. Value is a canonical capability path
(com.foo.Bar.capabilities.render) or a local capability name when paired with a type qualifier.
The owning type and capability must resolve. Used as the type of see capability=. A potential
capability that need not exist uses CapabilityIdentifier.

Existence-checked PropertyIdentifier. Introduces the owning Block bound B.
Value is a canonical property path (com.foo.Bar.properties.width) or a local property name
when paired with a Block qualifier. The owning type and property must resolve. Used as the
type of see property= and other PropertyDefinition reference sites. A potential property
that need not exist uses PropertyIdentifier.

Filled Extension descriptor for publisher blockml / name bml. Contribution children declare
milestone V1 or V2. Settings under configuration are the SSOT for package.json
contributes.configuration.

Read documentation blocks (V1Scope, V2Scope, GenerationWorkflow) before generating sources.
Concrete extension catalogue for BlockML (.bml) authoring — V1 file type, icon, and
simple highlighting; V2 language server, advanced highlighting, and Java-like navigation.

final="true" on a block definition prevents other definitions from extending it. Choose a non-final base or unseal the parent if you control it.
Emitted when a Block uses a final type as baseType.

final="true" seals a declaration. Private members are also non-overridable. Remove the override or change the parent declaration.
Emitted when a child attempts to override a final member, or to override a private member.

FunctionMapping translates between function-parameter lists and Capability inputType /
outputType. Concrete Mapping: org.blockml.bml.mapping.FunctionMapping.

Two application sites (opposite directions):
1. Expression calls — function syntax → FunctionMapping → Capability inputType
2. Capability implementation — inputType → FunctionMapping → target-language parameters
   (and reverse for returns)

Capabilities have no separate parameter list — only inputType / outputType. FunctionMapping
matters when a Capability is invoked as a function (built-ins, utility Sub-Blocks, expression
calls). Messaging transport ignores struct shape. Declared exception types live on
CapabilityDefinition.throws (type:TypeReferenceEntity(core:Exception)[]) and are not part of
FunctionMapping.

Host-language return types in an implementation body (TypeScript number, string, boolean) are
FunctionMapping / host encodings of the BML outputType — not a second type system.
PrimitiveType.parseValue has outputType bml:Self; a TypeScript number for Integer is mapping,
not the Capability signature (doc:ValueTypeParsing).

inputType shapes:
• Primitive → single positional or named argument
• Named StructType / anonymous struct { a: Float, b: Float } → arity = field count; names =
  declaration order
• Collection field { values: T[0..n] } → exactly one positional sequence argument — not
  fixed-arity multi-arg expansion
Anonymous struct field types are full TypeExpressions — qualified references, multiplicity,
unions, and nested anonymous structs included ({ list: core:ValueType[], index: Integer }). Arity
and named keys come from the field list; the field types themselves do not change the mapping
(doc:TypeExpressions — Anonymous StructTypes).

Nested collection inputType — for a grouped, nested multiplicity such as (core:ValueType[])[]
(doc:TypeExpressions — Nested multiplicities) the collection rule above applies to the outermost
collection. A positional/variadic function representation may therefore map each function
argument to one element of the outer collection:

  inputType="(core:ValueType[])[]"
  #lists.concat([1, 2], [3, 4], ["a"])  →  [[1, 2], [3, 4], ["a"]]

The inner collections stay ordinary typed values and are validated recursively against
core:ValueType[] — nesting changes the shape of the logical input value, not the mapping rules.

Canonical call forms normalize to the same logical input value (positional, named name=expr,
or object literal). Default FunctionMapping (when no explicit mapping is declared):
• Positional-only — arg i → field i in declaration order
• Named-only / object literal — keys = field names
• Mixed positional + named → BML_MIXED_FUNCTION_ARGUMENTS
• Too few / too many / unknown / duplicate → BML_MISSING_FUNCTION_PARAMETER,
  BML_TOO_MANY_FUNCTION_PARAMETERS, BML_UNKNOWN_FUNCTION_PARAMETER,
  BML_DUPLICATE_FUNCTION_PARAMETER

Declaration order — same contract as StructType positional literals and ValueType instance
configuration {…} positional args (doc:ValueTypeConfiguration). Member access in expressions
remains by name (point.x) — not numeric index on StructTypes.

Custom FunctionMapping on an implementation may reorder/rename parameters or reject forms.
Required custom mapping absent → BML_MISSING_FUNCTION_MAPPING (reserved until custom mappings
ship). Ambiguous custom mapping → BML_AMBIGUOUS_FUNCTION_MAPPING.

Default mapping properties on mapping:FunctionMapping: supportsPositional=true,
supportsNamed=true, supportsMixed=false.

Generic parameters belong exclusively to the Block that declares them — never inherited
implicitly. When a generic Block is used as baseType, the derived Block must account for every
base parameter by either binding it to a concrete TypeExpression in baseType or forwarding it
to a parameter declared on the derived Block. All bound → concrete; any forwarded → remains
generic. Resolution runs during inheritance: bound parameters are substituted throughout the
inherited definition. Validator checks: every base parameter accounted for, argument count
matches, each bound argument satisfies the parameter baseType (satisfiesTypeBound), forwarded
parameters are declared locally.

Type-level binding uses baseType application: a derived Block must bind or forward every base
parameter (PrimitiveEntity(T) → IntegerEntity with baseType PrimitiveEntity(Integer), etc.).
Instance-level binding uses bml:generics. A type whose genericTypes remain open after inheritance
cannot appear as an aggregation child unless bml:generics binds those parameters. Abstract
Blocks remain uninstantiable even with bml:generics.

Declaration — on the Block via <genericTypes> (meta-model GenericTypeDefinition). Parameter
name = XML element local name (<T baseType="…"/>). Optional defaultType when an application
omits the argument:
1. Concrete TypeExpression (e.g. type:Decimal)
2. Earlier sibling parameter name only (declaration-order DAG; no forward refs/cycles)
Resolution: authored args win → unbound params get defaults in declaration order → every
parameter must ground to a concrete TypeExpression → each binding satisfies baseType.
Diagnostics: BML_GENERIC_DEFAULT_FORWARD_REF, BML_GENERIC_DEFAULT_CYCLE,
BML_GENERIC_DEFAULT_UNRESOLVED, BML_GENERIC_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION.

BML attribute syntax — round parentheses: Box(Integer), TypeReference(core:Block),
InstanceReference(core:Block), SelectiveGrid(Boolean | type:HoleType). Each (…) argument is a
TypeExpression. With multiple parameters, labels match generic parameter names. At validate
time placeholders (T) are substituted; mismatch → BML_GENERIC_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION.

Instance syntax — bml:generics on the Block instance (attribute or child element). The value is
only the parenthesized argument list; the type name is the instance tag. Parentheses are
required. Same TypeExpression grammar as baseType arguments. Authored args win; remaining
parameters take defaultType in declaration order. After resolution every parameter must be
concrete. Incorrect: <MyBlock someProp="Value"/> when MyBlock still has open T. Correct:
<MyBlock bml:generics="(type:Integer)"/> or
<TestBlock><bml:generics>(type:String, myns:MyBlock)</bml:generics></TestBlock>.
Open generic aggregated without the directive → BML_OPEN_GENERIC_INSTANCE. bml:generics
anywhere other than a Block instance → BML_GENERICS_DIRECTIVE_NOT_ALLOWED. Argument list
incompatible with the instance's open genericTypes → BML_GENERICS_ARGUMENT_MISMATCH. Missing
required argument with no defaultType → BML_MISSING_GENERIC_TYPE_ARGUMENT. Ill-formed
TypeExpression → BML_INVALID_TYPE_REFERENCE.

Orthogonal to {…} ValueType instance configuration (doc:ValueTypeConfiguration) and to
multiplicity brackets (doc:TypeExpressions).

Sub-Blocks / embeds may declare own genericTypes (Java static nested class model) — they do not
see enclosing generics; forward explicitly (Item(T)). Name collisions on the same declaring
Block with Block name or direct Sub-Block → BML_GENERIC_BLOCK_NAME_COLLISION /
BML_GENERIC_SUBBLOCK_NAME_COLLISION.

Constraint generics — Constraint branches declare genericTypes but arguments are never authored;
the compiler binds T from the <constraints> embedding context (Property → ValueType,
Aggregation → AggregationDefinition, Block → BlockDefinition, …). Branch ↔ context mismatch →
BML_CONSTRAINT_TARGET_MISMATCH. Validation property (Error/Warning/Information) controls
enforcement; omitted → metadata only.

HowToIndex (relation)    — catalog of accomplishable how-tos on ReadMe

HowToStep (relation)     — ordered steps inside a HowTo (document order = step order)
Prerequisite (relation)  — understand before starting a HowTo
Diagnostic (branch)      — org.blockml.bml.diagnostic.* validator code documentation
Resolves (relation)      — Diagnostic → HowTo fix procedure

HowTo extends Documentation and lives in the documentation.howto subpackage — not
in core. Core holds root branches only. HowTo is not an executable workflow Task.

One mechanism: all navigation uses <references> and <see> with typed relation
attributes — no separate how-to aggregation on ReadMe. Automated process SPOE uses
Library.bootstrap (core:Bootstrap), separate from reading/how-to catalog on ReadMe.

Tooling (future):
• filter relation=ReadFirst → learn context bundle
• filter relation=HowToIndex → how-to menu
• load Diagnostic by code → follow Resolves → HowToStep chain

org.blockml.bml.README lists HowToIndex entries after ReadFirst entries. Future Bootstrap
subtypes (AgentBootstrap, CIBootstrap) supply automation SPOE members — not reading paths.

Implement with override="true" and a locally complete declaration (abstract defaults to false). To keep abstract, redeclare with abstract="true".
Emitted when a concrete Block still has an abstract member obligation from the inheritance/contract merge.

Implemented, validated, and mapping complete. Behavior is reliable and may be
depended on by downstream definitions and tooling. Implicit default when no status is declared
on an element — omit <status> and bml:status on Stable content.

In this context ${ … } forms are fixed tag recipes, not open Expression Language. Other roots, calls, or operators are invalid.
Emitted when a <bml:xml> body is not a literal local name, ${ bml:Self }, or ${ #this.name }.

Inheritance (baseType):
• Single inheritance — each Block has exactly one baseType (mandatory except org.blockml.bml.core.Block)
• Use for branch membership (ValueType, Language, domain base) and shared member fragments
• Framework branches inherit via org.blockml.bml.core.ValueType, Language, or domain bases
• Package org.blockml.bml.core — every root Block in this package must inherit directly from
  core:Block (Block itself omits baseType). Specializations of those branches live in sibling
  packages (type, relation, meta, documentation, …). Nested Sub-Blocks in core are exempt —
  they may extend any ancestor (for example Annotation.Directive and its descendants).
• final on Block or member prevents further override → BML_FINAL_BASE_TYPE / BML_FINAL_MEMBER_OVERRIDE

Contracts:
• Reusable partial Block definitions — not pure interfaces; may include default implementations
• Use when multiple Blocks share a member fragment without sharing a common baseType ancestor
• Declared on root block only via contracts aggregation — direct Block references
• Merge order: baseType chain → contracts (declaration order) → local declarations
• Contract may supply partial members (e.g. id type only); concrete Block completes defaults,
  constraints, and documentation
• subBlocks and compositions on contract types are ignored

Capabilities:
• All behaviour — init, get/set, render, parse, domain operations — express as Capabilities
• An implementation may be intent (PseudoCode / natural language), a companion template,
  or a host-evaluable function — no ranking (doc:CapabilitySemantics)
• Prefer PseudoCode or natural language when the body is intent for humans and LLMs
• Use Inbound/Outbound/Transformation/Action kinds to describe payload shape
• Public surface of a Block is Capabilities — Properties are internal configuration
• Declare throws for Exception types the Capability may raise
  (type:TypeReferenceEntity(core:Exception)[] — Java-style method throws; omit when none)

Constraints:
• Declare on Properties via constraints aggregation — Constraint Block instances
• Generic binding is automatic: Min/Max bind T from property type; MinItems/MaxItems from
  collection element type; MinLength/MaxLength from Text element type
• Use for validation rules expressible as reusable Constraint blocks (Min, Max, Pattern, …)
• Suggestions (optional Block instances of property type) guide editors — not validation

General: keep <is> stable; put cross-links in references; prefer explicit baseType over
implicit defaults; document partial members in contracts clearly.

Documentation formatting: block documentation is Markdown(English) by default — structure longer
prose with paragraphs, headings, lists, and inline code instead of one unbroken text; keep
summary plain text. Human-friendly formatting is a central part of BlockML
(doc:DocumentationModel).

Instantiable PrimitiveEntity(Text) for alternative Block type names in an aliases
aggregation on org.blockml.bml.definition.BlockDefinition only (root blocks and Sub-Blocks).
Not a core root branch. Ad-hoc names are Alias instances (for example
<meta:Alias value="Sub-Block" />). Comma-separated character content on <aliases> is
PrimitiveEntity value sugar and expands to Alias instances — one value per trimmed token —
not to FixedAlias catalogue blocks. Not XML namespace prefix aliases. Not search tags —

Those types set value on the definition; references are empty fixed blocks (for example
<vocab:SubBlockAlias />). Type FQN is the catalogue identity; value, language, and
legacy resolve from the alias definition.

Instantiable PrimitiveEntity(Text) for search and discovery tags in a keywords aggregation
on org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition. Not a core root branch. Ad-hoc tags are
Keyword instances (for example <meta:Keyword value="inheritance" />). Comma-separated
character content on <keywords> is PrimitiveEntity value sugar and expands to Keyword
instances — one value per trimmed token — not to FixedKeyword catalogue blocks.

Domain libraries define catalogue keyword blocks extending org.blockml.bml.meta.FixedKeyword
(for example org.example.keyword.Inheritance). Those types set value on the definition;
references are empty fixed blocks (for example <vocab:Inheritance />). Type FQN is the

Distinct from org.blockml.bml.meta.Alias (alternative Block type names on BlockDefinition).

Instantiable StructType with no fields. Unqualified name EmptyStruct resolves to
org.blockml.bml.type.EmptyStruct.

The only compatible value is an empty object {}. EmptyStruct is a named, reusable unit

Kinds of click-to-navigate targets between BML files — analogous to Java class,
field, and method navigation. Used by NavigationContribution and LSP go-to-definition
providers.

Legacy/alias style expression type error — prefer BML_EXPR_TYPE_MISMATCH where applicable.
Align expression result type with the target member type.
Legacy/alias style expression type error — prefer BML_EXPR_TYPE_MISMATCH where applicable.

LLMs repeatedly confuse member-declaration syntax with the syntax used when assigning members
on Block instances. The two most common mistakes are wrapping an instance Property in
<value> and wrapping instance Aggregation children in <composition>.

Incorrect on a Block instance:
<myns:MyBlock><myProperty><value>Hello!</value></myProperty></myns:MyBlock>
<myns:MyBlock><content><composition>…</composition></content></myns:MyBlock>

Two contexts, never mixed:

1. Definition context — a Property or Aggregation is being declared inside <properties>
   or <aggregations> (or an inherited member is filled on a Block definition).
2. Instance context — a concrete Block instance receives Property values or Aggregation
   children.

<value> is the value field of def:PropertyDefinition. <composition> is the
composition field of def:AggregationDefinition. Both are definition-context fields. They are
not general-purpose wrappers around instance payloads.

Critical authoring rule — inside a Block instance:
• NEVER introduce <value> as a wrapper around a Property assignment
• NEVER introduce <composition> as a wrapper around Aggregation children
Instead: the Property element (or Block attribute) contains the value; the Aggregation element
contains the child Blocks. Group instance children with bml:container, not composition.

PROPERTIES — definition. Inside <properties> the child element is a PropertyDefinition.
Its default value is the value field of that declaration. Element form is preferred when
serializing definitions:
<properties><description><value>BlockML core library</value></description></properties>
Compact attribute form on the declaration is also valid:
<properties><description value="BlockML core library"/></properties>
Do not specify both forms on the same declaration (conflicting payloads). Other declaration
fields (type, readOnly, override, constraints, suggestions) stay on this PropertyDefinition
element — they are not authored on domain instances.

PROPERTIES — Block instance. The instance is not a PropertyDefinition. It only supplies the
payload. Attribute form is preferred:
<myns:MyBlock myProperty="Hello!"/>
Element form is the Property element with direct character content — the element itself is
already the value container:
<myns:MyBlock><myProperty>Hello!</myProperty></myns:MyBlock>
Incorrect — definition value field used as an instance wrapper:
<myns:MyBlock><myProperty><value>Hello!</value></myProperty></myns:MyBlock>
Also incorrect as a wrapper (same category error):
<myns:MyBlock><myProperty value="Hello!"/></myns:MyBlock>
unless myProperty is actually named value (see exception below).

Exception — member whose name is value. PrimitiveEntity, TypeReferenceEntity, FilePathEntity
and similar types declare a Property named value. Then value="…" or <value>…</value>
on the Block instance is ordinary instance syntax for that member, not a PropertyDefinition
wrapper:
<type:FilePathEntity value="blockml-library.xsd"/>
Annotation value facets (e.g. <scad:value> under a property declaration) are a separate
namespace axis on PropertyDefinition.value — not instance wrappers. See doc:AnnotationModel.

AGGREGATIONS — definition. Inside <aggregations> the child element is an
AggregationDefinition. Its initial/default child structure is the composition field:
<aggregations><content><composition><myns:Child/></composition></content></aggregations>
<composition> is allowed only as that definition field, nested inside the aggregation
member — never standalone (BML_STANDALONE_COMPOSITION).

AGGREGATIONS — Block instance. Child Block instances are placed directly inside the
named Aggregation element. There is no composition wrapper and no default aggregation —
the aggregation must always be opened by member name:
<myns:MyBlock><content><myns:Child/></content></myns:MyBlock>
Incorrect — composition wrapper on an instance:
<myns:MyBlock><content><composition><myns:Child/></composition></content></myns:MyBlock>
Incorrect — implicit fill (bare child under the instance, aggregation not opened):
<myns:MyBlock><myns:Child/></myns:MyBlock>
The same rule applies recursively — a Block instance nested inside a definition composition
still fills its own aggregations without a composition wrapper:
<aggregations><myAggr><composition>
  <myns:MyBlock><content><myns:Child/></content></myns:MyBlock>
</composition></myAggr></aggregations>
Outer <composition> is valid (myAggr is an Aggregation definition). Inner
<composition> under content is invalid (content is populated on a Block instance).

On instances, the virtual grouping element is bml:container — not composition. Both
composition (definitions) and bml:container (instances) host bml:if, bml:each, and bml:with.

Unified pattern:
Definition Property → value attribute or <value> wrapper on the PropertyDefinition
Definition Aggregation → <composition> wrapper on the AggregationDefinition
Instance Property → attribute on the Block, or direct Property element content
Instance Aggregation → named aggregation element containing child Block instances
(bml:container for grouping). Always open the aggregation; there is no default aggregation.
A PrimitiveEntity aggregation may also take comma-separated character content that expands to
instances with value set per token (core:PrimitiveEntity) — not a PropertyDefinition wrapper.

Capabilities on instances follow the Property pattern: attribute or child element, no extra
wrapper. readOnly effective members must not be authored on instances
(BML_READONLY_MEMBER_WRITE). Declared exception types are the throws aggregation on the Capability
declaration — TypeReferenceEntity children (empty-QName sugar), not instance wrappers
(doc:CapabilitySemantics).
<value> and <composition> belong only to member declarations. On a Block instance
the Property element or attribute is already the value; the Aggregation element already holds
the child Blocks. Do not wrap instance payloads in those definition fields.

MarkupLanguage for BlockML (BML) document implementations on Capabilities — block
definitions, library catalogs, and other structured BML markup. Forwards MarkupLanguage.L
(NaturalLanguage, default English) for the content/text language inside the BML body — bare BML
is BML(English).

MarkupLanguage for JSON document implementations on Capabilities — configuration,
structured data, or templates. Forwards MarkupLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for
the content/text language inside the document — bare JSON is JSON(English).

MarkupLanguage for Markdown prose — documentation bodies and Markdown document
implementations on Capabilities — with lightweight structure (headings, lists, links, code
fences).

Generic parameter L (NaturalLanguage, default English) is forwarded from MarkupLanguage and names
the content language of the Markdown body: Markdown = Markdown(English), Markdown(German) for
German prose. Because L is forwarded rather than bound, Markdown(NaturalLanguage) is a usable
type bound — def:StructuralDefinition.Documentation.language binds
Markdown(NaturalLanguage) | NaturalLanguage, where the bare-language alternative is shorthand for
Markdown in that language.

Also the default content language of documentation prose: Markdown(English) is the default value
of language on def:StructuralDefinition.Documentation, so every <documentation> body is
Markdown unless it declares otherwise. summary is plain text and never Markdown. CDATA is an XML
serialization detail — Markdown itself never requires it. See doc:DocumentationModel —
Documentation, Summary, Markdown and CDATA.

MarkupLanguage for XML document implementations on Capabilities — templates,
configuration, or structured markup. Forwards MarkupLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English)
for the content/text language inside the markup — bare XML is XML(English).

MarkupLanguage for YAML document implementations on Capabilities — configuration,
structured data, or templates. Forwards MarkupLanguage.L (NaturalLanguage, default English) for
the content/text language inside the document — bare YML is YML(English).

Member and Sub-Block visibility controls BlockML access only — which definitions may reference,
read, or set a member or Sub-Block. It does not prescribe how a renderer manifests visibility.
Renderers always see the entire Canonical BOM (public, protected, and private). Visibility
restricts authoring access, not technical BOM access.

Naming convention (primary signal):
• myVar — public
• _myVar — protected
• __myVar — private

The prefix is BlockML visibility, not logical member identity. Collision checking uses the
normalizedLogicalName with visibility prefixes stripped (myVar / _myVar / __myVar → myVar).
Members that differ only by visibility prefix must not coexist in the same Block →
BML_DUPLICATE_MEMBER_VISIBILITY_VARIANT. A logical member exists exactly once with exactly one
visibility.

Override matching uses normalizedLogicalName. A child may redeclare with a different visibility
prefix only when the change widens access:
• protected → public — allowed
• private → any — forbidden (BML_FINAL_MEMBER_OVERRIDE)
• public → protected/private, or protected → private — forbidden (BML_VISIBILITY_NARROWING)
Effective visibility and authored name come from the child declaration. Member-level bml:xml may
change on the same override.

Formal access (D = declaring Block, C = Block whose definition contains the access, I = instance
type, O = immediate composition owner of that instance):
• public — always
• private — only when C = D (owning composite does not gain access to private members of
  contained Sub-Block instances)
• protected — when C = D, or C inherits from D, or C = O, or C inherits from I.
  Only the immediate composition owner grants protected configuration access on children — not
  the entire outer composition hierarchy.

Aggregation members: visibility also controls which bml:id values may be referenced
(basePresets, Step.part, {BlockFQN}::{id}, …):
• public — cross-document {EnclosingBlockFQN}::{id}; unqualified ids within permitted access
• protected — declaring Block and its child Blocks (derived / Sub-Blocks in the same tree)
• private — declaring Block definition only
No separate export flag on composition or bml:container — reachability follows the aggregation
member's visibility. Qualified cross-document references require a public target aggregation and
a literal static bml:id.

Optional visibility property on members (and optional root-level visibility on Sub-Blocks) must
match the naming convention → mismatch BML_VISIBILITY_MISMATCH. Root Blocks must not declare
root-level visibility.

Validator diagnostics (access checks do not alter the Canonical BOM):
BML_PRIVATE_MEMBER_ACCESS, BML_PROTECTED_MEMBER_ACCESS,
BML_DUPLICATE_MEMBER_VISIBILITY_VARIANT, BML_VISIBILITY_MISMATCH, BML_VISIBILITY_NARROWING,
BML_FINAL_MEMBER_OVERRIDE (private cannot be overridden).

Declared on org.blockml.bml.definition.MemberDefinition as visibility (and related override
rules). Sub-Block visibility uses the same naming convention — see also Sub-Block authoring
rules on org.blockml.bml.definition.SubBlockDefinition.

Member-shaped directive under an annotation namespace. name is fixed to "*"
— the concrete local name comes from the authoring QName (e.g. scad:value). Specialized by
Property, Aggregation, Association, and Capability. Not a Definition member type.

Meta-model type for document-root block documents. Extends
org.blockml.bml.definition.BlockDefinition, overrides definition (default RootBlockDefinition),
and adds the embeddedBlocks aggregation (Inline Library — virtual .bml files co-located in one
BomDocument). subBlocks is inherited from BlockDefinition.

The definition property defaults to org.blockml.bml.definition.RootBlockDefinition when
<definition> is omitted on the document root. Embedded entries use
org.blockml.bml.definition.EmbeddedBlockDefinition (see EmbeddedBlockDefinition) — they are not
RootBlockDefinition instances. Sub-Blocks use SubBlockDefinition — sibling specialization.

embeddedBlocks is allowed only on the document root. Each child is an EmbeddedBlockDefinition
(virtual file): own FQN from mandatory <type>, own members and subBlocks, no nested
embeddedBlocks. Nested embeds are forbidden (BML_NESTED_EMBEDDED_BLOCKS). Within this document,
embedded FQNs shadow library/file definitions; duplicate embed FQNs →
BML_DUPLICATE_EMBEDDED_BLOCK; externally embeds remain invisible.

Meta-model type for embedded Block documents — virtual .bml files inlined under
the document root's <embeddedBlocks> aggregation. Extends
org.blockml.bml.definition.BlockDefinition (subBlocks, identity, members) and overrides
definition to default EmbeddedBlockDefinition.

Embedded blocks are full Block documents. Authoring is the same as the document root
(doc:DocumentFormat): preferred type tag (<acme:MyBlock>), legacy <block> plus
<type>. The resolved type is the FQN (not nested under the root) and must be fully
qualified. They may declare subBlocks and generics like any Block. They must
not declare <embeddedBlocks> — nesting is forbidden (BML_NESTED_EMBEDDED_BLOCKS). Only the
document root (RootBlockDefinition) may own embeddedBlocks; compose fat artifacts by listing
virtual files flat at the root (bundlers flatten nested packages when merging).

Within the BomDocument, each embedded FQN shadows the corresponding library or file-based
BlockDefinition. Duplicate FQNs among embeds → BML_DUPLICATE_EMBEDDED_BLOCK. Externally,
embeds are invisible.

Meta-model type for nested Sub-Block documents within a BomDocument. Extends
org.blockml.bml.definition.BlockDefinition and overrides definition (default SubBlockDefinition).
Shared identity, members, and subBlocks are inherited from BlockDefinition — Sub-Block-specific
identity rules live here.

Block identity conventions for Sub-Blocks (see 02_mbml.md — Type References and Block Identity):
• Sub-Block: semantically nested type within the same BomDocument as the root block — does not
  open its own document or library scope. Analogous to a Java static nested class: may declare
  own <genericTypes>; does not see enclosing Block generics (forward with applications).
  Uses org.blockml.bml.definition.SubBlockDefinition
  as definition meta-model — default org.blockml.bml.definition.SubBlockDefinition when
  <definition> is omitted. name is the local identity (required) — preferred authoring:
  the element local name under <subBlocks> is the Sub-Block name (<MyBlock>);
  child <name> is then optional (doc:DocumentFormat). type is normally
  omitted and derived recursively from the immediate enclosing block as
  resolve(parent.type) + "." + name (BML_SUBBLOCK_TYPE_MISMATCH when an explicit type does not
  match). Sub-Blocks may declare further Sub-Blocks to any depth (for example
  com.foo.Vehicle.Engine.Cylinder). Unqualified nested names resolve enclosing-chain first
  (02_mbml.md — Unqualified nested type resolution). Sub-Blocks must not declare embeddedBlocks
  (BML_EMBEDDED_BLOCKS_ON_SUBBLOCK).

Root blocks use org.blockml.bml.definition.RootBlockDefinition; embedded virtual files use
org.blockml.bml.definition.EmbeddedBlockDefinition — sibling specializations of
BlockDefinition.

Name is required as local identity. Preferred authoring: the element local name under
<subBlocks> is the Sub-Block name. Legacy: child <name> under a <block>
wrapper (doc:DocumentFormat). Type is normally derived.
Emitted when a Sub-Block supplies neither a name element tag nor a name child.

Authored empty child whose element QName is not TypeReferenceEntity is syntactic sugar for a

<foo:Bar /> expands to <type:TypeReferenceEntity value="foo:Bar" /> (B bound by the
aggregation type). Optional bml:version on the sugar child is an exact-version assert against
the referenced type (value), not against TypeReferenceEntity itself — e.g.
<blockml:Library bml:version="3.0.0" />. Explicit TypeReferenceEntity authoring is always
valid and equivalent.

Contrast with scalar TypeReference(B) on properties — those remain plain text, not
